features.prose:
The Scale Editor sets the harmony of the whole song and holds 16 scale slots. Changing the scale changes the pitches that pattern degrees produce; it does not change rhythm or pattern degrees.

Apply a scale:

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor. The scale slots are the 16 buttons on Grid row 3. The applied slot is brightly lit.
2. Short-press a slot. It is applied to every channel and selected for editing.
3. To turn global scale off, short-press the applied slot again. The slot stays selected for editing. With global scale off and no scale lock, pattern degrees play as chromatic semitone offsets. Press the slot again to apply it.

A pattern uses the applied scale unless a global scale lock or a channel scale lock overrides it.

Edit a slot:

1. Turn E2 to select Root, Scale, Degree, Transpose or Rotation. Scale tasks are Scale, Scale clock and Overview.
2. Turn E3 to change the value of the selected row. The title row names the slot you are editing.
3. Release all grid keys, then press K3 to apply the changes or K2 to cancel. Tapping any grid key, including Play/Stop, cancels an unapplied edit, so press K3 first.

Edit a slot without playing it:

1. Hold K1 and press the slot, or long-press a slot that is not selected for editing.
2. Edit the slot as above and press K3. Playback does not change. A dim indicator marks the editing slot when it differs from the applied slot.
3. Long-press the slot already selected for editing to turn global scale off and clear the editing selection.

Applying changes to the slot that is playing changes the sound immediately.

Set a scale lock: hold a step and press a scale slot. On the Scale page the lock is global for channels without a channel scale lock; on a channel page it applies to that channel. See [Scale Locks](#scale-locks).

The global scale track has its own rate and length, so a chord progression can run over a different number of steps from the patterns. On the Scale clock task, E2 selects Rate and E3 changes it; K3 applies. The same screen shows the selected range, the global cap and the playable range as read-only values. To change the length, hold the first step of the range on the scale track and press its last step. The end must come after the start: a reversed selection is rejected with the tooltip End must follow start and the previous range stays, and ranges do not wrap from the last step back to the first.

Video: [Scale editor demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2741)

recipes.text:
Start with a channel that plays a four-step melody on pattern degrees 1 to 4 (see [Build a phrase](#build-a-phrase)) and scale slot 1 applied as C major. The melody sounds MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 (C, D, E, F). The captured examples below start from the same setup: Save D major, then apply it follows steps 1 to 5, and Prepare a scale before applying it adds browsing a slot with a long press, editing the applied slot and turning the global scale Off.

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor. Slot 1, the left button on row 3, is bright.

2. Hold K1, press slot 2 at (2, 3), then release both. The title row names slot 2 and a dim indicator marks it. Playback is still in C major.

3. Turn E2 to Root and turn E3 two clicks to D. Release all grid keys and press K3. The draft is saved to slot 2. Tap Play (1,8), listen, then tap Stop: the melody still plays C, D, E, F because slot 1 is still applied.

4. Short-press slot 2 at (2, 3). It becomes the bright applied slot. Tap Play (1,8), listen, then tap Stop: the melody plays D, E, F sharp, G (MIDI 62, 64, 66, 67). The rhythm has not changed.

5. Short-press slot 1 at (1, 3), tap Play and listen: C, D, E, F are restored.

Use the transposition fader on the Scale page to transpose every channel of the selected Song Sequence without editing any note. Rhythm and intervals stay the same.

Set global transposition:

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.
2. Press a button on the transposition fader, Grid row 8, columns 8–16. The tooltip shows Transpose and the new value.

The fader buttons set these values: (9,8) is -12, (10,8) -8, (11,8) -4, (12,8) 0, (13,8) +4, (14,8) +8 and (15,8) +12. The end buttons, (8,8) and (16,8), lower or raise the value by one semitone each press.

The global value is added to the active scale slot's Transpose value. With scale slot 1 as C major and the melody 60, 62, 64, 65, +2 plays 62, 64, 66, 67.

You can change transposition while playing. A note that is already sounding keeps its pitch and length. The next notes use the new value.

To change transposition from a certain step onwards, use [transposition locks](#transposition-locks).

recipes.text:
This recipe changes the transposition fader on a copy of a slot, so the copy plays a tone higher while the original stays put. It is a different workflow from the captured example below, which shows the fader being pressed while a note is sounding.

Start with Song slot 1 holding a finished sequence, such as a four-note melody on MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, with playback stopped and Song mode at its default (On).

1. Press Grid (6, 8) to open the Song Editor. Slot 1 at (1, 1) is lit: it is the slot you are working on.

2. Hold slot 1 at (1, 1) and press slot 2 at (2, 1), then release both. Slot 2 now holds a copy of slot 1 (copying overwrites whatever slot 2 held).

3. Press slot 2 at (2, 1) to select it while stopped.

4. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.

5. Press the right end of the transposition fader, (16, 8), twice. Each press adds one semitone and the tooltip shows Transpose: 2.

6. Press Play. Slot 2 plays 62, 64, 66, 67. With Song mode On, playback moves on to the next slot after the repeats set in Slot setup; to hold on one slot, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn Song mode Off (E3). Press Stop.

7. Press Grid (6, 8), then slot 1 at (1, 1), and press Play to hear the original at 60, 62, 64, 65, because slot 1 kept its transposition of 0.

Check that the raised notes are still inside the usable range of the sound you are playing.
recipes.title: Play a copied Song slot a tone higher

features.prose:
The Song Editor contains 96 Song Sequence slots, arranged in six rows of 16. Slot 1 is grid (1,1), slot 2 is (2,1), slot 16 is (16,1), slot 17 is (1,2) and slot 96 is (16,6). Each slot stores one complete sequence: which patterns each channel plays, merge modes, masks, scales, mutes and the sequence length. Use a slot for each section of a song.

Press Song, grid (6,8), to open the editor. The norns shows Song Playback. Fill slots by copying a finished section into a new slot and editing the copy (see Interacting with Slots). Read slot brightness in Button Indicators. Let Song mode chain slots automatically with Song Mode Operations. Set how many steps a section plays with the fader on row 7 (Adjusting Song Sequence Length).

Watch: [Song editor demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2972)

recipes.text:
Starting point: slot 1 holds a four-step motif on channel 1 (C D E F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; build it as in Creating a First Loop), playback is stopped and Song mode is On (the default; Song Playback shows it as AUTO). Slots 2 and 3 are empty and dim at (2,1) and (3,1).

1. Press Song (6,8). Slot 1 at (1,1) is bright because it is selected. A slot plays 64 steps by default, about eleven seconds at 90 BPM with Rate /1, so shorten the audition first: tap (2,7) to set the global length to 1 step, then tap (8,7) three times to make it 4 steps. The length belongs to the slot, so the copy in step 2 keeps it.

2. Hold slot 1 at (1,1), press slot 2 at (2,1), then release both. Slot 2 turns mid-bright: it is a full copy of slot 1.

3. Tap slot 2 at (2,1). It turns bright and slot 1 drops to mid-bright.

4. Press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Slot 2 now plays the motif an octave higher. Slot 1 is unchanged. Change a rhythm or a mask instead of the octave if you prefer.

5. Press Song (6,8) and look at slot 3 at (3,1). It stays dim because it is empty, and an empty slot ends the group after slot 2.

6. Tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Slot 1 plays the motif (60, 62, 64, 65), then slot 2 plays it an octave higher (72, 74, 76, 77), then playback returns to slot 1 and repeats.

Each slot plays for its global length times its Repeats, so with the length left at 64 a slot lasts about eleven seconds. Check or change Song mode in Song tasks > Slot setup (see Song Mode Operations). The captured example Loop a song group or hold one slot, below, plays two groups built this way (slots 1-2 and 4-5) and what happens when Song mode is turned Off.

features.prose:
Read Song slot status from the grid. The slots fill rows 1 to 6.

* Dim buttons indicate empty slots.
* Mid-glow buttons indicate slots containing rhythms and patterns.
* The brightly lit button identifies the Song Sequence that is selected, or playing.
* A slot you pressed during playback blinks (its light pulses down and back up) until the current sequence finishes and the slot takes over.

Example: copy slot 1 to slot 2 and select slot 2. Slot 1 is mid-bright, slot 2 is bright and slot 3 is dim. Press Play and slot 2 stays bright. Press slot 1 while slot 2 plays: slot 1 blinks until slot 2 finishes, then slot 1 turns bright and slot 2 returns to mid-bright. Copy empty slot 3 over slot 2 while stopped and slot 2 goes dim.

features.prose:
Press a slot button to select its Song Sequence. Slot 1 is grid (1,1), slot 2 is (2,1), slot 16 is (16,1) and slot 17 is (1,2). While stopped, the press selects the slot at once and the norns shows Slot setup for it. During playback, the press queues the slot until the current sequence finishes.

To copy a slot, press and hold the source slot, press the destination slot, then release both. The destination becomes a full copy of the source. Editing the copy leaves the source untouched. The destination’s previous contents are overwritten, so copy onto an empty slot unless you mean to replace it.

To erase a slot, copy an empty slot over it: hold the empty slot and press the slot to clear. There is no undo.

recipes.text:
Starting point: slot 1 holds a section you want to keep, for example the four-note motif C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Playback is stopped and the Song editor is open (Song, grid (6,8)).

1. Hold slot 1 at (1,1). While holding it, press an empty slot, slot 2 at (2,1). Release both. Slot 2 changes from dim to mid-bright: it is a full copy and slot 1 is untouched. Copying overwrites the destination, so choose an empty one.

2. Tap slot 2 at (2,1). It turns bright (selected) and slot 1 drops to mid-bright.

3. Edit the variation while stopped: press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Only slot 2 changes. (Changing a mask instead works too; either edit stays in the selected slot.)

4. Press Play (1,8). Slot 2 plays the motif an octave higher (72, 74, 76, 77); with Song mode On playback then carries on to slot 1, so press Stop when you have heard enough. Press Song (6,8), tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play: the original section still plays 60, 62, 64, 65. Tap slot 2 to compare.

The destination is a full copy, so editing it never changes the original. To erase a slot you no longer need, hold an empty slot and press the slot to clear. There is no undo. The captured example [Copy a slot, then change the copy](#song-mode-operations/song-copy-and-compare) shows steps 1 to 3 (the copy and the octave edit); to hear slot 1 and slot 2 compare, follow [Build two song groups](#song-mode-operations/song-build-two-groups), which plays the copies. The captured example [Read Song slot lights](#button-indicators/song-slot-light-states) shows the lights for a copy and for the erase.

features.prose:
Song mode plays your slots as an arrangement. It is on by default. With Song mode on, the sequencer advances to the next filled slot after the current slot has played its Repeats. Turn it on or off in Song tasks > Slot setup (select Song mode with E2, set it with E3, apply with K3) or in PARAMS > MOSAIC > Song mode.

A run of filled slots with no gap is a group. When playback reaches an empty slot, it returns to the first filled slot of its group. Slots 1 and 2 with slot 3 empty therefore play 1, 2, 1, 2 and so on. Use empty slots to separate groups.

Press another slot during playback to queue a change. The slot blinks, and the change takes effect after the current sequence, including its repeats, completes. This is how you move from one group to another.

With Song mode off, slots do not advance by themselves: the selected slot keeps repeating. A queued manual selection still takes over at the end of the current sequence.

recipes.text:
Starting point: channel 1 plays its default four-note motif (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) on slot 1, the first slot. Song mode is On (the default) and playback is stopped. Group A will be slots 1-2 and group B slots 4-5. Slots 3 and 6 stay empty.

1. Set the length: press Song (6,8) with slot 1 selected. Tap (2,7), which sets the global length to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once to add one step. The length is now 2 steps, so each slot plays only the first two notes, 60 and 62.

2. Copy slot 1 to slots 2, 4 and 5: hold slot 1 at (1,1) and press slot 2 at (2,1). Repeat for slot 4 at (4,1) and slot 5 at (5,1). The copies keep the two-step length.

3. Voice slot 2: tap slot 2 at (2,1), press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Slot 2 will play 72, 74.

4. Voice slot 4: press Song (6,8), tap slot 4 at (4,1), press Channel (3,8), tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +2 at (12,8). Slot 4 will play 84, 86.

5. Voice slot 5 the same way: Song (6,8), slot 5 at (5,1), Channel (3,8), channel 1 at (1,1) and octave -1 at (9,8). Slot 5 will play 48, 50.

6. Check the lights: slots 1, 2, 4 and 5 are mid-bright, slots 3 and 6 are dim and the selected slot is bright.

7. Tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Group A loops: slot 1 plays 60, 62, slot 2 plays 72, 74, then empty slot 3 sends playback back to slot 1.

8. While slot 1 sounds, tap slot 4 at (4,1). It blinks, queued. When slot 1 finishes, group B plays: slot 4 plays 84, 86, slot 5 plays 48, 50, then empty slot 6 returns playback to the first slot of group B. To go back, tap slot 1 or slot 2 to queue a return to group A.

For a more musical version, replace the octave edits with a different bass rhythm or harmony in group B and keep one motif in both groups. The captured examples below build these slots: Build two song groups follows steps 1 to 7, up to the first group looping, and Loop a song group or hold one slot builds the same slots and goes on to the second group and queued selection (step 8).

features.musical_use: Shorten a section without changing channel endpoints. Increase global length to restore the remaining steps. Channel lengths and clock rates can differ within this limit.
features.prose:
Use the fader at the lower left of the Song Editor to set the global length of the selected Song Sequence from 1 to 64 steps. It is on row 7, columns 1 to 8. Press Song (6,8) to open the editor. A press on the fader opens Song Playback on the norns, where Global length shows the new value.

* (1,7) subtracts one step. (8,7) adds one step.
* The inner buttons jump to a coarse value: (2,7) sets 1, (3,7) sets 13, (4,7) sets 32, (5,7) sets 38, (6,7) sets 51 and (7,7) sets 64.
* To reach an exact value, jump to a nearby coarse value and finish with the end buttons. For 16, tap (3,7) and then (8,7) three times.

Channel start and end steps may lie outside the global-length range. A channel’s played length cannot exceed global length. The limit counts steps from the channel start: with channel range 2–4 and global length 2, playback repeats steps 2 and 3. Increase global length to restore the remaining selected steps.

The same limit applies to the scale track. Each track follows its own clock rate, and explicit song reset options still apply.

Watch: [Global pattern length demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=3160)

recipes.text:
Starting point: channel 1 plays a four-step motif on steps 1 to 4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Its channel range is steps 1 to 4 and the global length is 64 steps. Playback is stopped.
1. Press Song (6,8). The length fader is on row 7, columns 1 to 8.
2. Tap (2,7) to set the global length to one step (the buttons between the ends jump to 1, 13, 32, 38, 51 and 64), then tap (8,7) once to add one step. Song Playback shows Global length reading two.
3. Press Play (1,8). Only the first two steps play: MIDI 60, 62, 60, 62 and so on. The channel range is still steps 1 to 4, so nothing is deleted.
4. Press Stop (1,8). Tap (8,7) twice to set the global length to four steps, then press Play. All four steps return: 60, 62, 64, 65.
Use this to loop a short fragment of a longer motif without editing it, then restore the full phrase. The end buttons (1,7) and (8,7) change the length one step at a time. The captured example Set the global song length, below, uses the two end buttons on the Song Playback screen: it takes one step off 64 (63) and puts it back. It does not play, so follow steps 2 to 4 to hear the effect.

features.prose:
The Song page opens on Playback. This read-only screen shows the playing slot (Playing), the slot that follows (Next, or HOLD when Song mode is off), the current pass within its repeats (Pass, for example 1 / 2), the global pattern length and whether Song mode is advancing (AUTO) or off (MANUAL). Turn E1 to open Song tasks: Playback, Slot setup, Tempo / feel and Channel view.

Open Slot setup to set Repeats, the number of passes the selected Song Sequence plays before Song mode advances, and to see Song mode. With Song mode off, select slots manually.

Open Tempo / feel (the screen is titled GLOBAL FEEL) to set the global tempo and Swing or Shuffle. The tempo is shared by every slot.

Channel view opens the same screen as in Pattern tasks: the viewed channel on its own.

features.musical_use: Change one step without editing the pattern: lift a single bass note an octave, accent one hit, open a filter on the last note, or change the scale for one part of the phrase.
features.prose:
A lock stores a value on one step, so that step differs from the channel default. Hold the step on the grid, change the value, then release the step. The lock stays in place and the screen returns to the channel default.

Each lock type has its own control:

1. Parameter lock: on Channel tasks > Trig params, hold a step and turn E3. See [Trig Param Locks](#trig-param-locks).
2. Mask lock: on Channel tasks > Masks, hold a step and turn E3. See [Mask Locks](#mask-locks).
3. Octave lock: hold a step and press an octave button on Grid row 8, columns 8–12. See [Octave Locks](#octave-locks).
4. Scale lock: hold a step and press a scale slot on Grid row 3. On a channel page the lock affects that channel. On the Scale page it is global. See [Scale Locks](#scale-locks).
5. Transposition lock: on the Scale page, hold a scale-track step and press the transposition fader on Grid row 8. See [Transposition Locks](#transposition-locks).

Parameter, mask and octave locks change their own step only. A transposition lock stays in force on the steps that follow it until a later transposition lock replaces it. A channel scale lock lasts as set by Scales lock until ptn end (see [Scale Locks](#scale-locks)). A global scale lock lasts until another global lock replaces it or the scale track wraps.

To remove a lock, hold its step and press K2 on the screen where you set it. For octave, scale and transposition locks you can also press the same button again.

features.prose:
Before you set a parameter lock, assign the parameter to one of the ten Trig params slots (see [Trig Parameters](#trig-parameters)). The value you set with no step held is the channel default that every step sends.

Set a parameter lock:

1. Open Trig params from Channel tasks with E1.
2. Turn E2 to select the assigned slot.
3. Hold a step on the channel sequencer.
4. Turn E3 to the value for that step. While the step is held, the cell shows the held value and an L marker.
5. Release the step. The cell shows the channel default again; the step keeps its lock.

Clear a step's parameter trig locks:

1. Open Trig params.
2. Hold the step and press K2.

Clear all parameter trig locks on the channel:

1. Open Trig params.
2. Release all steps.
3. Hold K1 and press K2.

Video: [Trig locks demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2235)

recipes.text:
Start with a channel that has trigs on steps 1 to 4 (see Build a phrase), sends to a device that lists a controller you can hear on a filter, and is stopped. This recipe uses CC 74, the usual filter cutoff controller: a generic CC device lists it as CC 74, and a device whose configuration names it shows it as Cutoff. The scenes on this page use CC 1 the same way.
1. Open Trig params: turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Trig params, press K3.
2. Turn E2 to slot 1, press K2, turn E3 to CC 74 (Cutoff), press K3 to assign it, then press K2 to return to the slot view.
3. With no step held, turn E3 to 40, the channel default: every step sends CC 74 = 40 before its note.
4. Hold step 4, the last trig, and turn E3 to 100 (the cell shows 100 and the L marker). Release step 4 and the cell shows 40 again.
5. Press Play. Steps 1 to 3 sound with cutoff 40 and step 4 sends CC 74 = 100 just before its note, so the last note of each loop is brighter.
6. To remove the accent, hold step 4 and press K2.
On this page, the scene Lock a value, then clear just that step shows the same gestures with Fixed Note, the MIDI strip of Use the first and last Trig params slots shows CC values arriving just before their notes, and Keep a stored value while locking a step shows one locked CC value ahead of a step's note while the other steps send the stored value. For a smooth rise instead of a jump, see Param Slides.

controls.gesture: Select an assigned parameter in Trig params and press K3 with no grid step or K1 held.
controls.result: Toggle channel-wide sliding for that parameter. Enabled cells show S.

controls.gesture: Hold a channel step and press K3 on the selected parameter.
controls.result: Toggle a slide from that step to the next lock of the same parameter. Other locks are unchanged.

controls.gesture: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and change Wrap param slides.
controls.result: On lets an eligible final slide reach the first lock across the repeat of the same pattern. It never slides into another song pattern.

features.musical_use: Open or close a filter, raise a send level or bend a modulation amount over a few steps, rather than in one jump.
features.prose:
A slide needs at least two parameter locks of the same parameter on the channel. Set them first (see [Trig Param Locks](#trig-param-locks)).

Slide a parameter across the whole channel:

1. Open Trig params and select the parameter with E2.
2. Release all steps and press K3. The cell shows S.

Between every pair of locks of that parameter the value now moves gradually. Press K3 again with no step held to switch it off.

Slide from one step only:

1. Hold the step that has the lock you want to slide from.
2. With the parameter selected, press K3.

The held step slides to the next lock of that parameter. Other locks of the parameter still jump.

Slides do not cross into a different song pattern. Turn on Wrap param slides to let the last lock of a repeating pattern slide back to the first lock (see [Parameter Slides Wrap](#parameter-slides-wrap)). Slides use extra processing, so use them only where you need them.

Video: [Param slides demo](https://youtu.be/iGx5fmrbatA?t=515)

recipes.text:
Start with a channel with trigs on steps 1 to 4, a controller assigned to a Trig params slot (CC 1 as in the scenes, or the CC that drives your filter), and playback stopped (see the Brighten the last note recipe on Trig Param Locks).
1. Open Trig params and turn E2 to that slot.
2. Hold step 1, turn E3 to 24 and release. Hold step 3, turn E3 to 96 and release.
3. Release all steps and press K3. The cell shows S. Press Play: the value leaves 24 at step 1 and reaches 96 as step 3's note starts (the CC strip in the scene lists 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96). Press Play again to stop.
4. To slide only the first lock, first add a third lock: hold step 4, turn E3 to 48 and release. Press K3 with no step held to switch the channel-wide slide off, then hold step 1 and press K3 (the cell shows S while step 1 is held). Press Play: 24 glides to 96 between steps 1 and 3, then jumps to 48 at step 4. With only two locks, a slide on step 1 alone and a slide on every lock sound the same; the third lock is what separates them. Stop.
5. To loop the sweep, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn Wrap param slides On.
6. Release all steps and press K3 to switch the channel-wide slide on again. The last lock, step 4, now slides back towards 24 across the loop boundary instead of holding at 48.

features.musical_use: Move a channel to a different scale for part of a phrase, or run a chord progression across all channels from the global scale track.
features.prose:
Scale slots are the 16 buttons on Grid row 3. A scale lock applies a slot from a chosen step. Set it on a channel page for that channel only, or on the Scale page for every channel that has no channel scale lock.

Set a channel scale lock:

1. Select the channel and hold a step on the channel sequencer.
2. Press the required scale slot on Grid row 3. The norns screen shows Scale source.

Set a global scale lock:

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.
2. Hold a step on the scale track and press the required scale slot on Grid row 3. The norns screen shows Scale overview.

Clear a step lock:

1. Hold the step.
2. Press K2, or press the same scale slot again.

A channel scale lock overrides the global scale and global locks.

With Scales lock until ptn end On (the default), a channel scale lock lasts until the channel wraps to its start or another channel scale lock replaces it.

With the option Off, the lock lasts until the next active trig that passes its probability check. A trig that fails its probability check does not clear it. A scale lock on the next accepted trig replaces the previous lock.

Global scale-track locks ignore this option. They last until another global lock replaces them or the global scale track wraps.

features.prose:
Transposition locks belong to the global scale track on the Scale page. Reach the Scale page from the Channel editor with Grid (4,8) and set the lock on a scale-track step there, not on a channel step.

Set a transposition lock:

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.
2. Hold a step on the scale track.
3. Press the required value on the transposition fader, Grid row 8, columns 8–16.
4. Release the step. The norns screen shows Scale overview.

From that step, the lock replaces the global transposition fader value. It is added to the selected scale's own Transpose value. It stays in force on the following steps until a later transposition lock replaces it.

A lock of 0 is a real lock. It cancels the global transposition from that step. It is not the same as having no lock.

Clear a transposition lock:

1. Hold the step on the Scale page.
2. Press K2, or press the same fader value again.

features.musical_use: Save a named project before trying a change, so you can return to the earlier version. Autosave is a safety net, not a version history.
features.prose:
Save a named project:

1. Press K1 to open PARAMS and choose MOSAIC.
2. Choose Save project.
3. Enter a descriptive name on the text entry screen and press K3 to confirm. The suggested name is new.

Mosaic writes a project file (.ptn) and a parameter file under that name. Saving under a name that already exists replaces that save. Press K2 in the dialog to cancel; no file changes.

Load a project: open PARAMS > MOSAIC, choose Load, pick the file in the file picker and press K3.

Use named saves for versions that autosave must not overwrite. When playback is stopped, 60 seconds of inactivity normally saves the current project as autosave. Mosaic loads the most recent autosave at startup. Named saves are separate files and autosave does not change them.

Before replacing the current project, Mosaic checks saved song slots, global lengths, channel ranges and scale-track ranges. If a check fails, the screen identifies the problem. The current project and playback are retained.

A rejected load suspends autosave to protect the rejected file. Editing, playing and cancelling a dialog do not resume autosave. A successful valid load, a successful named save or New resumes the normal idle autosave interval. A failed save leaves autosave suspended.

Valid saved one-step ranges are supported. There is no one-step range gesture. Validation covers the saved range structure; it does not check every possible corrupted project field.

features.musical_use: Leave On for a finished arrangement; turn Off to stay on one section or move between sections by hand.
features.prose:
Song mode is On by default. With Song mode On, the song steps through its slots on its own, according to the Song Editor's global length and the groups of slots you filled. Playback moves from one slot to the next when the current slot reaches its global length, and a group of slots loops.

With Song mode Off, Mosaic keeps playing the selected slot and moves only when you select another slot yourself. Use Off to rehearse a single section or to move between sections by hand. Song mode also decides whether the repeat reset in Reset on pattern repeat applies: with Song mode Off, a repeating slot is not reset.

recipes.text:
Starting point: Song mode is On (the default) and the song has two filled slots, slot 1 and slot 2, so it would normally play 1, 2, 1, 2 and so on. Playback is stopped.

1. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC (tap K1), select Song mode and turn E3 to Off.

2. Press Song (6,8) to open the Song editor. The slots are the buttons on rows 1 to 6; slot 1 is (1,1) and slot 2 is (2,1). Tap the slot you want to rehearse, for example slot 1 at (1,1).

3. Press Play at (1,8). The slot repeats: with Song mode Off it never moves on to slot 2 by itself, so you hear the same section again and again.

4. To move to another section, tap its slot, for example (2,1) while the music plays. The press is queued and takes over when the current pass ends. Turn Song mode On again to run the whole arrangement.

For comparison, with Song mode On the same two slots play 1, 2, 1, 2. The captured example [Loop a song group or hold one slot](#song-mode-operations/song-mode-groups-and-selection) shows both: with Song mode On a group of slots loops, and with Song mode Off slot 1 repeats (60, 62, 60, 62) and a manual selection of slot 2 still takes over at the end of the pass.

4. Turn Reset on song seq change On and play again. Slot 2 now enters on C4 (72), the first step, exactly at the change at 10.7 seconds.

features.prose:
Reset on pattern repeat is Off by default. With On and Song mode On, every channel returns to its first step when the same song slot repeats at the end of its global length. A channel with its own length or clock rate therefore starts its phrase again on each repeat. With Off, the channel's phase carries across the repeat, so unequal lengths drift against the song.

Example: a three-step channel at Clock Mod /9 plays a note every 1.5 seconds, so its three notes 60, 62, 64 cycle every 4.5 seconds. The slot repeats every 64 steps (10.7 seconds), which is not a whole number of cycles. With Off, the cycle carries on across the boundary, so the third note, 64, sounds at 12 seconds. With On, note 60 sounds exactly at the boundary. With Song mode Off the slot is not repeated by the song, so the reset does not apply.

features.musical_use: Turn On for a cyclic sweep, such as a filter that returns to its start without a jump.
features.prose:
Wrap param slides is Off by default. A parameter slide moves a value smoothly from one lock to the next. The last lock in a loop has no later lock to slide toward, so with Off it holds its value and the first lock is recalled when the loop restarts. With On, and the current song pattern repeating, the last slide runs on to the first lock of the same pattern, so the value arrives at the first lock with the first note of the next loop.

Example: CC 1 locks of 24 on step 1, 96 on step 3 and 48 on step 4, with a slide on step 4 in a four-step loop at 90 BPM. With Off, CC 1 holds 48 through step 4 and jumps to 24 at the loop point. With On, it descends in a straight line from 48 to 24 over one sixteenth-note step (one sixth of a second) and reaches 24 with the next first note.

recipes.text:
Start with a stopped channel with trigs on steps 1 to 4 and Wrap param slides Off (its default) in PARAMS > MOSAIC.
1. Open Trig params: turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Trig params, press K3. Press K2, turn E3 to CC 1 (or the CC that drives your filter), press K3 to assign it and K2 to return.
2. Hold step 1 and turn E3 to 24, release; hold step 3 and turn E3 to 96, release; hold step 4 and turn E3 to 48, release. Step 2 has no lock, so it sends only the channel default (the scenes store 63).
3. Hold step 4 and press K3 to give that last lock a slide.
4. Press Play and let it loop. On a MIDI monitor, or in the MIDI strip of the scene Carry a slide across the loop boundary, CC 1 holds 48 from step 4 and then jumps to 24 at the loop point. Stop.
5. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Wrap param slides and turn E3 to On, then Play again. CC 1 now glides from 48 through 40 and 32 to 24 across one step and arrives with the first note.

features.musical_use: Keep an Elektron pattern selection in step with Mosaic's song slots.
features.prose:
Elektron program changes is Off by default. With On, Mosaic sends a MIDI program change whenever it selects or moves to a song slot, so a receiving pattern-based instrument follows your song. The example in this manual uses the Digitakt device configuration; any receiver that accepts program changes on the same channel works the same way.

The value counts from 0 on the wire. Song slot 1 sends value 0, which the receiver labels pattern 1; slot 2 sends 1, labelled pattern 2. While playing, each incoming slot is announced once, at least half a step (about 83 ms at 90 BPM) before its first note, and pressing Play first sends the slot that is about to sound. Set the receiver to accept program changes, and set the channel in Elektron p.change channel.

recipes.text:
1. Give the song two slots. In the Song editor (grid (6,8)) hold slot 1 at (1,1) and tap slot 2 at (2,1) to copy it. Set Global length to 4 steps if you want to hear the changes quickly.
2. On channel 1's Device screen choose the Digitakt configuration. Set the receiver to accept program changes on MIDI channel 10, its default. If you have no Digitakt, watch the MIDI output instead: the strip lists Program 1 (ch 10) and Program 0 (ch 10), the bytes C9 01 and C9 00.
3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Elektron program changes and turn E3 to On.
4. While stopped, press song slot 2 at grid (2,1). Mosaic sends program change C9 01 and the receiver switches to its pattern 2 (wire value 1); the strip lists Program 1 (ch 10). Press slot 1 for pattern 1 (C9 00, Program 0 (ch 10)).
5. Select slot 1 and press Play. Each slot change is announced once, just before the new slot sounds.

Change it only if your receiver is set to a different channel. The same channel must be set on the receiver and in Mosaic, or the receiver ignores the messages.

recipes.text:
Use this when your receiver listens for program changes on a channel other than 10. Finish Follow Mosaic's slots with a Digitakt first, so Elektron program changes is On and the song has two slots.
1. Make sure the receiver listens for program changes on channel 1.
2. In PARAMS > MOSAIC select Elektron p.change channel and turn E3 left nine detents from 10 to 1.
3. While stopped, press song slot 2 at grid (2,1). Mosaic sends program change C0 01: the strip lists Program 1 (ch 1) instead of Program 1 (ch 10) (C9 01).

controls.gesture: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select Trigless locks. Change its value.
controls.result: On honours parameter locks on steps with no active trig. Default: On.

features.musical_use: Leave On to keep modulation moving through rests, for example a filter sweep under a sparse rhythm. Turn Off so rests stay fully still.
features.prose:
Trigless locks is On by default. A trigless lock is a parameter lock on a step with no trig, a rest. With On, Mosaic still sends the lock on that step, so a filter or other control keeps moving while no note plays. With Off, locks on steps without a trig are skipped, and only steps that have a trig send their locks.

A trig that fails its probability check still counts as a trig, so its locks are sent either way; only a removed trig is affected by this option. Example: CC 1 locks of 24, 48, 72 and 96 on steps 1–4. Remove the trig on step 3. With Off, CC 1 sends 24, 48 and 96. With On, it sends all four, 72 included. Locks are sent just before the step's note.

recipes.text:
Start with a stopped channel with a trig on every step 1 to 4, CC 1 assigned to a Trig params slot (see Trig Param Locks), and a device or MIDI monitor that shows CC 1.
1. Hold each of steps 1 to 4 in turn and lock CC 1 to 24, 48, 72 and 96 with E3.
2. Open the Pattern editor (grid (5,8)), tap step 3 to remove its trig, and return to the Channel editor with (3,8).
3. Play. Trigless locks is On by default, so the value 72 is still sent at step 3 although no note sounds. The scene silences channel 1 with Trig probability 0, so its MIDI strip shows only the CC values (24, 48, 72, 96) beside a steady timing reference on channel 2.
4. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Trigless locks and turn E3 to Off. Play again: step 3's 72 is no longer sent.

controls.gesture: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select Lock all to pentatonic. Change its value.
controls.result: On restricts resolved notes to Mosaic’s five-note selection for the selected scale. Default: Off.

features.musical_use: Turn On to keep every note inside a five-note set so loose or generative material stays consonant.
features.prose:
Lock all to pent. is Off by default. With On, every resolved note is restricted to Mosaic's five-note selection for the selected scale: degrees 1/2/3/5/6 for Major, 1/3/4/5/7 for Minor, 2/3/5/6/7 for Lydian, and so on (the full list is under Lock merged to pentatonic). A note outside the selection moves to the nearest allowed pitch, and an exact tie picks the lower one.

Example in C major with a seven-step pattern of degrees I–VII: Off plays 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71. On plays 60, 62, 64, 64, 67, 69, 72 (F falls to E, B rises to C). In C natural minor, On plays 60, 63, 63, 65, 67, 67, 70. In Lydian, the tonic C snaps down to B, giving 59, 62, 64, 67, 67, 69, 71.

recipes.text:
Use this option to keep generated, random or merged material consonant: with Lock all to pent. On, every note lands on the five-note version of the scale. The seven-note walk below is a diagnostic rather than a phrase, so you can hear exactly which degrees are replaced. Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) in C major.

1. Build seven degrees. Press Pattern (5,8), select pattern 1 (1,1) and tap trigs on steps 5, 6 and 7 at (5,4), (6,4) and (7,4). Press Pattern (5,8) again for the note page and tap (5,3), (6,2) and (7,1) to put steps 5 to 7 on degrees V, VI and VII: steps 1 to 7 now form a rising diagonal.

2. Set the range. Press Channel (3,8), hold step 1 (1,4), tap step 7 (7,4) and release both. Tap Play (1,8) and listen: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71. Tap Play to stop.

3. Restrict the notes. Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock all to pent. and turn E3 to On. Close the menu and tap Play: 60, 62, 64, 64, 67, 69, 72. F falls to E and B rises to C because only C D E G A are allowed. Tap Play to stop.

4. Change the scale. Open the Scale Editor (4,8), turn E3 to another scale, press K3 and return to Channel (3,8). Play again: each scale has its own five notes. Natural minor, for example, gives 60, 63, 63, 65, 67, 67, 70.

5. Turn the option Off in PARAMS > MOSAIC to restore all seven degrees of the current scale.
recipes.title: Hear every note restricted

controls.gesture: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select Lock random to pent.. Change its value.
controls.result: On restricts notes changed by random trig locks to the selected scale’s Mosaic five-note selection. Default: On.

features.musical_use: Leave On so random pitch changes stay consonant; turn Off to let random notes use the whole scale.
features.prose:
Lock random to pent. is On by default. Random Note and Twos Random Note shift a note by a random number of scale degrees. With On, a note moved by a nonzero random offset snaps to the nearest note of Mosaic's five-note selection for the scale; with Off it lands on any of the seven scale degrees. A step whose random offset is zero keeps its own note.

Example with Random Note 4 (offsets -2 to +2 degrees) on C D E F: with Off the draws can land on F (65) and B (59) as well as C, D, E, G and A. With On, every note moved by a random offset is one of C D E G A. The capture uses a fixed random seed; your own runs will differ each time.

recipes.text:
Lock random to pent. is On by default. This recipe lets you hear what it does by switching it Off and On with Random Note at 4. Random Note chooses its offsets at random, so listen to several loops: a short run may not include every note.

Starting point: channel 1 plays pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) in C major; no Trig params slot is assigned yet.

1. Assign Random Note. Select channel 1 and press E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Trig params and press K3. Press K2 to open the parameter list, turn E3 to Random Note, press K3 to assign it to the first slot and press K2 to return. The slot reads 0 and the pattern still plays C, D, E, F.

2. Set the amount. With the Random Note slot selected (E2), turn E3 four detents right to 4. Each note is now offset by -2, -1, 0, +1 or +2 scale degrees at random. A step that draws offset 0 keeps its own note.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock random to pent. and turn E3 to Off. Close the menu, tap Play and listen to several loops: F and B join the random notes, and one of them will turn up within a few passes. Tap Play to stop.

4. Turn Lock random to pent. On and play several loops again. The random notes now stay on C, D, E, G and A. A step that draws offset 0 keeps its own note, so a plain F in the pattern can still sound. The random stream is not reset between the two runs, so the two runs will not start with the same notes; compare which notes occur, not the order.
recipes.title: Compare random notes with and without the filter

controls.gesture: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select Lock merged to pent.. Change its value.
controls.result: On snaps merged scale degrees to Mosaic’s scale-specific five-note selection; the lower pitch wins exact ties and snapping can cross octaves. Default: On.

features.musical_use: Leave On so merge results stay inside the five-note selection; turn Off to hear the merge results unchanged.
features.prose:
Lock merged to pent. is On by default. A merge mode combines the notes of several patterns; this option restricts the result to Mosaic's five-note selection for the selected scale. Example in C major with pattern 1 on degrees I, III, V, VII and pattern 2 on III, V, VII, I: Average merge gives degrees II, IV, VI, IV. With Off you hear 62, 65, 69, 65 (D F A F). With On, F is not in the major selection and snaps to the nearer E, so you hear 62, 64, 69, 64.

The selections use one-based degrees of each named seven-note scale:
- Major and Harmonic Major: 1/2/3/5/6.
- Minor, Harmonic Minor and Melodic Minor: 1/3/4/5/7.
- Dorian: 1/2/4/5/7.
- Phrygian: 1/3/4/6/7.
- Lydian: 2/3/5/6/7.
- Mixolydian: 1/2/4/5/6.
- Locrian: 2/3/4/6/7.

Apply the named scale's alterations to these degrees. The selection does not always retain the tonic or avoid semitones.

Merged values remain seven-note scale degrees, not five-note indices. Their scale pitches snap to the nearest selected pitch across repeated octaves. An exact tie selects the lower pitch. Snapping can cross an octave boundary.

For example, Lydian C snaps to the B below it. Melodic Minor A snaps down to G rather than the equally distant B.

The scale root is used when set; otherwise, the song root is used. The effective octave offset is applied afterward.

recipes.text:
Lock merged to pent. is On by default. Merge modes can produce notes that no pattern contains, such as an average between two degrees; this option snaps those results onto the five-note version of the scale. Use this recipe to hear the difference.

Starting point: channel 1 is empty and the scale is C major.

1. Build pattern 1 on degrees I, III, V, VII (C E G B) on steps 1 to 4 and pattern 2 on III, V, VII, I (E G B C) on steps 1 to 4, as in Build a phrase, and pattern 3 as a velocity source (four trigs on steps 1 to 4, never assigned to the channel). Both note patterns have a trig on all four steps.

2. Assign both patterns to channel 1 with (1,2) and (2,2).

3. Choose the merge modes. Both patterns trig on the same steps, and the default trig merge, Skip, silences steps that trig in more than one pattern, so set the trig merge to All: press the trig merge button (14,8) until Channel tasks > Merge modes shows ALL. Check that the note merge reads AVERAGE; the average of each pair of degrees is II, IV, VI, IV (D, F, A, F).

4. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock merged to pent. and turn E3 to Off. Tap Play: 62, 65, 69, 65 (D, F, A, F). Tap Play to stop.

5. Turn Lock merged to pent. On and play again: 62, 64, 69, 64. The two F notes become E, because F is not in the pentatonic.
recipes.title: Compare merged notes with and without the filter

recipes.text:
Starting point: a MIDI keyboard is connected to Mosaic's MIDI input on port 1, channel 1 has a device selected (it plays through the test or your own synth) and the scale is C major. The norns names MIDI 60 as C3, so the key you call middle C sounds 60.

2. Open the Scale Editor (4,8). Turn E2 to Scale, turn E3 to natural minor and press K3 to apply it. Return to the Channel editor (3,8).

3. Play C to C on the white keys again: 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72. The keyboard keeps its layout while the scale underneath it has changed.

features.summary: Set decorative screen motion.
features.title: Screen Options

controls.gesture: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select UI motion. Change its value.
controls.result: Off keeps the screen still; On enables decorative motion and musical characters without changing input or sequencer timing. Default: On.

details.text: Overflow scrolling is restricted to the selected label or value. Fitting text and neighboring rows remain stationary. Off stops scrolling; ~ indicates shortened text, and exact values that cannot fit report LAYOUT OVERFLOW.
details.title: Selected overflow text

details.text: Playing uses musical sequencer transport position. Stopped uses the selected musical clock and does not start Mosaic or sound notes. Off or missing/invalid clock holds the rest pose. Native PARAMS owns its own screen.
details.title: Miniature header timing

features.musical_use: Turn Off for a calm, still screen, or when photographing or filming the display; leave On for animated feedback.
features.prose:
UI motion is On by default. It controls the decorative animation of the norns screen only; it never changes sequencer timing, input or the notes you hear. With Off the screen is still.

With On, a miniature graphic in the header identifies the screen and moves with the music: while playing it follows the sequencer's transport pulses, while stopped it follows the selected norns musical clock without starting playback. With Off, or if the clock is missing or invalid, it holds its rest pose. The start-up animation, the shadow that glides across the Masks and Trig params grids, values that roll into place, the characters on some screens and the small dial beside a single numeric value are decoration and are governed by the same setting.

Only the selected label or value that is too long for its row scrolls right to left. Fitting labels, neighbouring rows, the title and controls stay still. A long selected value first gets its own full-width row. With motion Off, shortened text ends in ~, and an exact value that cannot fit shows LAYOUT OVERFLOW instead of silently changing.

The light running round the Mosaic mark, the shadow gliding across the Masks and Trig params grids (diagonally when it changes row) and values rolling into place all stop with motion Off. The Rhythm Doctor dances to the tempo of the captured bank, and the Merge Shape garden sways and the Harmony choir bobs while the sequencer plays. Motion never delays input and never hides a value for more than a moment.

recipes.text:
Use this to see what the setting does before you film or photograph the display. Changing a value only makes the screen react: the point is the header mark.
1. Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select UI motion in the Screen section and turn E3 to Off.
2. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, select Clock and press K3. Turn E3 to /1.5 and press K3, then restore /1. All values stay readable and the header mark does not move.
3. Return to PARAMS, set UI motion to On, and repeat. The header mark now animates; values are as readable as before.
4. Play the pattern in each setting. The notes and timing are identical.
recipes.title: Compare the screen with motion Off and On

features.musical_use: Use Merge Shape to add or remove channel trigs without editing the assigned patterns. Use Harmony to set output registers.
features.prose:
Merge Shape changes a channel’s merged rhythm. Harmony places output notes in specified registers. Neither feature rewrites source patterns. Older projects restore their saved Skip, Only or All Strategy and retain its original MIDI, timing and random behavior. Foundation and Fragments are other exclusive choices of the same Strategy selector.

Merge modes, Merge Shape and Harmony are consecutive Channel tasks. Merge Shape and Voice leading use vertical lists. Editable rows display their current value. Submenus display OPEN >. The selected row is marked >.

1. Open Merge Shape or Harmony from Channel tasks.
2. Turn E2 to select a row.
3. Turn E3 to change a staged value.
4. Press K3 on OPEN > to open that settings list. The bottom line names the action, for example K3 OPEN RHYTHM.
5. Press K3 on an ordinary value row to validate and apply the complete draft.

Action rows, including Create group, Four-part smooth, Delete group and Reset map, display a plain >. Delete group and Reset map require confirmation.

Press K2 to discard a dirty draft, or to return from an opened list to its parent. Turn E1 to return to the feature’s first screen and discard an unapplied draft. From the first screen, E1 returns to Channel tasks.

A stopped edit applies immediately. During playback, Merge Shape displays NEXT CYCLE and applies before the next channel-cycle onset. Harmony displays NEXT PATTERN and applies at the next global pattern boundary. Stop activates the latest applied request for the next start.

Merge Shape shows a read-only Strategy summary. Its Strategy selector action discards an unapplied parameter draft and opens the shared selector on Merge modes. Grid (14,8) selects the same Skip, Only, All, Foundation and Fragments choices. A strategy request is immediate; parameter drafts still need K3 Apply. Active is sounding output, while Pending is an accepted request awaiting its displayed boundary.

details.text: Foundation retains anchor velocity. Note, velocity and length merge settings still apply. Explicit masks take precedence. Probability can reject an onset. Source patterns are unchanged.

details.text: While Foundation is Active, Merge modes shows Active FOUNDATION and Foundation decides the channel's trigs. Your saved Skip, Only or All trig merge setting is kept and is not edited. Choose Skip, Only or All on the Strategy selector to restore it. Note, velocity and length merge rows stay editable.
details.title: Saved trig merge while Foundation is active

details.text: Applying a Merge Shape draft, including the Interlock and Structure edits made in the same draft, is one step in the channel's Memory. Open History in Channel tasks and turn E3 back one step to restore the previous configuration.

details.text: Add amount and the Phrase curve decide how many additions play. Add accent decides how loud they are. Lowering Add accent therefore makes additions quieter without removing any; it does not change the Phrase curve.

features.musical_use: Use Foundation to keep one pattern as the spine of a part and vary how many extra notes, and how loud, other patterns add. Use Phrase to build the part up over two to eight loops.
features.prose:
Merge Shape turns several assigned patterns into one channel part. The Anchor pattern’s trigs always play. Trigs from the other assigned patterns are additions: Merge Shape decides how many of them play, how loud, and how close to an anchor. The source patterns are never changed.

Terms used on this page: Anchor is the pattern whose trigs are protected. An addition is a trig from another assigned pattern that Foundation admits. A draft is a set of edits shown on screen but not yet applied; K3 applies it and K2 discards it. Active is the strategy that is sounding, and Pending is a request waiting for its boundary.

[Captured two-cycle Build workflow](#merge-shape/foundation-two-cycle-build)

[Captured Foundation settings and output](#merge-shape/foundation-protected-and-added)

Choose Foundation with the shared Strategy selector on grid (14,8) or Merge modes. Merge Shape shows Strategy as a read-only summary; its Strategy selector action opens Merge modes and discards an unapplied parameter draft. K2 returns with the accepted configuration loaded. Foundation controls trigs only; note, velocity and length merge settings remain active. Choose Skip, Only or All to restore legacy trig merging with retained values. Foundation selects
one assigned pattern as the protected Anchor. Other assigned trig patterns offer
candidate additions at non-anchor steps; overlaps remain one anchor. Amount
admits a deterministic, seed-ranked subset, Accent scales addition velocity, and
Gap suppresses additions within 0–8 circular channel steps of an anchor. Anchor
velocity remains authored. Explicit channel/step masks still win, probability
can still reject an onset, and source patterns are never flattened or changed.

Phrase Cycles can be 1, 2, 4 or 8. Flat, Build, Answer and Fill are stored as
visible per-cycle percentages; changing a percentage makes a Custom curve.
Fixed repeats the same ranked additions. Per phrase changes ranking only after a
complete phrase. Each channel loop advances its own CYCLE counter—even with
polymetric ranges, swing or mute—and Stop restarts at cycle 1.

Keep anchor pitch uses the anchor pattern's relative note on anchor steps before
normal scale conversion. Addition Target can be Legacy, the full effective
scale, selected effective degree indices, or the immutable material of an enabled
Harmony Ensemble group. Targets affect admitted additions only. Note masks,
random shifts and fixed-note operations keep their existing precedence and show
a bypass rather than being quantised twice. Nearest-note ties choose the lower
pitch. A missing/empty target visibly falls back to the legacy pitch.

Foundation ranking is repeatable for the saved seed and grows as a nested set:
raising Amount cannot remove an already selected addition while source, gap,
seed and phrase are unchanged.

Fragments is another shared Strategy choice. Foundation's Interlock and Structure settings remain staged parameter edits: K3 applies the draft, K2 discards it. During playback the shown boundary is NEXT CYCLE, or NEXT PATTERN when applicable. Strategy choices themselves request immediately and do not need K3 Apply.

recipes.text:
Musical purpose: build a part over two loops. Loop 1 plays the anchor line with one extra note. Loop 2 plays the same line with both extra notes.

Starting point: channel 1 has an 8-step loop at 90 BPM with the default Rate /1, so each step is one sixteenth note (one sixth of a second). Pattern 1 holds C D E F on steps 1 to 4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97). Pattern 2 holds a C on steps 5 and 7, and both patterns are assigned to the channel. Strategy is SKIP.

1. Press E1 to open Channel tasks, select Merge Shape with E2 and press K3. The Merge Shape list opens: Strategy, Rhythm, Phrase, Pitch, Result.
2. Select Rhythm with E2 and press K3. The Rhythm list opens with Anchor on the first row.
3. Turn E3 once so Anchor reads 01, then press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Pattern 1 is now the anchor, so its four trigs always play.
4. Press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge modes, select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until it reads FOUNDATION (or press grid (14,8) until it does). Active reads FOUNDATION. The channel grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7: four anchors and two possible additions.
5. Return to Merge Shape. Select Phrase with E2 and press K3. The Phrase list opens: Cycles, Shape, Variation.
6. Select Cycles and turn E3 once right. Cycles reads 2 and two Cycle rows appear.
7. Select Shape and turn E3 once right, from FLAT to BUILD. Cycle 1 reads 50 and Cycle 2 reads 100, so the first loop admits half of the additions and the second loop admits all of them.
8. Press K3 on a value row. The footer reads APPLIED.
9. Press Play (grid (1,8)) and listen to four loops, then press Stop. Loop 1 plays C D E F and one extra C on step 7; loop 2 plays C D E F and extra Cs on steps 5 and 7; then the two loops repeat. The extra notes play at velocity 70, quieter than the anchors.

What each loop plays (an added C is shown as +C):

Loop 1: steps 1 to 4 C D E F, step 5 rest, step 7 +C.

Loop 2: steps 1 to 4 C D E F, step 5 +C, step 7 +C.

Listen for the loop-to-loop change: the extra C on step 5 is present in every second loop only.

To make the additions quieter or louder without changing how many play, change Add accent in Rhythm.

The captured version of this recipe is [Captured two-cycle Build workflow](#merge-shape/foundation-two-cycle-build).

features.musical_use: Use Fragments to build one phrase from sections of several patterns, for example the first half of a sparse pattern and the second half of a busier one, while every section keeps its authored notes, velocities and lengths.
features.prose:
[Captured Fragments seed and playback workflow](#fragments/fragments-seed-source-choice)

Fragments is a separate mode for building a phrase from pieces of the assigned
patterns. Choose Fragments with the shared Strategy selector, then open Rhythm from Merge Shape for Size (4,
8 or 16 steps), Keep anchor, Anchor (shown only with Keep anchor) and Seed. The
channel loop is cut into fragments of Size steps counted from the channel's own
start step; the last fragment is shorter when the loop does not divide evenly,
and a loop shorter than Size is one fragment. Fragments never cross the loop end.

Each fragment plays one assigned pattern, chosen repeatably by the Seed: the
same seed always gives the same choice. The fragment keeps that pattern's own
trigs, notes, velocities and lengths exactly, so the legacy trig, note,
velocity and length merge modes and merged-pentatonic do not apply while
Fragments is active. Merge modes marks its retained note, velocity and length rows inactive, with values such as `AVERAGE SAVED`. These rows and their grid buttons do not edit saved values. Choose Skip, Only or All to restore the retained settings. A note longer than the gap to
the next onset on the loop is shortened to that gap. Keep anchor also plays the
Anchor pattern's trigs where the fragment's own pattern has none; where both have
a trig, the fragment's pattern wins. With no assigned pattern the mode falls back
to legacy merging and Result says `ASSIGN PATTERN`.

Phrase shows only Cycles and Variation in this mode. Fixed repeats the same
fragment sources every phrase; Per phrase draws new ones for each phrase.
Shape percentages, Amount, Accent and Gap do not apply. Fragments hides Pitch; choose the adjacent Harmony task directly for voice leading. Explicit masks still win and probability can still reject an
onset. The channel grid shows exactly the trigs the fragments play.

recipes.text:
Musical purpose: build one phrase from two patterns, taking the first half of the loop from one pattern and the second half from the other. Each half keeps its source notes and velocities.

Starting point: channel 1 has an 8-step loop at 90 BPM and Rate /1. Pattern 1 holds C D E F on steps 1 to 4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97). Pattern 2 holds a C at velocity 100 on steps 3 and 6, and both are assigned to the channel. Strategy is SKIP.

1. Press E1 to open Channel tasks, select Merge modes and press K3. Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 until it reads FRAGMENTS. Active reads FRAGMENTS. A strategy choice applies at once and needs no K3.
2. Press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape and press K3. Select Rhythm with E2 and press K3. The Fragments list opens: Size 8, Keep anchor OFF, Seed 0; edits on this list are drafts until you press K3.
3. Select Size and turn E3 once left. Size reads 4, so the loop is cut into two fragments: steps 1 to 4 and steps 5 to 8.
4. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the channel grid lights only step 3, because Seed 0 gives the first fragment to Pattern 2 and the second to Pattern 1, and Pattern 1 has no trigs in the second half.
5. Press Play (grid (1,8)), listen to two loops and press Stop. Each loop plays a single C (MIDI 60) at velocity 100, and Pattern 1’s E on step 3 is not mixed in.
6. Select Seed with E2 and turn E3 once right. Seed reads 1, and a seed always makes the same choice, so Seed 1 gives the first fragment to Pattern 1 and the second to Pattern 2.
7. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the grid lights steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6.
8. Press Play. Each loop plays C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) and then Pattern 2’s C on step 6 at velocity 100, then press Stop.

Edits stay drafts until K3, so change Size and Seed first and apply once if you prefer. Turn Keep anchor ON to let the anchor pattern fill empty positions. Open Phrase and set Variation to Per phrase if you want new sources each phrase.

The seed is a repeatable dice roll: seed 0 and seed 1 above give opposite choices for the two halves, and every other seed gives its own choice that always repeats. Try a few more seeds and keep the one you like.

The captured version of this recipe is [Captured Fragments seed and playback workflow](#fragments/fragments-seed-source-choice).

features.musical_use: Use Interlock to keep one channel’s extra notes out of another channel’s way, for example hi-hat additions that never land on the kick’s anchors, bass additions that leave room for a lead, or two parts that should not double each other.
features.prose:
[Captured Interlock Leader and Window workflow](#interlock/interlock-leader-window)

Interlock makes one channel's Foundation additions leave room for another
channel's anchors. On the follower's Rhythm screen, Interlock opens Leader (Off
or any other channel) and Window (0–4 of the follower's steps). An addition is
removed when a leader anchor falls within Window steps of it; Window 0 removes
only additions that start exactly with a leader anchor. Anchors of either channel
are never removed, so an addition removed here simply does not play.

Leader anchors are the anchor pattern's trigs in the leader's loop, planned from
the song, not what the leader happened to sound: probability, mute and swing do
not change them, and swing or shuffle never change which additions are removed.
Channels at different clock divisions or loop lengths are compared in musical
time from Start. The leader must itself use Foundation for its anchors to count;
otherwise Status says `LEADER OFF` or `LEADER MISSING` and nothing is removed.

A channel can follow one leader, and a channel that has a leader cannot be one:
Apply refuses a chain with `LEADER HAS LEADER` or `CHANNEL IS A LEADER` and
keeps your draft. Where Mosaic cannot plan the leader exactly—after a clock
division, loop range or song change while playing (`RESYNC`, until the next
Start or song realign) or beyond its planning budget (`PLAN LIMIT`)—the
follower plays all of its admitted additions for that loop and shows why.
Status on the Interlock screen and the Interlock row on Result show `ON` or the
bypass.

Interlock's planning runs when a follower wraps its loop. On a norns each
follower that wraps on the same step adds about 0.7 ms to that step, so a few
followers wrapping together are inaudible, while every channel following one
leader and wrapping together (15 followers) can make that step land about
10 ms late. Stagger follower loop lengths or wraps if you need very many.

recipes.text:
Musical purpose: stop one channel’s extra notes landing on another channel’s anchor, for example hi-hat additions that never double the kick. Interlock changes only the follower’s additions. Anchors on both channels always play.

Starting point: Foundation is on for two channels, both with 8-step loops. Channel 1 (the follower, MIDI channel 1) has anchor Pattern 1 (C D E F on steps 1 to 4) and Pattern 2 (a C on steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (the leader, MIDI channel 2) has anchor Pattern 3, a single trig on step 5; channel 1 has no leader, and its grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.

1. Select channel 1 on the grid (button (1,1)). Press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape with E2 and press K3.
2. Select Rhythm and press K3, then select Interlock (the last row) and press K3. The Interlock list opens: Leader OFF, Window 0, Status.
3. Select Leader and turn E3 once right. Leader reads CH02. A channel cannot follow itself, so CH01 is not offered.
4. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED, Window stays 0 and Status reads ON. Step 5 goes dark on the channel 1 grid: Pattern 2’s addition starts exactly on the leader’s anchor and is removed. Steps 1 to 4 and step 7 stay lit.
5. Press Play (grid (1,8)) and listen to two loops, then press Stop. Channel 1 plays steps 1 to 4 and step 7, and channel 2 plays its anchor on step 5; nothing from channel 1 sounds on step 5.
6. Select Window and turn E3 twice right. Window reads 2.
7. Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Step 7 also goes dark, because it is two steps from the leader’s anchor on step 5, and only steps 1 to 4 remain on channel 1; if you apply while playing, the footer reads NEXT CYCLE and the change starts at the next loop.

Window 0 removes only additions that start with a leader anchor. Each step of Window widens the gap by one follower step, up to 4.

The captured version of this recipe is [Captured Interlock Leader and Window workflow](#interlock/interlock-leader-window).

features.musical_use: Use Structure to land chosen notes of a Foundation line on the tones of a chord while the notes between them keep their own pitch, for example a bass line that touches C, E or G on the strong beats.
features.prose:
[Captured Structure group and marker workflow](#structure/structure-anchor-chord-and-delete)

Structure snaps chosen moments of a Foundation line to a chord while the notes
in between keep their own pitch. Pitch opens Structure: Markers (Off, Anchors,
Every 4 or Every 8) and Chord group, an enabled Harmony Ensemble group. Anchors
marks every anchor onset; Every 4 and Every 8 mark steps 1, 5, 9… or 1, 9… of the
channel loop counted from its start step. A note at a marker is converted to the
scale as usual and then moved to the nearest pitch class of the group's chord,
taking the lower one on a tie. Notes between markers keep their Addition Target
(additions) or their own pitch (anchors); Mosaic makes no claim that they
resolve. Note masks, random shifts and fixed notes still win at a marker.

Apply needs an enabled group while Markers is on. If the group becomes
unavailable during playback the markers play their ordinary pitch and Result
says `CHORD MISSING`. Deleting or disabling the group turns Markers Off for every
channel that uses it in the same change; Delete group lists those channels first.
During playback that change waits for the next pattern boundary, and a Merge
Shape edit applied to one of those channels before then waits with it and shows
`NEXT PATTERN` instead of `NEXT CYCLE`.
A snapped marker keeps its chord tone when Harmony Revoice or Ensemble would move
it: Harmony's Result says `MARKER PRIORITY`. With Harmony Pattern, a mapped note
value that snaps to a different pitch class at a marker than it plays between
markers has no single mapped pitch, so it is silent at both, whichever fallback
is chosen; unmapped values keep their own pitch.

recipes.text:
Musical purpose: land the strong notes of a line on the tones of a chord while the notes between them stay as written. Anchors snaps every anchor note. Every 4 snaps only steps 1 and 5 of an 8-step loop and leaves the rest of the line alone.

Terms: a Harmony group is a stored chord. Its Template count is how many tones the chord has, each Tone row sets that tone's offset from the root, and Group enabled lets other features use it. Structure moves a marked note to the nearest tone of an enabled group's chord.

Starting point: channel 1 has an 8-step loop with Foundation on. Pattern 1 is the anchor (C D E F on steps 1 to 4, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65). Pattern 2 supplies additions (a C on steps 5 and 7). If Foundation is not on yet, follow steps 1 to 4 of Set a two-cycle Build phrase first. Steps 1 to 3 build a group that holds the chord C E G; if you already have an enabled group with that chord, start at step 4.

1. Create the group: press E1 for Channel tasks, select Harmony and press K3. Select Groups with E2 and press K3. Select Create group and press K3. Group 1 appears.

2. Set the chord: select Source and press K3. Select Template count and turn E3 twice right, so the chord has 3 tones. Select Tone 2 and turn E3 twice right. Select Tone 3 and turn E3 four times right. With the root, the offsets 2 and 4 are C E G in C major. Press K3 on a value row. The footer reads APPLIED.

3. Enable the group: press K2 to return to Groups. Select Members and press K3, select Group enabled, turn E3 once right to ON and press K3. The footer reads APPLIED. Group 1 is enabled.

4. Open Structure: press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape and press K3. Select Pitch and press K3, then select Structure and press K3. The Structure list opens with Markers OFF.

5. Select Markers and turn E3 once right. Markers reads ANCHORS and a Chord group row appears showing 1, then press K3. The footer reads APPLIED.

6. Press Play (grid (1,8)) and listen to two loops. The anchors C D E F sound as C C E E (MIDI 60, 60, 64, 64): D is equally near C and E and takes the lower one, and F is nearer E than G. The additions on steps 5 and 7 stay C. Press Stop.

7. Now the contrast. Select Markers and turn E3 once right. Markers reads EVERY 4, so only steps 1 and 5 are markers. Press K3.

8. Press Play. Step 1 and step 5 are C, which is already a chord tone, so nothing moves. D on step 2 and F on step 4 are not markers any more and return to their own pitches. The line plays MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, 60 and 60 in each loop. Then press Stop.

Choosing Anchors snaps every anchor, and Every 4 snaps only the beats you choose. Deleting or disabling the group turns Markers OFF.

The captured version, [Captured Structure group and marker workflow](#structure/structure-anchor-chord-and-delete), covers steps 1 to 6 with Anchors and then deletes the group. Steps 7 and 8 are captured in [Mark every fourth step](#structure/structure-every-4-markers), which starts from the enabled C E G group with Foundation on and shows Markers set to Every 4 and the line playing 60, 62, 64, 65, 60, 60 in each loop.

features.musical_use: Open Result and Reason before changing a pattern or adding a mask to bring back an addition that does not play.
features.prose:
Use Result and Reason when an expected addition is silent. They tell you whether the step is an anchor, an admitted addition or empty, and which rule removed it, so you can fix the setting instead of editing a pattern or adding a mask.

The examples below use a follower channel with Foundation (anchor Pattern 1 on steps 1 to 4, additions from Pattern 2 on steps 5 and 7) that follows channel 2 through Interlock, where channel 2 has an anchor on step 5. See Interlock to set that up.

1. Press E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape with E2 and press K3. Select Result and press K3.
2. Select Step with E2. Turn E3 to the step to inspect. Role and Decision show that step.
3. Select Reason with E2 and press K3. The Merge Reason dashboard opens with six rows. K2 returns to Result.

The six rows of Reason:

- Step: the step you are inspecting.
- Role: what the step is, followed by its source patterns. ANCHOR is a trig from the anchor pattern, ADDITION P2 is an addition taken from Pattern 2, and EMPTY means nothing plays.
- Decision: OK when the step plays, otherwise every rule that excluded it, in order. GAP comes first, then INTERLOCK CH02. When both apply, both are listed, as in GAP, INTERLOCK.
- Interlock: ON while the leader’s anchors are being avoided, OFF when there is no leader, RESYNC or PLAN LIMIT when Interlock cannot plan the leader and is bypassed.
- Velocity: the velocity the step plays, or NONE when it does not play.
- Pitch target: LEGACY unless an Addition Target or Structure marker applies.

A suppressed addition shows Role EMPTY with its source patterns, for example EMPTY P2, and Velocity NONE. EMPTY P2 does not mean Pattern 2 has no trig on that step. Read Decision to see why the candidate was removed.

During a planning bypass, Gap and Amount still decide the step as if Interlock were Off.

A fragment step names its fragment and source, for example FRAGMENT 1 P03 or KEPT ANCHOR. A Structure marker shows MARKER CHORD G01 when its pitch is snapped, CHORD MISSING when the group is unavailable, or a reason such as BYPASS NOTE MASK, BYPASS RANDOM, BYPASS FIXED or BYPASS QUANTISED FIXED.

When a leader is set, Result also shows the Interlock status. A queued edit refused at the loop boundary is shown as Rejected. Silence-aware Interlock, which would keep space free while another channel’s notes sustain, is not available in this release.
