features.musical_use: Give two channels different lengths so a short and a long phrase drift apart and realign. Use it for evolving rhythmic patterns from simple loops, and use song reset options when each section should restart together.
features.prose:
Run two channels at the same clock rate with different lengths: channel 1 loops a four-step phrase and channel 2 loops a three-step phrase. Both channels start together on step 1, drift apart, and meet again after 12 steps, the smallest number that both 4 and 3 divide into. At the default Rate /1 and 90 BPM, 12 steps last two seconds. Playback is continuous: each channel simply starts its own loop again when it reaches the end of its range.

1. On channel 1, assign a pattern with active steps 1–4. Using the default C-major scale, set relative pattern notes 0, 1, 2 and 3, which produce MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Set the velocities to 127, 117, 107 and 97 and each note length to one step. Set the range to steps 1–4 (hold step 1, tap step 4, release step 1).

2. On channel 2, assign the same pattern and set the range to steps 1–3.

3. Open channel 2 Masks. With no step held, set the channel defaults to Note MIDI 79, Vel 40 and Len ½.

4. Hold step 2 and set Note MIDI 81, Vel 60 and Len 1¼. Release the step. Channel 2 now repeats MIDI 79, 81, 79, independent of the four notes on channel 1.

5. Start playback. Both channels begin together. Compare their first steps again after 12 steps (about two seconds).

6. Stop playback before changing the arrangement.

Use separate MIDI routes for the two instruments. For internal sound, assign different supported players, for example Polyperc 1 for channel 1 and Doubledecker for channel 2. Song transitions and reset options can restart channels earlier than 12 steps; the second recipe shows how.

recipes.text:
Starting point: the six steps above are done and playback is stopped. Both channels run at the same rate. At 90 BPM and Rate /1 one step is a sixth of a second, so you can count 12 steps in two seconds.

1. Press Play and count steps. Channel 1 plays MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 and then repeats, so it completes three phrases in 12 steps. Channel 2 plays MIDI 79, 81, 79 and repeats, so it completes four phrases in the same 12 steps.

2. Listen at step 1: MIDI 60 and MIDI 79 sound together. They do not coincide again on steps 2 to 12: for example, on step 4 channel 1 plays MIDI 65 while channel 2 starts a new phrase with MIDI 79.

3. Listen at step 13, two seconds after step 1: MIDI 60 and MIDI 79 sound together again, and the pattern repeats every 12 steps. Press Stop when you have heard the alignment.

4. Optional extra check, unrelated to the alignment: with both channels playing, try a reversed range on channel 1. Hold step 4 as the start, press step 2 as the end and release both. The reversed range is rejected with a message, the ranges stay 1–4 and 1–3, and neither phrase changes timing.
recipes.title: Comparing the Loop Alignment

recipes.text:
Starting point: the two looping channels above (channel 1 range 1–4, channel 2 range 1–3), with Song slot 1 holding them and playback stopped. Song mode is On by default, so the slots play in turn, and Reset on song seq change (PARAMS > MOSAIC) is On by default while Reset on pattern repeat is Off. This comparison hears how the first option changes both channels at a slot boundary.

1. Copy the slot. Open the Song Editor, hold slot 1 at (1,1), tap slot 2 at (2,1) and release slot 1. Slot 2 is now a copy of slot 1, so slots 1 and 2 play one after the other.

2. Set the slot length. Use the global length fader at the lower left of the Song Editor (see Adjusting Song Sequence Length) to set 10 steps. The length belongs to the whole song, so both slots get it. 10 is not a multiple of 4 or of 3, so each channel is part-way through its loop when a slot ends.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and check that Reset on song seq change reads On. Play both slots. At the start of slot 2 both channels restart from step 1: channel 1 plays MIDI 60 and channel 2 plays MIDI 79. The 4-against-3 pattern starts again from the beginning in every slot. Press Stop.

4. Set Reset on song seq change to Off and play both slots again. Now neither channel restarts: at the start of slot 2 channel 1 continues with MIDI 64, the third note of its phrase (10 steps is two phrases and two steps), and channel 2 continues with MIDI 81, the second note of its phrase (10 steps is three phrases and one step). The two channels no longer meet at the slot boundary. Press Stop.

5. Set Reset on song seq change back to On to restore the default.

Use Off when you want the 12-step relationship to carry across slots without a restart; use On when each slot should begin with both loops on their first step.
recipes.title: Comparing Song Boundary Resets

recipes.text:
Starting point: two channels with audible notes. Give each channel a voice (for example Oilcan 1 on channel 1 and Polyperc 1 on channel 2, or any two MIDI outputs) and set Note, Vel and Len on each channel's Masks page as in Make your first loop (a channel needs at least one audible note to be heard).

Enter the two patterns. Tap Pattern (5,8) for the Trig view. In pattern 1 tap steps (1,4), (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4): a drum pattern with trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13. In pattern 2 tap steps (1,4), (3,4) and (4,4): a short figure with trigs on steps 1, 3 and 4.

1. Channel 1: tap (1,1) and assign pattern 1 at (1,2). Hold step 1 (grid (1,4)), tap step 16 ((16,4)), then release step 1. Steps 1-16 on row 4 are now brighter.

2. Channel 2: tap (2,1) and assign pattern 2 at (2,2). Hold step 1, tap step 5 ((5,4)), then release step 1. On this channel only steps 1-5 are brighter.

3. Tap Play at (1,8). The drum channel repeats every 16 steps (four hits per bar) and the figure repeats every 5 steps, so its three notes slide across the drum hits. Listen for the figure landing on a different drum beat each bar.

4. Keep listening until the start of drum bar 6. After 80 steps (five drum bars, sixteen figure passes) both channels start together again. 80 is the first step count that both 16 and 5 divide. Tap Play again to stop.

If the song moves to another song pattern, channels are reset together while Reset at Song Sequence Change (on by default) is enabled, so the 80-step cycle only completes while the same song pattern keeps playing. Use the Options page to change how channels of different length behave. The captured example [Play sixteen steps against five](#loops-that-meet/loops-sixteen-against-five) builds this setup and plays the 80 steps until both channels start together again. The captured example "Keep a valid range when a gesture is reversed" shows the range gesture and what happens when the end comes before the start.
recipes.title: Run two channels at different lengths

review.native_gap: The unchanged native case verifies independent four-/three-step phrases, simultaneous first onsets, exact timing and gates, and a rejected range edit preserving both schedules. The 12-step relationship is the least common multiple of those lengths. Physical sound and the optional song-reset comparison are separately scoped.

features.summary: Use independent channel lengths to create a 12-step repeating relationship.
features.title: Combining Four-Step and Three-Step Loops

learning_path.goal: Learn what a pattern, a channel and a song slot each do, and how this manual names grid buttons and norns controls, before you change anything.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Nothing in the project has changed. You can find a grid button from its (column,row) coordinates, tell the norns keys K1-K3 from the encoders E1-E3, and say what a pattern, a channel and a song slot do.
learning_path.prerequisite: Mosaic is running on norns with a 128 grid connected. Start a new project (PARAMS > MOSAIC > + New) so the course begins from an empty project. Have a MIDI instrument, or a norns voice such as Polyperc 1, ready for chapter 2.
learning_path.recovery: If a tap opens the wrong page, tap Channel (3,8) to return to the channel page. If the grid does not respond, check the grid connection in the norns menu. If playback later makes no sound, open No Sound.

stages.action:
Read these three ideas first. Nothing changes until the last line.
1. A pattern holds a rhythm of trigs (steps that play a note) and relative notes. You write patterns on the Pattern page.
2. A channel plays patterns through one sound: a MIDI instrument or a norns voice. Its masks are values that override pitch, velocity and length, for the whole channel or for single steps.
3. A song slot stores one section of the song. You arrange slots in chapter 9.
Then do one thing: tap Channel (3,8) on the grid to open channel 1.
stages.goal: Know what a pattern, a channel and a song slot are for before you edit any of them.
stages.result: The norns screen reads NOTE MASKS with CH01 in the title row. Its eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4) all show X, which means no value is set: the new channel has no pattern, pitch or sound yet. On the grid, (1,1) is lit because channel 1 is the channel you edit, and (3,8) is lit because you are on the Channel page. In chapter 3 you give channel 1 a pattern and a pitch.
stages.title: Learn the three objects

stages.action:
1. A grid position is written (column,row). Columns count from 1 at the left to 16 at the right; rows count from 1 at the top to 8 at the bottom. (3,8) is column 3 on the bottom row.
2. The bottom-left buttons open the main pages: Play (1,8), Record (2,8), Channel (3,8), Scale (4,8), Pattern (5,8) and Song (6,8). Row 1 selects the channel on the channel page, the pattern on the Pattern page and the song slot on the Song page.
3. On the norns, K1-K3 are the three keys and E1-E3 the three encoders, numbered as printed on the norns. "Tap" means a short press. "Hold K1" means keep K1 down while you act: it is the shift key.
4. Tap Pattern (5,8) on the grid to try a button. Chapter 2 starts by tapping Channel (3,8), so you can leave the Pattern page that way.
stages.goal: Be able to find any button from its coordinates for the rest of the course.
stages.result: The screen changes to PATTERN TRIG with PAT01 CH01 in the title row. No trigs are set yet, so the steps are dim. On the grid, (1,1) is lit because pattern 1 is the pattern you edit, and (5,8) is lit because you are on the Pattern page.
stages.title: Read the grid and norns controls

learning_path.title: 1. Meet Mosaic

learning_path.goal: Send channel 1 to one instrument you can hear, and set a known tempo of 90 BPM.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Channel 1 routes to your instrument or to Polyperc 1; the tempo is 90 BPM; no pattern is assigned yet, so nothing plays.
learning_path.prerequisite: New project, transport stopped, Record off. A MIDI instrument is connected and set to receive on a MIDI channel you know, or Polyperc 1 is enabled for norns. Switch it on and set its volume before you start.
learning_path.recovery: If the Device page does not offer your instrument, check the connection, the MIDI port and the enabled norns voices before changing notes. K2, or E1, cancels a draft without changing the active output.

stages.action:
1. Tap Channel (3,8). Channel 1 is selected (CH01 in the title row).
2. Turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens. This list holds everything you can do with the channel: Masks, Trig params, Output, Clock, Merge modes, Merge Shape, Harmony, Device and History.
3. Turn E2 until Device is highlighted.
4. Press K3 to open it.
stages.goal: Reach the page where a channel is given its sound.
stages.result: The title row reads DEVICE with CH01. Only the Device row is listed, set to None: the MIDI channel and MIDI port rows appear once you choose a device. What you change here is only a draft until you press K3.
stages.title: Open the Device page

stages.action:
1. Turn E3 one detent to choose a Device. The first entry after None is CC Device, a generic MIDI device that suits any MIDI instrument. If your instrument has its own entry, choose that instead. With no external instrument, choose Polyperc 1, the norns voice.
2. The MIDI channel and MIDI port rows now appear. CC Device reads CC1 and OUT 1, so notes leave on port 1, MIDI channel 1. If your instrument listens elsewhere, turn E2 to a row and E3 to the value it needs. A device entry that fixes a value does not let you change it, and Polyperc 1 needs neither row.
3. Press K3 to apply. Until K3 the page only shows a draft and the channel keeps its old routing; K2 cancels the draft.
stages.goal: Make channel 1 play your instrument.
stages.result: The DEVICE page lists Device CC Device, MIDI channel CC1 and MIDI port OUT 1 (or your own choices), and the routing is now active for channel 1. You hear it in chapter 3 when the first notes play. If it stays silent, open No Sound.
stages.title: Choose the output and apply it

stages.action:
1. Tap Song (6,8).
2. Turn E1 right one detent to open Song tasks, turn E2 to Tempo & feel and press K3. GLOBAL FEEL opens.
3. Turn E2 up to Tempo, the top row. Turn E3 left until Tempo reads 90. Tempo follows the norns clock, so it shows whatever your norns is set to (often 120 on a fresh norns; this walkthrough's recording opens at 90). It moves one BPM per detent with no coarse step: keep turning E3 until the screen reads 90.
4. Press K3 to apply.
stages.goal: Fix a known tempo so every timing in later chapters is exact: at 90 BPM a beat is 2/3 s. If you prefer another tempo, keep it and scale the times.
stages.result: The GLOBAL FEEL page for SONG 01 shows Tempo 90. At 90 BPM a beat lasts 2/3 s. A channel's default Rate, /1, makes each step a sixteenth note, so each step lasts 1/6 s; four steps make one beat.
stages.title: Set the tempo to 90 BPM

learning_path.title: 2. Choose one sound

learning_path.goal: Write four trigs, give them a pitch and hear them repeat as a very fast four-note loop.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1-4; channel 1 plays pattern 1 over steps 1-4; its masks are Note 60 (C3), Vel 80 and Len 1/2; no step has its own mask; playback is stopped.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue with the routed project from chapter 2: tempo 90, channel 1 routed to your instrument, transport stopped.
learning_path.recovery: If you hear nothing, check in this order: Play (1,8) was tapped; pattern 1 is lit on row 2 of the channel page; steps 1-4 are lit on row 4; Note, Vel and Len are set in Masks; the Device page from chapter 2 was applied with K3. If Play will not stop because Shift press stop is on (PARAMS > MOSAIC > sequencer options), hold K1 while you tap Play.

stages.action:
1. Tap Pattern (5,8). The screen reads PATTERN TRIG.
2. Tap (1,1) on the top row to choose pattern 1. PAT01 appears in the title row.
3. Tap (1,4), (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4). Row 4 holds steps 1 to 16 of the pattern. Each tap switches one step on; tap a lit step again to remove it.
stages.goal: Write a first rhythm. A trig is a step that will play a note. Four neighbouring trigs are deliberately plain; chapter 4 reshapes them.
stages.result: Four bright buttons light at (1,4) to (4,4), and PATTERN TRIG PAT01 CH01 shows four bright trigs. Nothing sounds yet: the pattern is not assigned to a channel and no pitch is set.
stages.title: Enter four trigs

stages.action:
1. Tap Channel (3,8). Channel 1 is selected on row 1.
2. Tap (1,2), the first pattern slot on row 2. It lights: channel 1 now plays pattern 1. The screen opens MERGE MODES for CH01 because assigning a pattern always shows it; Patterns reads 01. You do not need the other rows yet.
3. Row 4 of the channel page is the range row: it sets which steps the channel loops. Hold (1,4), tap (4,4), then release (1,4). Steps 1 to 4 stay bright and the other steps go dark, so the channel loops four steps. A short loop keeps the first sound easy to hear; chapter 4 widens it.
stages.goal: Connect the pattern to channel 1 and make the channel repeat steps 1 to 4 only.
stages.result: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 and repeats steps 1 to 4. The grid shows (1,2) lit and steps 1 to 4 bright on row 4, and the tooltip reads Channel 1 length changed.
stages.title: Assign pattern 1 and loop four steps

stages.action:
1. Turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens.
2. Turn E2 to Masks and press K3. The title reads NOTE MASKS with CH01.
3. A mask is a value that overrides what the pattern would use. With no step held, E2 chooses a cell and E3 sets that cell for every step of the channel.
stages.goal: Find where a channel's pitch, velocity and length are set.
stages.result: NOTE MASKS CH01 lists eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4). They all read X, which means no mask is set, so the channel has no pitch, velocity or length yet.
stages.title: Open the Masks page

stages.action:
1. With no step held, turn E2 to Note and turn E3 right until Note reads C3 (MIDI 60; norns labels MIDI note 60 as C3). It starts at X, so expect about 60 detents; turn until the screen shows C3.
2. Turn E2 to Vel and turn E3 right until Vel reads 80 (about 80 detents from X).
3. Turn E2 to Len and turn E3 right until Len reads 1/2, a note half a step long (8 detents).
stages.goal: Give all four trigs the same note, loudness and duration with the channel's mask defaults.
stages.result: NOTE MASKS shows Note C3, Vel 80 and Len 1/2. All four trigs use these values: a medium-loud, short note. You do not need to count detents; turn until the screen shows the value.
stages.title: Set pitch, velocity and length

stages.action:
1. Tap Play (1,8).
2. Listen for about two repeats. Four identical notes, C3 at velocity 80, follow each other 1/6 s apart and the pattern restarts every 2/3 s, so you hear a fast stutter rather than a tune. The MIDI strip under the step lists the notes.
3. Tap Play again to stop.
stages.goal: Hear the four trigs repeat.
stages.result: Four equal C notes repeat, then stop with no note left sounding. The strip shows note 60 at velocity 80, about 167 ms apart. The stutter confirms that pattern, channel, masks and output all work. Chapter 4 spreads these four trigs out so each one lands on a beat.
stages.title: Play the loop

learning_path.title: 3. Make four equal notes

learning_path.goal: Turn the four fast trigs into four evenly spaced beats by stretching the loop to 16 steps.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13; channel 1 plays steps 1-16; Rate is /1, the default sixteenth-note rate (1/6 s per step at 90 BPM); Note 60, Vel 80 and Len 1/2 are unchanged; playback is stopped.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 3, stopped. Note 60, Vel 80 and Len 1/2 stay set.
learning_path.recovery: Remove an accidental trig by tapping it again in Pattern Trig. If the loop still repeats after four steps, hold (1,4), tap (16,4) and release (1,4) again on the channel page.

stages.action:
1. If you are not on the channel page, tap Channel (3,8).
2. Set the range, the loop length, on row 4: hold (1,4), tap (16,4) and release (1,4). This is a range gesture, not a trig tap. The range is now steps 1 to 16: one bar of sixteenth notes, 16 x 1/6 s = 2.7 s. Steps 5 to 16 now glow dimly because they are inside the loop.
3. Open the Clock page: turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens, turn E2 to Clock and press K3.
stages.goal: Make the channel play a whole bar before it repeats.
stages.result: The grid shows the 16-step range on row 4 (dim pads inside the loop, bright trigs on steps 1 to 4) and the screen opens CLOCK for CH01. The trigs stay on steps 1 to 4 until the stage after next.
stages.title: Loop all 16 steps

stages.action:
1. Turn E2 up to Rate, the top row, if it is not highlighted.
2. Check that it reads /1, the default rate (one step per sixteenth note). If it shows something else, turn E3 to /1.
3. Press K3 to apply.
stages.goal: Confirm that a step is a sixteenth note, so the timings in this course hold.
stages.result: The CLOCK page shows Rate /1 for CH01, so a step lasts 1/6 s at 90 BPM and the channel plays 16 steps before it repeats. This check changes nothing when the rate is already /1.
stages.title: Check the clock rate

stages.action:
1. Tap Pattern (5,8). The screen reads PATTERN TRIG and pattern 1 is still chosen.
2. Tap (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4) to remove those trigs. Step n is column n of row 4.
3. Tap (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4) to add trigs. Keep (1,4).
stages.goal: Space the four trigs one beat apart.
stages.result: Row 4 shows trigs at (1,4), (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4). Four steps lie between trigs, which is one beat at 90 BPM, so the trigs fall on beats 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the bar.
stages.title: Move the trigs onto the beats

stages.action:
1. Tap Channel (3,8).
2. Turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens, turn E2 to Masks and press K3.
stages.goal: Leave the Masks page open, so the next chapter starts where it needs to.
stages.result: NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note C3, Vel 80 and Len 1/2 as before, and row 4 of the grid shows the four trigs one beat apart inside the 16-step range.
stages.title: Open Masks for chapter 5

stages.action:
1. Tap Play (1,8) and listen for two passes of the 16-step phrase, about 5.3 s.
2. Tap Play again to stop.
stages.goal: Hear the same note spread across a bar.
stages.result: C3 sounds once per beat, 2/3 s apart, over four beats and then repeats; the MIDI strip lists the note-ons about 667 ms apart. Compare it with the stutter of chapter 3: the pitch is the same, only the spacing changed.
stages.title: Hear the wider phrase

learning_path.title: 4. Spread the rhythm across a bar

learning_path.goal: Change only the last note of the phrase, without rewriting the rhythm, by giving step 13 its own mask. Chapter 7 removes the channel Note mask again so the scale can move the pitch; this chapter shows how masks override the pattern and how to undo them.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Same rhythm. Step 13 has Note 62 (D3) and Vel 50; the channel defaults are still Note 60, Vel 80 and Len 1/2; no other step has a mask; stopped.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 4: channel 1 plays pattern 1 on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13, range 16; Note 60, Vel 80 and Len 1/2 are the channel defaults; stopped.
learning_path.recovery: If every note changes, you edited the channel default: release all steps and check that the title row shows ST13 while you edit. To remove a step's masks, hold the step and press K2; this clears Note and Vel together, so set them again.

stages.action:
1. Turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens, turn E2 to Masks and press K3 if you are not already on this page from chapter 4.
2. With no step held, turn E2 to Note.
stages.goal: See the value every step uses before any step has an exception, so you can tell later what an exception changes.
stages.result: NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note C3 (MIDI 60) in the highlighted cell. The title row has no step number, so C3 is the default for the whole channel. A step mask will override it for one step only.
stages.title: Find the channel default

stages.action: Hold (13,4), the fourth trig, and keep holding it for the next stage.
stages.goal: Choose the one step you will change.
stages.result: The title row now reads CH01 ST13: the screen edits step 13 only. Note still reads C3 because step 13 has no exception yet.
stages.title: Select the last beat

stages.action: While you hold (13,4), turn E3 right two detents. Note moves by one semitone per detent, 60 to 61 to 62, and reads D3 (MIDI 62).
stages.goal: Give step 13 a pitch of its own.
stages.result: Only step 13 now has a Note exception, D3. Steps 1, 5 and 9 still use the channel default C3.
stages.title: Raise the last note

stages.action:
Release (13,4).
To check that the exception is still there, hold (13,4) again: the title row shows ST13 and Note reads D3. Release it again.
stages.goal: Leave step 13 and see that its exception is kept.
stages.result: The title row loses ST13 and Note shows the channel default, C3, again. Step 13 still holds D3; you hear it in the next stage.
stages.title: Return to the default view

stages.action:
1. Tap Play (1,8) and listen for two passes, about 5.3 s.
2. Tap Play again to stop.
stages.goal: Hear the exception on the beat it belongs to.
stages.result: You hear C, C, C, D: three beats of C3, then the fourth beat a whole tone higher. The MIDI strip shows notes 60, 60, 60 and 62, all at velocity 80, one beat apart. The rhythm and the other notes are unchanged.
stages.title: Hear the new ending

stages.action:
1. With no step held, turn E2 to Vel. It reads 80, the default.
2. Hold (13,4). The title row shows ST13, and Vel reads 80 because step 13 has no velocity exception yet. Turn E3 left 30 detents until Vel reads 50, then release (13,4).
3. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.goal: Give step 13 its own velocity as well.
stages.result: While you hold step 13 the screen shows its own Vel 50; after you release it shows the channel default Vel 80 again. The last D sounds quieter: the MIDI strip shows velocity 50 for note 62 against 80 for the others. The pitches and the timing do not change.
stages.title: Make the ending softer

stages.action:
1. With no step held, turn E2 to Note. Turn E3 right seven detents to G3 (MIDI 67).
2. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop. You hear G, G, G, D: the three steps without a Note mask follow the new default and step 13 keeps its own D.
stages.goal: See what a step mask protects.
stages.result: The ending note stayed D while the other three moved to G, so a step mask overrides the channel default. The MIDI strip shows 67, 67, 67 and 62 (velocity 50).
stages.title: Change the default, not the exception

stages.action:
1. Turn E3 left seven detents to return Note to C3 (MIDI 60).
2. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.goal: Put the channel default back to C3.
stages.result: With the default back at C3, the phrase is C, C, C, D again, with step 13 still at velocity 50.
stages.title: Restore the default

stages.action:
K2 on a held step clears every mask on that step, Note and Vel together; the channel defaults are not touched.
1. Hold (13,4).
2. Press K2.
3. Release (13,4).
4. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.goal: Learn the undo for step masks, using the ending you just built. The next stage rebuilds it.
stages.result: You hear C, C, C, C, all at velocity 80: step 13 uses the channel defaults again, so K2 removed both the Note and the Vel exception. The screen still shows Note C3 and Vel 80, because K2 left the defaults alone.
stages.title: Clear a step's masks with K2

stages.action:
1. With no step held, turn E2 to Note. Hold (13,4), turn E3 right two detents to D3 and release (13,4).
2. Turn E2 to Vel. Hold (13,4), turn E3 left 30 detents to 50 and release (13,4).
3. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.goal: Put back D3 at velocity 50 for the rest of the course, using the two edits you already know.
stages.result: The phrase is C, C, C, D again with a softer last note (62 at velocity 50 in the MIDI strip). This is the phrase the next chapters build on.
stages.title: Rebuild the ending

learning_path.title: 5. Give the phrase an ending

learning_path.goal: Add a second channel that plays a root-and-fifth bass beneath the phrase.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Channel 1 still plays C, C, C, D. Channel 2 plays pattern 2 (trigs on steps 1 and 9, degrees 0 and 4) over 16 steps at octave -1, with no masks, so it sounds MIDI 48 and 55 at velocity 100 and length 1. If you tried the optional merge detour, channel 1 plays pattern 1 alone again and its merge Strategy is left on All.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 5, stopped. You need a second output: another MIDI port or MIDI channel, or Doubledecker. Do not give Polyperc 1 to both channels.
learning_path.recovery: If the first part changes, select channel 1 and check its Device page and masks: selecting channel 2 does not change channel 1. If channel 2 repeats too fast, set its range to 16 steps again.

stages.action:
1. Tap Pattern (5,8) until the screen reads PATTERN TRIG. Tap (2,1) on the top row to choose pattern 2 (PAT02). It starts empty.
2. Tap (1,4) and (9,4): two trigs, half a bar apart.
3. Tap Pattern (5,8) once more. The screen reads PATTERN NOTE. Here row 7, the bottom row of notes, is degree 0, the root of the scale, and each row above it is one scale step higher. The bright band along row 7 is the degree 0 baseline every step starts on.
4. Tap (1,7) for degree 0 at step 1 and (9,3) for degree 4, the fifth, at step 9.
Pattern notes are relative: the scale decides the real pitch. The title still says CH01 because channel 1 is selected; pattern 2 is not assigned to anything yet.
stages.goal: Write pattern 2: two trigs, one on the root of the scale and one on the fifth.
stages.result: PATTERN NOTE PAT02 shows the tooltip Step 9 note set to 4, with a pad at (9,3); the root stays on the row 7 baseline at step 1. The extra pad at (13,6) is not one of yours and does not play, because pattern 2 has no trig on step 13. In C major your two notes will sound as C and G.
stages.title: Write a root-and-fifth bass pattern

stages.action:
1. Tap Channel (3,8), then tap (2,1) to select channel 2 (CH02).
2. As in chapter 2: turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens, turn E2 to Device and press K3.
stages.goal: Reach the page where channel 2 is given its own sound.
stages.result: The title row reads DEVICE with CH02. Channel 2 has its own Device row: choose an output that differs from channel 1's in the next stage.
stages.title: Open channel 2's Device page

stages.action:
1. Choose a second output that differs from channel 1's. Turn E3 one detent to choose CC Device, turn E2 down to MIDI channel and E3 one detent to CC2, turn E2 down to MIDI port and E3 one detent to OUT 2. Any other port or MIDI channel works for your own instrument, and Doubledecker is another choice. Do not give Polyperc 1 to both channels. Press K3 to apply.
2. Tap (2,2) to assign pattern 2 to channel 2. Row 2 should show only (2,2) lit for CH02; if another pattern slot is lit, tap it to remove it.
3. Set the range so channel 2 loops the same 16 steps as channel 1: hold (1,4), tap (16,4) and release (1,4). This is a range gesture on row 4, not a trig tap.
4. Tap (9,8) to set the channel octave to -1. The octave buttons run from -2 at (8,8) to +2 at (12,8); (10,8) is 0.
stages.goal: Give the bass its own sound, pattern, loop length and register.
stages.result: The screen reads NOTE MASKS CH02 OCT-1 and shows Ch. 2 octave: -1. On the grid, (2,2) is lit on row 2 and (9,8) is lit on the bottom row. Channel 2 now plays pattern 2 an octave down, as MIDI 48 (C2) and 55 (G2) in the default C-major scale, and repeats every 16 steps like channel 1. The output you chose is on its Device page.
stages.title: Route channel 2 and set its octave

stages.action:
1. Tap Play (1,8).
2. Listen for two passes of 16 steps, about 5.3 s. Channel 1 plays C, C, C, D on beats 1 to 4. Channel 2 plays a low C on beat 1 and a low G on beat 3. The MIDI strip lists both channels' notes.
3. Tap Play again to stop.
stages.goal: Hear the bass under the phrase.
stages.result: You hear the phrase above a two-note bass: C on beat 1 and G on beat 3. The strip shows channel 1 on port 1 (60, 60, 60 at velocity 80, 62 at 50) and channel 2 on port 2 (48 and 55 at velocity 100). Each channel keeps its own output, pattern and settings.
stages.title: Hear the two parts

stages.action:
1. Tap Channel (3,8), then (1,1) to select channel 1.
2. Tap (2,2) to assign pattern 2 as well as pattern 1. MERGE MODES shows Patterns 01 02 and the trig merge button (14,8) is on Skip, the default. Skip plays a step only if exactly one assigned pattern has a trig there. Patterns 1 and 2 both have trigs on steps 1 and 9, so those two go silent: on row 4 only steps 5 and 13 stay bright.
3. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop. Channel 1 plays only steps 5 and 13: one C and the D. The bass is unchanged.
stages.goal: Hear why assigning a second pattern to a channel can remove a trig. This detour is optional and you undo it at the end. It edits channel 1 temporarily, so skip it if you would rather not touch the phrase. Merge modes has the full reference.
stages.result: With Skip, channel 1 drops the overlapping steps 1 and 9 and plays only steps 5 and 13 (60 and 62 at velocity 50 in the MIDI strip).
stages.title: Detour: add pattern 2 to channel 1

stages.action: Tap (14,8) once. The button cycles Skip, Only, All.
stages.goal: See the middle merge mode.
stages.result: MERGE MODES shows Strategy ONLY with the tooltip ONLY APPLIED, and the (14,8) button changes brightness. Only plays a step only when more than one assigned pattern has a trig there, so on row 4 just steps 1 and 9 stay bright. This example does not play it.
stages.title: Press the merge button once

stages.action:
1. Tap (14,8) once more: Strategy reads ALL. All plays a step if any assigned pattern has a trig there.
2. Tap Play, listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.goal: Hear that All keeps every trig.
stages.result: All four trigs light on row 4 and return in the sound: C, C, C, D. The pitches and velocities come from channel 1's Note and Vel masks, whichever pattern's trig fires.
stages.title: Merge mode All

stages.action:
1. Tap (2,2) to remove pattern 2 from channel 1.
2. Tap Play, listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
3. Optional: tap (14,8) until Strategy reads SKIP again. With one pattern the mode makes no difference, and chapter 7 works with either.
stages.goal: Take pattern 2 off channel 1 again.
stages.result: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 alone, C, C, C, D, and channel 2 keeps its bass (48 and 55). The merge Strategy stays on All until you tap (14,8) back to Skip.
stages.title: Undo the detour

learning_path.title: 6. Add a second part

learning_path.goal: Move the whole piece from C major to D major by changing the scale, not the notes or the rhythm. A Note mask fixes a pitch whatever the scale says, so this chapter first removes the one you made in chapter 5.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Channel 1's pattern 1 has degrees 0, 0, 0, 1 on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13; its channel Note is X (no mask); step 13 keeps Vel 50; the defaults Vel 80 and Len 1/2 are kept. Channel 2 is unchanged. Scale slot 1, C major, is applied again.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 6, stopped, with the detour undone (channel 1 plays pattern 1 only; its merge Strategy may still read All, which changes nothing with one pattern). Masks override pattern notes, so channel 1's Note mask must be removed before the scale can change its pitch.
learning_path.recovery: If the pitch does not follow the pattern, check that channel 1's Note is X and that step 13 has no Note mask before editing the pattern again. If the scale looks wrong, tap scale slot 1 at (1,3) and press K3 to return to C major.

stages.action:
1. On channel 1, open Masks (E1, E2, K3) if the NOTE MASKS page is not already open.
2. With no step held, turn E2 to Note and turn E3 left until it reads X. X means no mask: steps use the pattern's note through the scale.
3. Hold (13,4) and press K2. K2 clears every mask on the held step, Note and Vel together, so the Note 62 and the Vel 50 both go. Release (13,4).
4. Bring the quiet ending back, because K2 cannot clear the Note alone: turn E2 to Vel, hold (13,4), turn E3 left 30 detents until Vel reads 50 and release (13,4).
stages.goal: Remove the Note masks so the pattern and the scale decide the pitch.
stages.result: NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X and Vel 80, the channel defaults. Step 13's own Vel 50 is not shown until you hold (13,4). No step has a Note mask now, so the next stage writes the melody into the pattern.
stages.title: Let the pattern notes through

stages.action:
1. Tap Pattern (5,8) until the screen reads PATTERN NOTE and tap (1,1) to choose pattern 1. Row 7 is degree 0, the scale root; each row above is the next scale degree.
2. Tap (1,7), (5,7) and (9,7): degree 0 on steps 1, 5 and 9.
3. Tap (13,6): one row up is degree 1, the second scale note (D in C major), on step 13.
4. Tap Channel (3,8), tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.goal: Make pattern 1 carry C, C, C, D as relative notes.
stages.result: You hear C, C, C, D again, now from pattern notes read through the C-major scale: the MIDI strip shows 60, 60, 60, 62. The softer last note still comes from step 13's Vel mask on the channel.
stages.title: Write the melody into the pattern

stages.action:
1. Tap Scale (4,8) to open the scale page.
2. Tap (2,3), scale slot 2. A slot stores one scale; slot 2 holds C major, like slot 1, so nothing changes. Ignore the Degree and Transpose rows: they stay at I and 0 in this chapter.
3. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop. The phrase and bass sound as before: C, C, C, D above C, G.
stages.goal: Prepare a second scale without changing what plays.
stages.result: SCALE SLOT 02 opens with Scale Major. The MIDI strip still shows 60, 60, 60, 62 and 48, 55: still C major.
stages.title: Add a second scale slot

stages.action:
1. Turn E2 to Root and turn E3 right two detents to D.
2. Turn E2 down to Scale and check that it reads Major.
The page shows the change as a draft with Press K3 to confirm. Until K3, playback keeps using the applied scale.
stages.goal: Change the root of slot 2 without applying it yet.
stages.result: SCALE SLOT 02 shows Root D and Scale Major as a draft, with Press K3 to confirm on screen. You still hear C major until you press K3.
stages.title: Draft D major

stages.action:
1. Press K3 to apply D major. The Press K3 to confirm line disappears: that is how you tell applied from draft.
2. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop. Channel 1 now plays D, D, D, E (MIDI 62, 62, 62, 64) and channel 2 plays D and A (MIDI 50 and 57). Rhythm and velocities are unchanged.
stages.goal: Hear the same rhythm transposed.
stages.result: The same rhythm sounds a whole tone higher in D major; the MIDI strip lists 62, 62, 62, 64 and 50, 57.
stages.title: Apply D major

stages.action:
1. Tap (1,3), scale slot 1, and press K3 to apply C major again.
2. Tap Play, listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop: C, C, C, D over C, G.
stages.goal: Restore the arrangement scale so the next chapters match chapter 5.
stages.result: SCALE SLOT 01 shows Root C and the MIDI strip is back on 60, 60, 60, 62 and 48, 55.
stages.title: Return to C major

learning_path.title: 7. Change harmony without changing the rhythm

learning_path.goal: Extend the phrase with a quiet extra note just before the loop restarts.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1, 5, 9, 13 and 15; step 15 is degree 0; velocities are 80 on steps 1, 5 and 9, 50 on step 13 and 35 on step 15; channel 2 is unchanged; stopped.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 7 in C major, stopped.
learning_path.recovery: To go back to the four-beat phrase, tap (15,4) again in Pattern Trig to remove step 15.

stages.action:
1. Tap Pattern (5,8) until the screen reads PATTERN TRIG and tap (1,1) for pattern 1.
2. Tap (15,4) to add a trig on step 15.
3. Tap Pattern (5,8) once to open PATTERN NOTE, then tap (15,7): degree 0, the root.
stages.goal: Place a pickup note between the last beat and the next bar.
stages.result: PATTERN NOTE PAT01 shows the tooltip Step 15 note set to 0 and trig stripes on steps 1, 5, 9, 13 and 15. A C pickup now sounds 1/3 s after beat 4 and 1/3 s before the bar restarts, halfway between the last beat and the next bar.
stages.title: Add a late trig

stages.action:
1. Tap Channel (3,8).
2. Turn E1 right until Channel tasks opens, turn E2 to Masks and press K3.
stages.goal: Reach the Masks page, where a step can get its own velocity.
stages.result: NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X (the pattern notes decide pitch), Vel 80 and Len 1/2: the channel defaults the new trig uses until you give step 15 its own velocity.
stages.title: Open Masks

stages.action:
1. Turn E2 to Vel.
2. Hold (15,4), the step you just added. While a step is held, the screen shows that step's own value. Turn E3 left 45 detents until Vel reads 35 (from 80), then release (15,4).
3. Tap Play (1,8), listen for two passes, then tap Play to stop.
stages.goal: Shape the dynamics: main beats 80, ending 50, pickup 35.
stages.result: You hear three beats of C at velocity 80, the D at 50, and a very quiet C pickup at 35 just before the bar restarts; the MIDI strip lists velocity 35 for the step 15 note. After release the screen shows the channel default Vel 80 again. This version stays deterministic; probability and parameter slides are optional follow-up guides.
stages.title: Make the pickup quiet

learning_path.title: 8. Add a pickup

learning_path.goal: Alternate a bass-only section and the full two-part phrase.
learning_path.outgoing_state: Slot 1 has channel 1 muted and channel 2 audible; slot 2 has both channels audible. Global length is 16 and Repeats is 1 on both slots; Song mode is On; slot 3 is empty; slot 1 is selected; stopped.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 8 on slot 1, stopped. Song slots 2 and 3 are empty.
learning_path.recovery: Stop playback before you edit. Check the title row to see which slot you are editing: it reads SONG 01 or SONG 02. Copying a slot overwrites the target slot, and there is no undo.

stages.action:
1. Tap Song (6,8). Slot 1 at (1,1) is the selected slot.
2. Hold slot 1 at (1,1), tap slot 2 at (2,1), then release slot 1. This copies the whole section (patterns, channel settings, masks and mutes) into slot 2 and overwrites what was there.
3. Tap (2,1) to select slot 2. The title row reads SONG 02.
stages.goal: Make a second section from the complete first section.
stages.result: Slot 2 holds the same phrase, bass and settings as slot 1. The screen reads SLOT SETUP, SONG 02, the tooltip says Song sequence 2 selected, and (2,1) is the bright slot button.
stages.title: Copy slot 1 into slot 2

stages.action:
1. Tap Song (6,8) and tap (1,1) to select slot 1.
2. Tap Channel (3,8). Hold K1, the shift key from chapter 1, tap (1,1), then release K1. K1 plus a channel button mutes that channel in the selected slot only.
stages.goal: Make slot 1 a bass-only section.
stages.result: The title row shows CH01 MUTE and the tooltip says Channel 1 muted. Slot 1 will play the bass alone.
stages.title: Mute channel 1 in slot 1

stages.action: Tap Song (6,8), tap (2,1) to select slot 2, then tap Channel (3,8).
stages.goal: Confirm slot 2 keeps the full phrase.
stages.result: The title reads CH01 S02 with no MUTE: channel 1 is audible in slot 2. Slot 1 plays the bass alone; slot 2 plays the bass, the phrase and the pickup.
stages.title: Check that slot 2 stays full

stages.action:
1. Tap Song (6,8) and tap (1,1) to select slot 1. Playback is stopped.
2. The length fader is row 7, columns 1 to 8. (1,7) subtracts one step and (8,7) adds one. The inner buttons jump to coarse values: (2,7) 1, (3,7) 13, (4,7) 32, (5,7) 38, (6,7) 51 and (7,7) 64. Tap (3,7) to jump to 13.
3. Tap (8,7) three times: 13 + 3 = 16.
stages.goal: Make slot 1 one bar long. Global length is how many steps a section lasts before the song moves on; a slot starts at 64.
stages.result: SONG PLAYBACK, SONG 01 shows Global length 16. Song mode reads AUTO there, which means Song mode is on and advancing.
stages.title: Set slot 1 to one 16-step bar

stages.action: Tap (2,1) for slot 2 and repeat the fader taps: (3,7), then (8,7) three times.
stages.goal: Make slot 2 one bar long too, so the song alternates every 2.7 s.
stages.result: SONG PLAYBACK, SONG 02 shows Global length 16.
stages.title: Set slot 2 to one 16-step bar

stages.action:
1. Turn E1 to Song tasks, turn E2 to Slot setup and press K3. With slot 1 selected, check that Repeats reads 1; with slot 2 selected, check it again.
2. For slot 2, turn E2 to Song mode. It should read On, the default. If it reads Off, turn E3 to On and press K3.
3. Leave slot 3 empty and select slot 1.
stages.goal: Confirm two settings that are already right by default. Skip this stage if you like.
stages.result: Slots 1 and 2 form one chain: each plays 16 steps once. After slot 2 the song wraps to slot 1, because slot 3 is empty. The Slot setup screen shows Repeats 1 and Song mode On for SONG 02.
stages.title: Optional: check Repeats and Song mode

stages.action:
1. Tap Song (6,8) and tap (1,1) to select slot 1.
2. Tap Play (1,8). Listen for four sections of 16 steps, about 10.7 s. The MIDI strip lists the notes: the bass (port 2) in every section and the phrase (port 1) only in the slot 2 sections.
3. Tap Play again to stop.
stages.goal: Hear the two sections alternate.
stages.result: You hear the bass alone, then the bass with the phrase and pickup, then the bass alone, then the bass with the phrase. The screen returns to SLOT SETUP, SONG 01 once you stop.
stages.title: Hear the arrangement

learning_path.title: 9. Arrange two sections

learning_path.goal: Save the arrangement under a name, reload it and play it back.
learning_path.outgoing_state: The saved project Four notes contains both sections and restores their playback exactly. Playback is stopped and no note is held.
learning_path.prerequisite: Continue chapter 9, stopped, with slot 1 selected.
learning_path.recovery: K2 cancels the Load dialog without replacing the current project. Keep the saved name Four notes until you have finished the optional follow-ups.

stages.action:
1. Stop playback. Tap K1 briefly to open the norns system menu.
2. Turn E1 to PARAMS and press K3, open MOSAIC and turn E2 to < Save project.
stages.goal: Reach the save command in the norns menu.
stages.result: The norns menu shows Pattern project management with Save project selected.
stages.title: Open Save project

stages.action:
1. Press K3 on < Save project. The norns text entry screen opens with the suggested name new.
2. Press K3 on DEL to delete the old name, then turn E2 to each character of Four notes and press K3 to enter it. Confirm the name when it is complete.
3. Tap K1 to return to Mosaic.
stages.goal: Store the project under a name so autosave cannot replace it.
stages.result: Saving writes the project files Four notes.ptn and Four notes.pset. Mosaic's own screen does not change; it still shows SLOT SETUP, SONG 01.
stages.title: Save the arrangement

stages.action: Tap Channel (3,8). Hold K1, tap (1,1) and release K1. This unmutes channel 1 in slot 1: a deliberate change you have not saved.
stages.goal: Change something you will not save, so the reload has something to undo.
stages.result: The title row reads CH01 with no MUTE and the tooltip says Channel 1 unmuted.
stages.title: Make an unsaved change

stages.action: With playback stopped, tap K1, open PARAMS, then MOSAIC, and turn E2 to > Load project. K2 cancels the dialog.
stages.goal: Reach the load command.
stages.result: The norns menu shows Load project selected.
stages.title: Open Load project

stages.action:
1. Press K3 on > Load project, turn E2 to Four notes in the file list and press K3.
2. Tap K1 to return to Mosaic and tap Channel (3,8).
stages.goal: See that loading brings back the saved arrangement.
stages.result: Slot 1 is bass alone again: the title row shows CH01 MUTE and the unsaved change is gone.
stages.title: Reload to check the saved version

stages.action:
1. Tap Song (6,8) and tap (1,1) to select slot 1.
2. Tap Play (1,8), listen for four sections (about 10.7 s), then tap Play to stop.
stages.goal: Hear that the loaded project plays the same arrangement.
stages.result: You hear bass alone, bass with the phrase, bass alone, bass with the phrase, as before the save; the MIDI strip lists the same notes as chapter 9. Next you can follow the merge, recording or modulation task guides; keep the saved Four notes project unchanged while you try them.
stages.title: Replay the restored sections

learning_path.title: 10. Save, reload and perform

project.incoming_state: Fresh project. Do not load separate reference-example projects during the course.
project.name: Four notes
project.output: One MIDI instrument or Polyperc1; an independent MIDI channel or Doubledecker for the second part. Polyperc1 is used once.

steps.caption: In a new empty project with playback stopped and Record off, tap Pattern (5,8), then tap the third algorithm button (14,2). The five algorithm buttons on row 2 are, from the left: Drum (12,2), a library of classic bass, snare and hi-hat patterns; Tresillo (13,2), a 3-3-2 grouping; Euclidean (14,2), trigs spread as evenly as a mathematical rule allows; Numeric (15,2), patterns from Noise Engineering's Numeric Repetitor; and Rhythm Doctor (16,2). The Trig Algorithm screen marks Euclidean as SELECTED and the fader on grid row 2 lights its third position.
steps.title: Choose Euclidean

steps.caption: Turn E2 left. The screen passes Tresillo and stops on Drum, the first algorithm (a further turn stays on Drum). Drum shows no SELECTED mark and the third fader position stays lit: turning E2 only browses. Euclidean is still the algorithm in use until you press K3.
steps.title: Browse without applying

steps.caption: Press K3. Drum now reads SELECTED and the fader lights its first position. Drum draws on classic drum patterns, so it suits a kick, snare or hi-hat lane, where Euclidean suits an even pulse.
steps.title: Apply Drum

steps.caption: Tap Prime (16,8). The Paint Preview screen opens on Algorithm Drum with Shift 0, but no step flashes on the pattern grid: at its default settings Drum previews no steps. Prime previews whichever algorithm is selected.
steps.title: Prime with Drum selected

steps.caption: Tap Cancel (14,8). The preview closes and nothing was painted.
steps.title: Cancel the empty preview

steps.caption: Turn E1 to open Pattern tasks, turn E2 to Algorithm and press K3. The Trig Algorithm screen returns (a Painting cancelled tip may still show) and Drum is still SELECTED.
steps.title: Return to the algorithm list

steps.caption: Turn E2 two detents right, past Tresillo. Euclidean is highlighted but carries no SELECTED mark yet, and the fader still shows Drum.
steps.title: Browse back to Euclidean

steps.caption: Press K3. Euclidean reads SELECTED and the fader lights its third position again.
steps.title: Apply Euclidean

steps.caption: Tap Prime (16,8) again. Now every step on the pattern grid flashes and Paint Preview reads 64 trigs: at the default settings Euclidean fills all 64 steps, where Drum previewed none. Prime always previews the algorithm that is selected, so changing the algorithm changes what Prime shows.
steps.title: Prime now previews Euclidean

steps.caption: Tap Cancel (14,8) to close the Euclidean preview and tap Tresillo (13,2), the second algorithm button. Like Drum, Tresillo previews nothing until you choose a pattern: tap drum bank 1 at (12,3), then tap both ends of the first fader on row 2, (2,2) and (10,2), and of the second fader on row 3, (2,3) and (10,3). Tap Prime (16,8). The algorithm fader lights its second position and Paint Preview reads Algorithm Tresillo with 8 trigs. The flashing steps are spaced 9, 9 and 6 steps apart, over and over: the 3-3-2 grouping, scaled up. Nothing is painted yet.
steps.title: Prime Tresillo for a 3-3-2 preview

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Its Device page is open, so the header reads CH01, and Device shows CC Device, Mosaic's built-in generic MIDI device. Channel 2 is not set up yet. Both channels run at the default clock Rate /1 (one step per sixteenth note).
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Device page stays open but now reads CH02 and Device shows None: channel 2 has no output yet, and setting up channel 1 did not change it. The channel buttons choose which channel the screen edits.
steps.title: An unused channel has no output

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1). The header returns to CH01 and Device shows CC Device again: each channel keeps its own device.
steps.title: Return to channel 1

steps.caption: Device was the first of a channel's own settings; Rate is the second. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, turn E2 to Clock and press K3. The Clock page for CH01 shows Rate /1, the default: one step per sixteenth note. Rate divides the clock, so /2 will run half as fast and make each step twice as long.
steps.title: Open the Clock page

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Clock page stays open and now reads CH02, with its own Rate /1.
steps.title: Select channel 2

steps.caption: Turn E3 down two detents to Rate /2 and press K3 to apply. Channel 2 now runs at half the speed of channel 1: each of its steps lasts two sixteenth notes.
steps.title: Give channel 2 a different rate

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1). Its Clock page still reads Rate /1: changing channel 2's rate left channel 1 alone.
steps.title: Channel 1 keeps its rate

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1) again. Its Clock page reads Rate /2. Each channel remembers its own settings, so channels can run at different speeds against one tempo.
steps.title: Channel 2 remembers its rate

steps.caption: Open the Device page for channel 2, give it its own MIDI output, give it pattern 1 with the range steps 1-4 and open its Clock page again. Select channel 1 and press Play. Channel 1 plays one note every sixteenth note; channel 2 plays one note every two sixteenth notes, so its notes are twice as far apart. Look at the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", where the second port's notes arrive at half the pace of the first. Press Play again to stop.
steps.title: Hear channel 2 at half speed

channel-routing-visible-scope.title: Each channel keeps its own device and rate

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8): the Masks page opens for CH01. Turn E1 one detent. From any page, E1 opens Channel tasks, with the page you came from highlighted, here Masks. The nine tasks, top to bottom, are 1 Masks, 2 Trig params, 3 Output, 4 Clock, 5 Merge modes, 6 Merge Shape, 7 Harmony, 8 Device and 9 History.
steps.title: Open tasks

steps.caption: With the list open, E1 and E2 both scroll it, one row per detent. Turn E1 two detents to row 3, Output, then turn E2 four detents: Clock, Merge modes, Merge Shape, and Harmony, row 7, is highlighted.
steps.title: Scroll down to Harmony

steps.caption: Turn E2 four detents back up the list to Output (row 3), then turn E1 four detents the same way. The highlight stops on Masks, row 1, and the list does not wrap.
steps.title: Scroll back up to Masks

steps.caption: Turn E2 one detent down to Trig params (row 2) and press K3. The Trig params screen opens for CH01.
steps.title: Open Trig params

steps.caption: Turn E1 one detent. Channel tasks reopens with Trig params highlighted, the page you came from, so E1 always brings you back to the task list at your current page.
steps.title: Return to the list with E1

steps.caption: Press K3 to open Trig params again. The header reads TRIG PARAMS CH01.
steps.title: Open Trig params again

steps.caption: Turn E1 to reopen Channel tasks, then turn E2 down to row 9. History, the last row, is highlighted and its value reads OPEN >.
steps.title: Scroll to History (row 9)

steps.caption: Press K3. The History screen opens. Every task in the list opens its own screen this way.
steps.title: Open History

steps.caption: Turn E1 to open Channel tasks from History, scroll up to row 4, Clock, and press K3. The Clock screen opens for channel 1.
steps.title: Open Clock (row 4)

steps.caption: Turn E1 to open Channel tasks again, then turn E2 to row 8. Device is highlighted and its value reads OPEN >.
steps.title: Scroll to Device (row 8)

steps.caption: Press K3. The Device screen opens for channel 1, where its output is chosen.
steps.title: Open Device

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Only Chd1 (E, 64) and Chd4 (C, 72) are set, so Chd2 and Chd3 are empty slots; the output is polyphonic. Chord Note Strum is 1/2, Chord Pattern is <- (reverse: slot 4, 3, 2, 1, then the root), Mute Chord Root is assigned and left at X, and Chord Velocity Mod is +10. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Spread; Spread and Chord Accel Mod are not assigned yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Spread and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/4. Each gap is now 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4 step. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Accel Mod.
steps.title: Set a quarter-step Spread

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Accel Mod and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent up to +1: each gap is a quarter step (Spread x 1) longer than the one before. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The gaps are 3/4, 1, 1 1/4 and 1 1/2 steps, so slot 4 (C4, 72) sounds at once, empty slots 3 and 2 pass in silence at 3/4 and 1 3/4 steps, slot 1 (E3, 64) sounds at 3 steps and the root C3 (60) at 4 1/2 steps. Look at the MIDI strip "MIDI sent in this step": the three notes arrive further and further apart.
steps.title: A positive Accel makes each gap longer

chord-acceleration-slowing.title: Slow the strum down with Accel +1

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Only Chd1 (E, 64) and Chd4 (C, 72) are set, so Chd2 and Chd3 are empty slots; the output is polyphonic. Chord Note Strum is 1/2, Chord Pattern is <- (reverse: slot 4, 3, 2, 1, then the root), Mute Chord Root is assigned and left at X, and Chord Velocity Mod is +10. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Spread; Spread and Chord Accel Mod are not assigned yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Spread and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/4. Each gap is now 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4 step. Acceleration works on Spread, so with Spread at zero it would do nothing. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Accel Mod.
steps.title: Set a quarter-step Spread

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Accel Mod and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent down to -1: each gap is a quarter step (Spread x 1) shorter than the one before. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The gaps are 3/4, 1/2 and 1/4 step, and the gap after that would be 0, so scheduling stops. Slot 4 (C4, 72) sounds at once, empty slots 3 and 2 pass in silence at 3/4 and 1 1/4 steps, and slot 1 (E3, 64) sounds 1 1/2 steps after the trigger. The MIDI strip lists only those two notes; the root C3 (60) never sounds.
steps.title: A faster reverse strum can end early

chord-acceleration-termination.title: Stop when the next gap closes

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Note Arpeggio. No slot is assigned yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Arpeggio to the first slot and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/2. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Pattern.
steps.title: Set a half-step Arpeggio

steps.caption: An arpeggio gives every note its own gate: each note lasts one division, here half a step, from its own start. A strummed note is held to the end of the step. Assign Chord Pattern and turn E3 one detent to -> (forward); Assign Mute Chord Root and leave it at X so the root still sounds; then assign Chord Velocity Mod and turn E3 to +10 (E2 moves to the next slot, K2 opens the list, E3 browses, K3 assigns, K2 returns). Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip the five voices start half a step apart: C3 (60), E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69) and C4 (72).
steps.title: Hear a gate on every voice

chord-arpeggio-timed-gates.title: Give every arp voice its own gate

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Pattern. Chord Note Strum is already assigned and set to 1/2, half a step.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Pattern and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent to -> (forward). Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Mute Chord Root.
steps.title: Choose forward order

steps.caption: Assign Mute Chord Root and leave it at X so the root still sounds; then assign Chord Velocity Mod and turn E3 to +10 (E2 moves to the next slot, K2 opens the list, E3 browses, K3 assigns, K2 returns). Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The five slots are the root and Chd1 to Chd4. The MIDI strip lists them in that order, half a step apart, root first: C3 (60), E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69) and C4 (72).
steps.title: Hear the root first

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, with Chd1 to Chd4 set to 64, 67, 69 and 72; the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Note Strum. Nothing is assigned yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Strum to the first slot and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/2: the notes will be half a step apart. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Spread.
steps.title: Set a half-step Strum

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Spread and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/4. Chord Accel Mod is not assigned, so every gap stays the same. Each gap is now 3/4 step (1/2 + 1/4) instead of 1/2. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The MIDI strip lists the root C3 (60) and then E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69), C4 (72), evenly spaced 3/4 step apart.
steps.title: Widen each gap for a slow, harp-like roll

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Note Strum. No slot is assigned yet, so the five notes would sound together.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Note Strum to the first slot and K2 to return, then turn E3 up to 1/2. Turn E2 to the next slot, press K2 and turn E3 to Chord Pattern.
steps.title: Set a half-step Strum

steps.caption: Finish the setup the next examples reuse: assign Chord Pattern and turn E3 one detent to -> (forward); Assign Mute Chord Root and leave it at X so the root still sounds; then assign Chord Velocity Mod and turn E3 to +10 (E2 moves to the next slot, K2 opens the list, E3 browses, K3 assigns, K2 returns). Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip the notes arrive one after another, half a step apart: C3 (60), E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69) and C4 (72). With Strum at X they would all start together.
steps.title: Hear the strummed chord

chord-strum-a-timed-chord.title: Separate a chord into timed voices

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays one trig on step 1: root C (MIDI 60, C3) at velocity 50, held for 4 steps. Chd1 to Chd4 on the Masks page are E, G, A and C (MIDI 64, 67, 69, 72) and the output is polyphonic. Trig params is open on its parameter list, showing Chord Velocity Mod. Chord Note Strum (1/2), Chord Pattern (-> forward) and Mute Chord Root (X, off) are already assigned, so the root and four chord notes strum half a step apart.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Chord Velocity Mod and K2 to return, then turn E3 up ten detents to +10. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip the notes C3 (60), E3 (64), G3 (67), A3 (69) and C4 (72) carry velocities 50, 60, 70, 80 and 90: each note is 10 louder than the one before, so the chord swells upward.
steps.title: Raise each voice by 10

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major. The sequencer is stopped. Channel 1's output is a test device whose parameter Control 1 sends MIDI CC 1 from 0 to 127 and has an Off position shown as X. No value is stored for Control 1 yet. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Choose the test device on channel 1's Device screen. Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, go to MOSAIC, open channel 1's device parameters and turn E2 to Control 1. It reads X: Off, so no CC is sent.
steps.title: Select Control 1

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent right from X. Control 1 reads 0 and sends MIDI CC 1 with value 0.
steps.title: Turn up from X to 0

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent right. Control 1 reads 1 and sends MIDI CC 1 with value 1. Each detent moves the value by one.
steps.title: One more detent

steps.caption: Keep turning E3 right until Control 1 reads 64, passing 63. In the MIDI strip, CC 1 shows 63 and then 64.
steps.title: Turn up to the middle

steps.caption: Keep turning E3 right until Control 1 reads 126, one below the highest value.
steps.title: Turn up to just below the top

steps.caption: Turn E3 right once more: Control 1 reads 127, the highest value, and sends MIDI CC 1 with 127. One more turn leaves it at 127.
steps.title: Turn up to the top and stop

steps.caption: Turn E3 left: the value falls to 64, then 1, then to X, which means Off: no CC is sent. One more turn down stays at X. The last frame shows Control 1 back at X.
steps.title: Turn down to X

steps.caption: Pattern 1 has trigs on steps 1 to 4 and is assigned to channel 1, which loops steps 1 to 4. Channel 1's Masks are Note C3 (60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2, and the tempo is 90 BPM. Playback is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold (1,4), tap (16,4) and release (1,4): the range is now 16 steps, one bar. On row 4, steps 5 to 16 now glow dimly because they are inside the loop (they were dark at range 4), and the trigs are still on steps 1 to 4. Then open the Clock page for the next step: turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Clock and press K3.
steps.title: Loop all 16 steps

steps.caption: Select Rate (the top row of the CLOCK page; turn E2 up if it is not highlighted) and press K3. CLOCK CH01 shows Rate /1, the default sixteenth-note rate: each step lasts 1/6 s at 90 BPM and the 16 steps last 2.7 s. Nothing changes here; this confirms the rate that every timing in the course relies on.
steps.title: Check the rate

steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8), tap (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4) to remove those trigs, then tap (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4) to add trigs. Keep (1,4). PATTERN TRIG PAT01 CH01 shows trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13: four steps apart is one beat at 90 BPM.
steps.title: Move the trigs onto the beats

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note C3, Vel 80 and Len 1/2 as before, and row 4 of the grid shows the four trigs one beat apart inside the 16-step range. Masks stays open so chapter 5 starts on the page it needs.
steps.title: Open Masks for the next chapter

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two 16-step passes run (about 5.3 s), then tap Play to stop. While it plays the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4, one beat at a time over the four trigs. The MIDI strip shows note 60 (C3) at velocity 80 once per beat, about 667 ms (2/3 s) apart: the same note as chapter 3, spread over a bar instead of 167 ms apart. Stop leaves no note sounding.
steps.title: Hear the longer phrase

course-build-a-phrase.title: 4. Spread the rhythm across a bar

steps.caption: The project from chapter 2: channel 1 sends to a MIDI instrument on port 1, MIDI channel 1 (its Device page shows CC Device, MIDI channel CC1, MIDI port OUT 1), and the tempo is 90 BPM (GLOBAL FEEL shows Tempo 90). No pattern has trigs yet, nothing is assigned to a channel and playback is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), then Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 1 at (1,1), then tap (1,4), (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4). Row 4 holds steps 1 to 16, so these are the first four steps. PATTERN TRIG PAT01 CH01 shows four bright trigs at the left of row 4. Four neighbouring trigs are a deliberately plain rhythm to hear first; chapter 4 spreads them out.
steps.title: Enter four trigs

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), then tap (1,2), the first pattern slot on row 2, to give channel 1 pattern 1. Mosaic opens MERGE MODES for CH01 because assigning a pattern always shows it, and the tooltip reads Pattern 1 added to ch. 1. Patterns reads 01; ignore the other rows for now.
steps.title: Assign pattern 1

steps.caption: Row 4 of the channel page is the range row: hold (1,4), tap (4,4) and release (1,4) to loop only steps 1 to 4. Steps 1 to 4 stay bright, the rest go dark, and the tooltip reads Channel 1 length changed.
steps.title: Loop four steps

steps.caption: Turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. NOTE MASKS CH01 lists eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4), all X: no mask is set, so the channel has no pitch, velocity or length yet. With no step held, E2 chooses a cell and E3 sets that cell for every step of the channel.
steps.title: Open Masks

steps.caption: Select Note with E2 and turn E3 right until it reads C3 (it starts at X, so about 60 detents), select Vel and turn E3 right to 80 (about 80 detents), then select Len and turn E3 right to 1/2 (8 detents). NOTE MASKS CH01 now lists Note C3, Vel 80 and Len 1/2, the defaults for every step.
steps.title: Give the trigs a pitch, level and length

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), listen for two repeats of the four-step loop, then tap Play again. While it plays the screen stays on NOTE MASKS, the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows note 60 (C3) at velocity 80 about every 167 ms (1/6 s): four notes per repeat, so you hear a fast stutter rather than a tune. Stop leaves no note sounding. This confirms the whole chain (pattern, channel, masks, output) before you shape the rhythm.
steps.title: Play and stop

steps.caption: You start from a new, empty project: transport stopped, nothing set up, channel 1 selected. Tap Channel (3,8), the third button on the bottom row. The screen opens NOTE MASKS for CH01 with eight cells (Trig, Note, Vel, Len and Chd1 to Chd4) that all read X: no value is set, because a new channel has no pattern, pitch or sound yet. On the grid, (1,1) is lit because channel 1 is the channel you edit, and (3,8) is lit because it is the page you are on.
steps.title: Open channel 1

steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8), the fifth button on the bottom row. The grid and screen switch to the pattern editor: the title row reads PATTERN TRIG with PAT01 CH01, and every step is dim because pattern 1 has no trigs yet. (1,1) is lit because pattern 1 is the pattern you edit, and (5,8) is lit because you are on the Pattern page.
steps.title: Try the Pattern button

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 alone, C, C, C, D, from channel and step masks: Note C3 (60), Vel 80, and on step 13 Note D3 (62) at Vel 50; NOTE MASKS CH01 is open. Channel 2 plays pattern 2 (degrees 0 and 4, octave -1) as MIDI 48 and 55. The merge Strategy is still All, which changes nothing with one pattern. Scale slot 1 is C major and the tempo is 90 BPM.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Note and turn E3 left until it reads X (no mask). NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X: the channel no longer decides the pitch, the pattern notes will.
steps.title: Let the pattern notes through

steps.caption: Hold (13,4) and press K2: the tooltip reads Masks for step 13 cleared, and K2 removes every mask on the step, so its Note 62 and Vel 50 both go. Then select Vel, turn E3 left 30 detents to 50 while still holding: NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Note X and Vel 50, the quiet ending back on step 13 alone. Release (13,4).
steps.title: Restore the quiet ending

steps.caption: Release (13,4). NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X and Vel 80 (the channel defaults); step 13's own Vel 50 only shows while you hold it.
steps.title: Back to the channel defaults

steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 1 at (1,1), tap Pattern (5,8) again for the note view and tap (1,7), (5,7), (9,7) and (13,6): degree 0 on steps 1, 5 and 9, and degree 1, one row up and the next note of the scale, on step 13. PATTERN NOTE PAT01 CH01 shows the tooltip Step 13 note set to 1.
steps.title: Write the melody as degrees

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), play two passes and stop. While it plays the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding 60, 60, 60, 62 from the pattern's own notes, step 13 at velocity 50, and channel 2 sounding 48 and 55.
steps.title: Play it from the pattern

steps.caption: Tap Scale (4,8) to open the scale page, tap scale slot 2 at (2,3), then play two passes and stop. While it plays the screen shows SCALE SLOT 02 with Root C and Scale Major. Slot 2 holds C major like slot 1, so nothing changes: the MIDI strip shows 60, 60, 60, 62 on channel 1 and 48 and 55 on channel 2. Ignore the Degree and Transpose rows on this page; they stay at I and 0.
steps.title: Prepare a second scale

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Root and turn E3 right two detents to D. SCALE SLOT 02 shows Root D, Scale Major and the line Press K3 to confirm. The change is only a draft until K3, so playback would still use C major.
steps.title: Draft D as the root

steps.caption: Turn E2 down to Scale. SCALE SLOT 02 shows Scale Major beside the draft Root D, and Press K3 to confirm is still on screen: nothing is applied yet.
steps.title: Check the Scale row

steps.caption: Press K3 to apply: the Press K3 to confirm line disappears. Play two passes and stop. While it plays SCALE SLOT 02 shows Root D and the Play pad (1,8) is lit. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding 62, 62, 62, 64 (the last at velocity 50) and channel 2 sounding 50 and 57: the same rhythm in D major.
steps.title: Apply D major

steps.caption: Tap scale slot 1 at (1,3), press K3 to apply, then play two passes and stop. SCALE SLOT 01 shows Root C. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 back on 60, 60, 60, 62 and channel 2 on 48 and 55.
steps.title: Return to C major

course-harmony-design.title: 7. Change harmony without changing the rhythm

steps.caption: Slot 1 has channel 1 muted and slot 2 has both channels audible, each 16 steps with Repeats 1 and Song mode On. The project has not been saved under a name yet and playback is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 briefly for the norns menu, turn E1 to PARAMS and press K3, open MOSAIC and turn E2 to < Save project. The norns menu lists Pattern project management with Save project selected.
steps.title: Open Save project

steps.caption: Press K3 on < Save project. The norns text entry screen opens with the suggested name new: press K3 on DEL to delete it, then turn E2 to each character of Four notes and press K3 to enter it, and confirm. Saving writes Four notes.ptn and Four notes.pset. Tap K1 to return to Mosaic, which still shows SLOT SETUP, SONG 01; the text entry itself is on the norns menu, not on this frame.
steps.title: Save the arrangement

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), then hold K1, tap (1,1) and release K1. The title reads CH01 with no MUTE and the tooltip says Channel 1 unmuted: slot 1 now plays the phrase. This change is not saved.
steps.title: Make an unsaved change

steps.caption: Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn E2 to > Load project. The norns menu shows Load project selected; K2 would cancel the dialog.
steps.title: Open Load project

steps.caption: Press K3 on > Load project, turn E2 to Four notes in the file list and press K3, then tap K1 to return to Mosaic and tap Channel (3,8). The title reads CH01 MUTE again: the unsaved change is gone and slot 1 is bass alone.
steps.title: Reload the saved version

steps.caption: Select slot 1, tap Play (1,8) and listen. SLOT SETUP, SONG 01 is on screen and the bass alone (48, 55) sounds, as before the save.
steps.title: Replay slot 1

steps.caption: Keep listening: the screen follows the song to SONG 02 and the phrase and pickup join the bass, as in chapter 9. Let four 16-step sections run, then tap Play to stop. The MIDI strip lists the same notes as the arrangement in chapter 9.
steps.title: Replay slot 2

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1, trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13, over steps 1 to 16 at Rate /1 and 90 BPM. Its channel masks are Note C3 (60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2, and the NOTE MASKS page is open; no step has a mask yet. Playback is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: With no step held, turn E2 to Note. NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note C3 in the highlighted cell. With no step number in the title row, C3 is the default for every step of the channel; no step has a mask of its own yet.
steps.title: Find the channel default

steps.caption: Hold (13,4), the fourth trig, and keep holding it. The title row changes to CH01 ST13: from now the screen edits step 13 only, and its Note still reads C3 because step 13 has no exception yet.
steps.title: Select the last beat

steps.caption: While you hold (13,4), turn E3 right two detents. NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Note D3: a pitch for step 13 only, two semitones above the default.
steps.title: Raise the last note

steps.caption: Release (13,4). The title row returns to CH01 and Note shows the channel default C3 again. Step 13 still keeps D3: hold (13,4) again to see it, or listen in the next step.
steps.title: Release the step

steps.caption: Hold (13,4) again. The title row returns to CH01 ST13 and Note reads D3: step 13 kept its own note when you let go, and holding it is how you see it. Release (13,4) before the next step.
steps.title: Hold the step again

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), listen to two passes, then tap Play to stop. The screen is back on the channel defaults, the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows C, C, C, D: steps 1, 5 and 9 sound note 60 and step 13 sounds note 62, all at velocity 80, one beat apart.
steps.title: Hear the new ending

steps.caption: Select Vel with E2, hold (13,4) and turn E3 left 30 detents. While you hold it, NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Vel 50 and Note D3: both belong to step 13 alone. Keep holding for this frame, then release (13,4).
steps.title: Make the ending softer

steps.caption: After you release (13,4) the screen shows the channel default Vel 80 again. Play two passes and stop. The Play pad (1,8) is lit while it plays. The MIDI strip shows notes 60, 60, 60 at velocity 80 and note 62 at velocity 50.
steps.title: Hear the softer ending

steps.caption: With no step held, select Note with E2 and turn E3 right seven detents to G3 (MIDI 67, seven semitones above C). NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note G3: the default for the whole channel changed.
steps.title: Set the channel default to G3

steps.caption: Hold (13,4) again. NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 still shows Note D3 and Vel 50: step 13 keeps its own values whatever the channel default says. Release (13,4).
steps.title: Check step 13 kept its own note

steps.caption: Play two passes and stop. The Play pad (1,8) is lit while it plays. The MIDI strip shows 67, 67, 67 on steps 1, 5 and 9 and 62 at velocity 50 on step 13: you hear G, G, G, D because step 13 keeps its own note.
steps.title: Hear the new default
