steps.caption: Turn E3 left seven detents to return the default Note to C3 (MIDI 60). Play two passes and stop. The MIDI strip shows 60, 60, 60, 62 again, and step 13 is still at velocity 50.
steps.title: Restore the default

steps.caption: Hold (13,4) and keep holding it. NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Note D3 and Vel 50, the exceptions you built for this step.
steps.title: Hold step 13 before clearing

steps.caption: While you still hold (13,4), press K2. The tooltip reads Masks for step 13 cleared and the screen shows Note C3 and Vel 80, the channel defaults: K2 on a held step removes every mask on that step and leaves the channel defaults alone. Release (13,4).
steps.title: Clear it with K2

steps.caption: Play two passes and stop. The Play pad (1,8) is lit while it plays. The MIDI strip shows 60 at velocity 80 on all four steps.
steps.title: Hear the cleared step

steps.caption: Rebuild the ending with the two edits you already know. Select Note, hold (13,4) and turn E3 right two detents: NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Note D3 while you hold.
steps.title: Rebuild: raise step 13 to D3

steps.caption: Release, select Vel, hold (13,4) and turn E3 left 30 detents: NOTE MASKS CH01 ST13 shows Note D3 and Vel 50 together. Release (13,4).
steps.title: Rebuild: step 13 velocity 50

steps.caption: Play two passes and stop. The Play pad (1,8) is lit while it plays. The MIDI strip shows 60, 60, 60 at velocity 80 and 62 at velocity 50.
steps.title: Hear the rebuilt ending

steps.caption: The project at the end of chapter 7: channel 1 plays degrees 0, 0, 0, 1 from pattern 1 with step 13 at velocity 50, channel 2 plays its bass, and C major is applied. Step 15 has no trig. Playback is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Choose pattern 1, tap (15,4) on Pattern Trig to add a trig on step 15, press Pattern (5,8) once to open the note view and tap (15,7) for degree 0. PATTERN NOTE PAT01 CH01 shows the tooltip Step 15 note set to 0 and a trig stripe on steps 1, 5, 9, 13 and 15.
steps.title: Add the late trig

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Masks and press K3. NOTE MASKS CH01 shows Note X (the pattern notes decide pitch), Vel 80 and Len 1/2: the channel defaults the new trig will use until you give step 15 its own velocity.
steps.title: Open Masks

steps.caption: Select Vel with E2, hold (15,4) and turn E3 left 45 detents until Vel reads 35. While you hold the step, NOTE MASKS CH01 ST15 shows Vel 35, that step's own value. Keep holding for this frame, then release (15,4).
steps.title: Set step 15 to velocity 35

steps.caption: After you release, the screen shows the channel default Vel 80 again. Play two passes and stop. While it plays the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows the phrase (60 at velocity 80, then 62 at 50) and a quiet 60 at velocity 35 on step 15, just before the bar restarts.
steps.title: Hear the quiet pickup

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays C, C, C, D over 16 steps at 90 BPM: step 13 has Note D3 (62) and Vel 50, the other trigs use C3 at 80. Channel 2, pattern 2 and a second MIDI output are still to be set up.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Pattern 2 starts empty. Tap Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 2 at (2,1) and tap (1,4) and (9,4) for two trigs. PATTERN TRIG PAT02 CH01 shows the two trigs as bright squares on steps 1 and 9, and the tooltip reads Pattern 2 selected.
steps.title: Enter two bass trigs

steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8) again to open the note view, then tap (1,7) for degree 0 on step 1 and (9,3) for degree 4 on step 9. PATTERN NOTE PAT02 shows the tooltip Step 9 note set to 4. Only those two note taps are yours: the bright band along row 7 is the note view's degree 0 baseline, and the extra pad at (13,6) is not one of your notes and does not play. It is the note view also showing what channel 1 last played on step 13, D3 (degree 1); pattern 2 has no trig there.
steps.title: Give them notes

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 2 at (2,1), turn E1 right three detents to Channel tasks, turn E2 until Device is highlighted and press K3, as in chapter 2. DEVICE CH02 opens with its own Device row: channel 2 needs its own output, different from channel 1's.
steps.title: Open channel 2's Device page

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent to CC Device, turn E2 down to MIDI channel and E3 one detent to CC2, turn E2 down to MIDI port and E3 one detent to OUT 2, then press K3 to apply. DEVICE CH02 lists Device CC Device, MIDI channel CC2 and MIDI port OUT 2, and the last line reads OK.
steps.title: Apply the second output

steps.caption: Tap (2,2) to give channel 2 pattern 2. MERGE MODES for CH02 shows Patterns 02 and the tooltip reads Pattern 2 added to ch. 2.
steps.title: Assign pattern 2

steps.caption: Set the range, a gesture and not a trig: hold (1,4), tap (16,4) and release (1,4), so channel 2 loops the same 16 steps as channel 1. The tooltip reads Channel 2 length changed.
steps.title: Loop 16 steps

steps.caption: Tap (9,8) for octave -1. The screen reads NOTE MASKS CH02 OCT-1 and the tooltip shows Ch. 2 octave: -1; (2,2) and (9,8) are lit.
steps.title: Drop it an octave

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two passes run, then tap Play to stop. While it plays the screen stays on NOTE MASKS CH02 OCT-1 and the Play pad (1,8) is lit. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 on port 1: notes 60, 60, 60 at velocity 80 and 62 at velocity 50, a beat apart. Channel 2 is on port 2: note 48 on step 1 and note 55 on step 9, both at velocity 100. That is the phrase above a low C and G.
steps.title: Hear the two parts

steps.caption: Optional detour. Select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap pattern slot (2,2) to add pattern 2 next to pattern 1: MERGE MODES shows Patterns 01 02 and Strategy SKIP, the default. Play two passes and stop. Skip plays a step only when exactly one assigned pattern has a trig there, so with both patterns trigging steps 1 and 9, only steps 5 and 13 stay bright on row 4. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding only 60 and 62 at velocity 50; the bass (48, 55) is unchanged.
steps.title: Add pattern 2 to channel 1 (Skip)

steps.caption: Tap (14,8) once. MERGE MODES shows Strategy ONLY with the tooltip ONLY APPLIED, and the (14,8) button changes brightness. The button steps through Skip, Only, All and further strategies. Only plays a step only when more than one assigned pattern has a trig there: on row 4 just steps 1 and 9 stay bright.
steps.title: Press the merge button once

steps.caption: Play two passes and stop, with Strategy still ONLY. While it plays the Play pad (1,8) is lit and a dim playhead cell moves along row 4. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding only note 60 at velocity 80, on steps 1 and 9, two beats apart; the bass (48, 55) is unchanged. These are exactly the steps Skip silenced.
steps.title: Hear Only

steps.caption: Tap (14,8) once more: Strategy reads ALL and all four trigs on row 4 light again. Play two passes and stop. The MIDI strip shows channel 1 sounding 60, 60, 60, 62 (velocity 80, 80, 80, 50): channel 1's Note and Vel masks supply the pitch and velocity, whichever pattern's trig fires.
steps.title: Merge mode All

steps.caption: Tap (2,2) to remove pattern 2 from channel 1, then play two passes and stop. MERGE MODES now shows Patterns 01. Channel 1 plays pattern 1 alone, 60, 60, 60, 62, and channel 2 keeps 48 and 55. Strategy stays on ALL, which makes no difference with one pattern. Another tap of (14,8) would move on to a different strategy this course does not use, so leave it.
steps.title: Remove pattern 2 again

steps.caption: A new, empty project with the transport stopped and nothing assigned to a channel. The pattern editor from chapter 1 is on screen. Channel 1 has no output chosen yet and no tempo has been set; the rest of the course uses MIDI port 1, MIDI channel 1 for channel 1.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), then turn E1 right three detents. The title row reads CHANNEL TASKS with CH01: a list of the pages of channel 1, each marked OPEN >, with the footer Channel Editor. This list is how you reach every channel page (Masks, Trig params, Output, Clock, Merge modes, Merge Shape, Harmony, Device and History).
steps.title: Open Channel tasks

steps.caption: Turn E2 down the list to Device, the eighth task (seven detents below Masks), and press K3. The title row reads DEVICE with CH01. Only the Device row is listed, set to None: the MIDI channel and MIDI port rows appear once you choose a device.
steps.title: Open Device

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent to choose the first entry after None, CC Device (a generic MIDI device). DEVICE CH01 now lists Device CC Device, MIDI channel CC1, MIDI port OUT 1 and Device locks RESET, and the last line reads Press K3 to confirm: this is only a draft, the channel still has no output and K2 would cancel it.
steps.title: Choose CC Device (draft)

steps.caption: Press K3 to apply the draft. The Press K3 to confirm line is replaced by OK, and notes from channel 1 now leave on MIDI port 1, MIDI channel 1. With your own gear, choose its device entry and set its port and channel; with no external gear, choose Polyperc 1 for the norns voice.
steps.title: Choose a device and apply it

steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), turn E1 right one detent to Song tasks, turn E2 to Tempo & feel and press K3, then turn E2 up to Tempo. GLOBAL FEEL for SONG 01 lists Tempo, Swing type and Swing, and Tempo shows the norns clock tempo; in this recording it already reads 90, the value every timing in the chapters ahead assumes. On your norns it may read something else, such as 120.
steps.title: Open Tempo

steps.caption: Tempo moves one BPM per detent between 30 and 300, with no coarse step. To see it work, turn E3 left or right and watch the number follow, then bring it back to 90 and press K3 to apply. GLOBAL FEEL shows Tempo 90, which makes a beat exactly 2/3 s for every timing in the chapters ahead.
steps.title: Set the tempo to 90

steps.caption: Slot 1 holds the whole project, including the pickup on step 15 at velocity 35. Global length is the default 64, Repeats is 1 and Song mode is On; slots 2 and 3 are empty. Playback is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), hold slot 1 at (1,1), tap slot 2 at (2,1), release slot 1 and tap (2,1) again to select slot 2. Holding slot 1 while you tap slot 2 copies the whole section (patterns, channel settings, masks and mutes). The screen reads SLOT SETUP, SONG 02, the tooltip says Song sequence 2 selected, and (2,1) is the bright slot button. The next two steps check the copy: slot 2 stays audible when slot 1 is muted.
steps.title: Copy the complete section

steps.caption: Select slot 1 at (1,1), tap Channel (3,8), then hold K1, tap (1,1) and release K1. K1 is the shift key from chapter 1: K1 plus a channel button mutes that channel in this slot only. The title reads CH01 MUTE and the tooltip says Channel 1 muted: slot 1 will play the bass alone.
steps.title: Mute channel 1 in slot 1

steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), select slot 2 at (2,1) and tap Channel (3,8). The title reads CH01 S02 with no MUTE: channel 1 is audible in slot 2, so slot 2 keeps the full phrase.
steps.title: Check slot 2 stays full

steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), select slot 1 at (1,1), tap (3,7) on the length fader, then tap (8,7) three times. The fader is row 7, columns 1 to 8: (3,7) jumps to 13 steps and each tap of (8,7) adds one, so 13 + 3 = 16. SONG PLAYBACK, SONG 01 shows Global length 16; Song mode reads AUTO there, which means Song mode is on and advancing.
steps.title: Set slot 1 to one bar

steps.caption: Optional check. Open Slot setup from Song tasks (E1 right one detent, E2 to Slot setup, K3), select Repeats, turn E3 left until it reads 1 and press K3. Repeats already starts at 1: SLOT SETUP, SONG 01 shows Repeats 1.
steps.title: Optional: check Repeats for slot 1

steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), select slot 2 at (2,1), tap (3,7), then tap (8,7) three times: 13 + 3 = 16 again. SONG PLAYBACK, SONG 02 shows Global length 16.
steps.title: Set slot 2 to one bar

steps.caption: Optional check. Open Slot setup, select Repeats, turn E3 left until it reads 1 and press K3. SLOT SETUP, SONG 02 shows Repeats 1, the default.
steps.title: Optional: check Repeats for slot 2

steps.caption: Optional check. In Slot setup select Song mode, turn E3 right to On and press K3. SLOT SETUP, SONG 02 shows Song mode On, the default: the song moves from slot 1 to slot 2 and wraps to slot 1 because slot 3 is empty.
steps.title: Optional: check Song mode

steps.caption: Select slot 1, tap Play (1,8) and listen to slot 1 first. SLOT SETUP, SONG 01 stays on screen with Song mode On, the slot button (1,1) is bright, and the MIDI strip shows only the bass (port 2: note 48, then 55, velocity 100) because channel 1 is muted in this slot.
steps.title: Hear slot 1

steps.caption: Keep listening for the second section (about 2.7 s later) and then tap Play to stop; four 16-step sections run in all (about 10.7 s). The screen follows the song to SLOT SETUP, SONG 02 and the bright slot button moves to (2,1). The MIDI strip now shows the phrase on port 1 (60, 60, 60 at velocity 80, 62 at 50 and the pickup 60 at 35) joining the bass, only in the sections that play slot 2.
steps.title: Hear slot 2 join

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major. The sequencer is stopped. The test device has a CC 1 control; no value is stored for it yet. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Choose the test device on channel 1's Device screen. Press K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, go to MOSAIC > channel 1's device parameters, select CC 1 and turn E3 right until it reads 63. This is the stored value: the level CC 1 holds whenever no step overrides it.
steps.title: Store CC 1 at 63

steps.caption: Close the menu. On Channel tasks > Trig params assign CC 1 to a slot with E3 and K3. Its slot is the one you will lock per step.
steps.title: Assign CC 1 to a Trig params slot

steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm the assignment and K2 to go back. Hold step 1 at (1,4) and turn E3 right 36 detents from 63 to 99. Slot 1 shows 99 with an L in its corner while the step is held. The stored value, 63, is not changed. Release the step.
steps.title: Lock step 1 to 99

steps.caption: Press Play, let two loops sound and press Play again to stop. In the MIDI strip, CC 1 = 99 comes just before step 1's note, and CC 1 = 63, the stored value, before the other steps; at the very first note the stored 63 is sent first and then the lock 99.
steps.title: Play two loops

steps.caption: Press K1 and reopen the device parameters: CC 1 still reads 63, because a lock never changes the stored value.
steps.title: The stored value is unchanged

device-stored-value-and-step-lock.title: Keep a stored value while locking a step

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 has a MIDI device on OUT 1 with pattern 1 assigned (range steps 1-64) and playback is stopped. Play a steady loop into the norns audio input, with a short thump on every beat at 120 BPM; the example uses a 29-second loop, so use one at least that long. Press Pattern (5,8) and choose the Rhythm Doctor algorithm at (16,2). Rhythm Doctor opens on the norns: Record READY, Tempo AUTO, Manual BPM 120, Input STEREO. The bank is EMPTY, so no lane buttons are lit yet.
Leave Tempo on AUTO and tap Record at (1,2). Doctor starts listening to the audio input and will estimate the tempo and phrase start itself. The screen reads CAPTURE, MORE AUDIO NEEDED, LISTENING.

Let the take run until the screen reads ENOUGH / REC OR K3 (about 25 seconds of the loop; this is real time, so wait for the readout), then press K3. Doctor stops recording and analyses it: ANALYSING, Lanes BD SD CYM.

Wait while the norns analyses the recording; a short take takes roughly half a minute, and this wait cannot be shortened. When it finishes, the Window screen shows READY with Window bar 1, Window step 1, Sensitivity 0 and Paint policy TOGGLE. Window bar moves the view by 16 steps and Window step by one, Sensitivity is set for the selected lane, and Paint policy (Toggle, Add or Replace) decides how painted hits meet trigs already in the pattern. The lane buttons BD (bass drum), SD (snare) and CYM (cymbal) light at (3,2) to (5,2).

Select the BD lane (bass drum) at (3,2) and tap Paint at (16,8). The grid flashes the detected bass-drum hits on steps 10, 14, 18 and so on every fourth step to step 62, one per beat. The first hit is on step 10, not step 1, because Auto estimates the phrase start from the recording and the first thump comes some way into it; a Manual-tempo take of the same loop shows it on step 11. This is only a preview: nothing is stored yet. The screen reads PAINT, Policy TOGGLE, Destination 1.
Press Paint at (16,8) again to commit. The tooltip reads Pattern painted and the flashing steps become solid trigs in pattern 1, on the same steps as the preview. The captured bank stays unchanged.

Press Channel (3,8), then Play at (1,8). Channel 1 sends MIDI note 60 on each painted step at velocities between 123 and 126, taken from the recording, one hit per beat. The frame shows the Masks screen with the pattern stopped; check the MIDI strip below for the notes sent. Press Play again after about three seconds to stop.

doctor-local-auto-capture-and-paint.title: Record audio in Auto mode and paint detected attacks

steps.caption: Starting point: channel 1 has a MIDI device on OUT 1 with pattern 1 assigned (range steps 1-64) and playback is stopped. Play a steady loop into the norns audio input, with a short thump on every beat at 120 BPM; the example uses a 29-second loop, so use one at least that long. Press Pattern (5,8) and choose the Rhythm Doctor algorithm at (16,2). Rhythm Doctor opens on the norns: Record READY, Tempo AUTO, Manual BPM 120, Input STEREO. The bank is EMPTY, so no lane buttons are lit yet.

Turn E2 to Tempo and E3 to MANUAL, then press K3 to confirm: Manual BPM reads 120, so you tell Doctor the tempo instead of letting it estimate. Tap Record at (1,2). Doctor starts listening to the audio input; the screen reads CAPTURE, MORE AUDIO NEEDED, RECORDING.

Let the take run until the screen reads ENOUGH / REC OR K3 (about 25 seconds of the loop; this is real time, so wait for the readout), then press K3. Doctor stops recording and analyses it: ANALYSING, Lanes BD SD CYM.

Wait while the norns analyses the recording; a short take takes roughly half a minute, and this wait cannot be shortened. When it finishes, the Window screen shows READY with Window bar 1, Window step 1, Sensitivity 0 and Paint policy TOGGLE. Window bar moves the view by 16 steps and Window step by one, Sensitivity is set for the selected lane, and Paint policy (Toggle, Add or Replace) decides how painted hits meet trigs already in the pattern. The lane buttons BD (bass drum), SD (snare) and CYM (cymbal) light at (3,2) to (5,2).

Select the BD lane (bass drum) at (3,2) and tap Paint at (16,8). The grid flashes the detected bass-drum hits on steps 11, 15, 19 and so on every fourth step to step 63, one per beat at 120 BPM. The first hit is on step 11, not step 1, because Manual starts the phrase at the very start of the recording and the first thump comes some way into it. This is only a preview: nothing is stored yet. The screen reads PAINT, Policy TOGGLE, Destination 1.
Press Paint at (16,8) again to commit. The tooltip reads Pattern painted and the flashing steps become solid trigs in pattern 1, on the same steps as the preview. The captured bank stays unchanged.

Press Channel (3,8), then Play at (1,8). Channel 1 sends MIDI note 60 on each painted step at velocities near 123, taken from the recording, one hit per beat; the painted steps are the bass-drum hits. The frame shows the Masks screen with the pattern stopped; check the MIDI strip below for the notes sent. Press Play again after about three seconds to stop.

doctor-local-capture-and-paint.title: Record audio and paint detected attacks

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The channel range is steps 1 to 4, tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and every Mosaic option is at its default. The sequencer is stopped. The Digitakt device configuration is installed next to the test device and Elektron program changes is Off. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: On channel 1's Device screen turn E3 to the Digitakt configuration and press K3. The picker shows Digitakt: this device accepts program changes.
steps.title: Choose the Digitakt device

steps.caption: In the Song editor (grid (6,8)) set Global length to 4 steps, copy slot 1 into slot 2 (hold slot 1, press slot 2) and, with slot 2 selected, raise the channel octave by one (11,8) so slot 2 sounds an octave above slot 1. Return to the Song editor and select slot 1 (1,1): slot 1 is bright and slot 2 is lit.
steps.title: Build a two-slot song

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let it run about a second, tap Play to stop, and tap slot 2 and slot 1. With Elektron program changes at its default Off, the strip below shows notes but no program change at any point.
steps.title: Play with the option Off: nothing is sent

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Elektron program changes and turn E3 right to On. The row shows On. From now on Mosaic sends a program change whenever it selects or moves to a song slot; set your receiver to accept program changes.
steps.title: Enable the option in PARAMS

steps.caption: Close the menu (K2, then K1). While stopped, press song slot 2 at grid (2,1), then slot 1 at (1,1). The strip below lists two program changes, C9 01 and then C9 00 (program values 1 and 0 on MIDI channel 10). The wire values count from 0, so the receiver selects the patterns it labels 2 and 1: receiver pattern number = Mosaic slot number.
steps.title: Select slots while stopped

steps.caption: With slot 1 selected, tap Play (1,8), let the two four-step slots alternate for about three seconds, then tap Play again. Play first sends the program change for the slot about to sound. After that each slot change is announced once, at least half a step (about 83 ms at 90 BPM) before the new slot's first note, so the receiver has time to queue its pattern: compare the program-change times with the note times in the strip.
steps.title: Hear the slot announced early

elektron-child-enable-and-announce.title: Announce song patterns to an Elektron receiver

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 and the sequencer is stopped. Channel 1's Device is the Digitakt configuration and Elektron program changes is On. Song slots 1 and 2 are four steps long and slot 2 plays an octave higher. Program changes are sent on the default channel 10.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Elektron p.change channel and turn E3 left nine detents from the default 10 to 1. The row shows 1.
steps.title: Set the program-change channel to 1

steps.caption: Close the menu (K2, then K1). While stopped, press song slot 2 at grid (2,1). Mosaic sends program change C0 01 (the strip shows it): program value 1 on MIDI channel 1 instead of channel 10. Set this channel to the one your receiver listens on for program changes; the default 10 suits an Elektron device left at its default.
steps.title: The next selection uses channel 1

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major. The sequencer is stopped, Rate is /1 and every Mosaic option is at its default. The norns clock is internal at 90 BPM. A separate MIDI device is connected on port 1 and will send clock at 100 BPM when Mosaic follows it. The PARAMS menu is closed.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu and open the CLOCK group. Source reads internal: Mosaic keeps its own tempo of 90 BPM.
steps.title: Begin with internal clock

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent. Source reads midi. Mosaic now follows incoming MIDI clock, Start and Stop from the connected device and waits for them, so its own tempo no longer sets the speed.
steps.title: Select MIDI clock

steps.caption: You do nothing in this step: the connected device sends clock, a Start, more clock, then a Stop. Mosaic stays silent through the first clock pulses, begins when Start arrives, plays the phrase at the sender's 100 BPM and halts when Stop arrives. The MIDI strip below lists the notes, 0.15 seconds apart, one sixteenth at 100 BPM.
steps.title: The other device sends clock

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent back down to put Source on internal. Mosaic is on its own clock again.
steps.title: Return to internal

steps.caption: Turn E2 to the tempo row. It reads 100 BPM: while Source was midi the incoming clock set the tempo, and switching Source back does not restore your own. Turn E3 ten detents down to bring it back to 90 BPM, the tempo the project used before.
steps.title: Bring the tempo back to 90 BPM

steps.caption: Close the menu and press Play. The notes are again one sixth of a second apart, the pace of 90 BPM, as the MIDI strip shows.
steps.title: Play on the internal clock

steps.caption: Starting point: a new, empty project, stopped, with Record off. No channel has an output, no pattern has trigs and no masks are set. Tap Channel (3,8): the header reads CH01. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, choose Device with E2 and press K3. Turn E3 one detent to the first output in the list and press K3 to apply it. Whichever name the row shows is fine for this walk-through; in your own project pick the note-capable output you set up in Connect a sound. The Device page for CH01 stays on screen.
Tap Pattern (5,8) for the Trig view of pattern 1, then tap steps (1,4), (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4). Four steps light on row 4. Each lit step is a trig, a moment where a note will sound.

Tap Channel (3,8), then tap pattern slot (1,2) to feed pattern 1 to channel 1. Next limit the channel to four steps: hold step 1 at (1,4), tap step 4 at (4,4), then release step 1. Hold the first step of the range, tap the last, then let go. The channel now loops steps 1 to 4, and those four steps are brighter than the rest of row 4.

Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, scroll up to Masks with E2 and press K3. Select Note with E2, then turn E3 right until the screen reads C3, which is MIDI 60. The Note row shows the name, so stop on the readout instead of counting. With no step held this sets the channel note for all steps.
Turn E2 one detent to select Vel, then turn E3 right until the screen reads 80. Every step now plays at velocity 80, a medium-loud level.

Turn E2 one detent to select Len, then turn E3 until the screen reads 1/2, so each note lasts half a step. Tap Play (1,8) to hear four equal C notes (MIDI 60, velocity 80) repeating as the playhead runs along steps 1 to 4; the frame shows the Masks screen, so listen to your output or check the MIDI strip below. Tap Play again to stop.

first-sound-equal-note-loop.title: Create a four-step loop from an empty project

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device on OUT 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major at 90 BPM, with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). All Trig params slots are empty, and the Device page is showing.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Fixed Note makes the channel send one chosen MIDI note while the pattern still decides when. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Trig params with E2 and press K3. Press K2 to open the parameter list and turn E3 until it shows Fixed Note.
steps.title: Find Fixed Note

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Fixed Note to the first slot and K2 to return. Slot 1 reads X, which means Off, so the parameter is assigned but sends nothing yet.
steps.title: Assign Fixed Note to a slot

steps.caption: With no step held, turn E3 to 60 (C3). Slot 1 reads C5, this slot's name for MIDI note 60 (it numbers octaves two higher than the C3 used elsewhere in this manual). This is the channel's default pitch, the note every step plays unless it has its own lock.
steps.title: Set the channel pitch

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop. The MIDI strip lists four C3 (60) note-ons at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The pitch is fixed and the velocities are not.
steps.title: Play the default

steps.caption: Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 to 63 (D#3) and release. A value set on a held step is a lock, and it belongs to step 2 alone. Play, then stop: the strip reads 60, 63, 60, 60 (C3, D#3, C3, C3).
steps.title: Give step 2 another pitch

steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 down to 0 and release. 0 is a real pitch, the lowest MIDI note (C-2), not Off. Play, then stop: the strip reads 0, 63, 60, 60.
steps.title: Zero is a note

steps.caption: Hold step 4 at (4,4), turn E3 down to X (Off) and release. X on a step means no lock, and step 4 had none, so a Play and Stop still gives 0, 63, 60, 60. Then, with no step held, turn E3 up five detents to raise the channel pitch to 65 (F3), and Play and Stop again: steps 3 and 4 follow the new default and steps 1 and 2 keep their locks, 0, 63, 65, 65.
steps.title: X is no lock; raise the default beneath the locks

steps.caption: Hold step 2, press K2 and release: its lock is gone, so Play and Stop gives 0, 65, 65, 65. Then, with no step held, turn E3 down to X (Off), and Play and Stop again: steps 2, 3 and 4 return to the written phrase, 62, 64, 65, while step 1 still plays its own lock, 0.
steps.title: Clear a lock, then turn the channel pitch off

steps.caption: Hold step 1, press K2 and release. With no lock and no channel pitch left, Play and Stop gives the original C, D, E, F phrase again: 60, 62, 64, 65.
steps.title: Clear the last lock

fixed-note-default-and-locks.title: A pitch default with local exceptions

steps.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps on the test device with Merge Shape set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, velocities 127, 117, 107, 97, on steps 1 to 4) is saved as the protected Anchor: its steps always play as written. Pattern 2 (a C at velocity 100 on steps 5 and 7) offers additions. Add amount is how many additions are admitted and Add accent scales their velocity. The norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Add amount, which reads 100: every candidate addition is admitted. Turn E2 two detents on to Add accent, which reads 70 and scales the velocity of the added trigs to 70 percent. Both settings are already at these values; you only read them here. The grid shows the anchors on steps 1 to 4 and the additions on steps 5 and 7.
steps.title: Read Add amount and Add accent

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two eight-step loops sound, then tap Stop. Each loop plays the four anchors, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97, then two additions as MIDI 60 at velocity 70, shown in the strip below. Anchor velocities are untouched; only the added notes use Add accent.
steps.title: Hear anchors and additions

steps.caption: Turn E3 left 30 detents. Add accent reads 40; press K3 to apply it, as the sequencer is stopped.
steps.title: Lower Add accent to 40

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops sound, then tap Stop. The four anchors are exactly as before, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97, but the two additions are now MIDI 60 at velocity 40 in the strip below, quieter than the 70 you heard before.
steps.title: Hear quieter additions

foundation-protected-and-added.title: Keep anchors and accent the additions

steps.caption: Channel 1 loops 8 steps on the test device with Merge Shape set to Foundation. Pattern 1 (C, D, E, F, MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65, on steps 1 to 4) is the protected Anchor and pattern 2 (trigs on steps 5 and 7) offers additions; both are assigned. Add amount is 100 and Add accent 70, so all candidate additions are allowed and sound at 70 percent of their velocity. The Phrase settings are still at their defaults, the norns shows the Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press E1 once to the Phrase screen, turn E2 to Phrase and press K3. A cycle is one pass of the eight-step loop. Turn E3 once to set Cycles to 2.
steps.title: Set Cycles to 2

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Shape and E3 once to choose BUILD, which reads Cycle 1 50 and Cycle 2 100.
steps.title: Choose the Build shape

steps.caption: Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED.
steps.title: Apply the phrase

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen. The first loop plays steps 1 to 4 plus one addition (step 7), five notes in the strip below.
steps.title: Loop 1 adds one note

steps.caption: The second loop plays steps 1 to 4 plus both additions (steps 5 and 7), six notes. Keep listening to at least four loops, then tap Stop.
steps.title: Loop 2 adds both

steps.caption: The two loops keep alternating: the strip below shows the notes of each pass, loop 1 with step 7 added and loop 2 with steps 5 and 7 added, back to the first anchor at the end.
steps.title: Build over two channel loops

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays through the test device on an 8-step loop at 90 BPM, rate /1. Pattern 1 holds C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 and pattern 2 holds a C at velocity 100 on steps 3 and 6. Both patterns are assigned to channel 1 and Strategy is still SKIP. Merge modes is open for channel 1. In this scene a Seed makes a repeatable draw of which pattern each fragment comes from: the same seed always gives the same choice.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Select Strategy and turn E3 to FRAGMENTS. Strategy and Active both read FRAGMENTS: the loop will be cut into fragments and each fragment will come from one source pattern, chosen by the Seed.
steps.title: Choose Fragments

steps.caption: Open Merge Shape > Rhythm. Turn E3 once left so Size reads 4 and press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the eight-step loop is now cut into two four-step fragments, one for steps 1 to 4 and one for steps 5 to 8. On the grid only step 3 is bright: with the starting seed the first fragment comes from pattern 2 (a note on step 3 only) and the second from pattern 1, which has no notes in steps 5 to 8.
steps.title: Set Size to 4

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops sound, then tap Stop. Each loop plays one C (MIDI 60) at velocity 100, a single note in the strip below. Seed 0 gives steps 1 to 4 to pattern 2 and steps 5 to 8 to pattern 1, which has no trigs there, and pattern 1's own E on step 3 is not mixed in.
steps.title: Seed 0 picks the sparse draw

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Seed and turn E3 once right so it reads 1. The grid still shows the result of seed 0 until you apply the change.
steps.title: Pick seed 1

steps.caption: Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED and the grid now lights steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6. Seed 1 gives steps 1 to 4 to pattern 1 and steps 5 to 8 to pattern 2. Try other seeds, 2, 3 and so on, and listen for how each draw reshuffles the fragments.
steps.title: Apply seed 1

steps.caption: Tap Play, let two loops sound, then tap Stop. Each loop plays pattern 1's C D E F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) and then pattern 2's C on step 6 at velocity 100. Each fragment keeps the notes and velocities of the pattern it came from.
steps.title: Each fragment keeps its source

fragments-seed-source-choice.title: Let each fragment keep its source notes

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1. Quantise Note Mask works on three levels, strongest first: a step lock, then the channel value, then the global option. On follows the scale, Off keeps the written pitch, and X means inherit from the next level down. The state is listed as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: Off / X / Off / On. The global Off is inherited by the channel, step 1 is Off and step 2 is On, so the strip reads 60, 65, 69, 71.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: State: Off / On / Off / On. With no step held, turn E3 two detents up to On. Play, then stop: the channel On beats the global Off, so steps 3 and 4 follow the scale again, 60, 65, 71, 60.
steps.title: Channel: On beats the global Off

steps.caption: First hold step 1, press K2 and release: the Off lock clears and the channel On applies. Play, then stop: 62, 65, 71, 60 (state Off / On / X / On). Then hold step 1, turn E3 all the way down to X and release. An explicit step X skips the channel and uses the global option directly, here Off, so step 1 plays its written note: 60, 65, 71, 60.
steps.title: Step: clear an Off, then try an explicit X

full-quantisation-channel-beats-global.title: Let the channel beat the global setting

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1. Quantise Note Mask works on three levels, strongest first: a step lock, then the channel value, then the global option. On follows the scale, Off keeps the written pitch, and X means inherit from the next level down. The state is listed as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: On / Off / X / On. The channel Off beats the global On and step 2 has its own On lock, so the strip reads 60, 65, 69, 71.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: State: On / X / X / On. With no step held, turn the channel value down to X (unset). The global On applies again: 62, 65, 71, 60. Step 2 keeps its own On lock.
steps.title: Channel: X inherits the global On

steps.caption: State: On / X / Off / On. Hold step 1, turn E3 one detent up from X to Off and release. Play, then stop: step 1 plays its written note, 60, even though the global option is On. The strip reads 60, 65, 71, 60.
steps.title: Step: switch one step Off

steps.caption: State: Off / X / Off / On. Press K1, open the Mosaic params and turn Quantise note masks Off. The channel value is still X, so it follows the global Off. Play, then stop: steps 3 and 4 play as written and step 2 keeps its On lock, 60, 65, 69, 71.
steps.title: Global: turn full quantisation Off

full-quantisation-inherit-and-step-off.title: Let the channel inherit the global setting

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays four trigs with note masks 60, 64, 69 and 71 on steps 1-4 (velocities 127, 117, 107, 97), in a scale with Degree II and Rotation 1; both are already set in the scale editor. In PARAMS > MOSAIC, Snap note masks to scale is On, while Quantise note masks (the global full-quantisation option) and Lock merged to pent. are Off. With Snap alone the masks play as written, 60, 64, 69, 71 in the MIDI strip, because Degree and Rotation affect masks only under full quantisation. Quantise Note Mask works on three levels, strongest first: a step lock, then the channel value, then the global option. On follows the scale, Off keeps the written pitch, and X means inherit from the next level down. Each step below lists the state as global / channel / step 1 / step 2. Now: Off / X / X / X.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: State: On / X / X / X. Press K1, open the Mosaic params and turn Quantise note masks On (the global option). Play, then stop: the same masks now follow Degree II and Rotation 1 and the strip reads 62, 65, 71, 60.
steps.title: Global: turn full quantisation On

steps.caption: State: On / Off / X / X. Open Channel tasks > Trig params, press K2 and turn E3 to Quantise Note Mask in the parameter list. Press K3 to assign it and K2 to return, then turn E3 one detent to Off. Play, then stop: the written phrase 60, 64, 69, 71 returns, because the channel setting beats the global On.
steps.title: Channel: an Off beats the global On

steps.caption: State: On / Off / X / On. Hold step 2 and turn E3 to On to lock that step, then release. Play, then stop: only step 2 changes, to 65. The strip reads 60, 65, 69, 71.
steps.title: Step: map just one step

full-quantisation-precedence.title: Choose which note masks follow the scale

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a device with MIDI CCs, at 90 BPM with Rate /1, so one step lasts a sixth of a second. PARAMS is open on the device's CC 1 control at its stored value, 63, set in PARAMS > MOSAIC. CC 1 is not assigned to a Trig params slot yet, and parameter slides are off.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K1 to leave PARAMS. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Trig params with E2 and press K3, then press K2 and turn E3 to CC 1 in the parameter list.
steps.title: Find CC 1

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign CC 1 and K2 to return. Slot 1 now reads 63, the stored value, with no marker in its corner, because no step has a lock for it yet.
steps.title: Assign CC 1 to the slot

steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4) and turn E3 to 24. Slot 1 shows 24 with an L in its corner while the step is held, so this step now has its own value for CC 1. Release the step.
steps.title: Lock step 1 to 24

steps.caption: Hold step 3 at (3,4) and turn E3 to 96. Slot 1 shows 96 with the L. Release the step. Steps 1 and 3 now carry different CC 1 values, two steps apart.
steps.title: Lock step 3 to 96

steps.caption: With no step held, press K3. Slot 1 reads 63 again and gains an S in its corner, so every lock of CC 1 slides toward the next one.
steps.title: Turn slides on for the parameter

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops play, then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip, CC 1 starts at 24 on step 1 and climbs in equal steps of 12, about every 56 ms: 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, reaching 96 as step 3's note starts. The glide fills the two steps between the locks.
steps.title: Play and watch the glide

steps.caption: Press K1 to open PARAMS. CC 1 still shows its stored value, 63: playback never changes the setting you stored, so the glide exists only in the CC messages that were sent.
steps.title: The device setting does not change

steps.caption: Four channels play through the test device, each on its own MIDI channel (1 to 4) with its own sparse rhythm: channel 1 plays the four-step phrase, channel 2 steps 1 and 3, channel 3 steps 2 and 4 and channel 4 step 4. Scale slot 1 (C major) is applied, Harmony is Off on every channel and no scale or octave locks are set, so each channel plays its own written pitches. A Harmony Ensemble group lets several channels share one chord: each member gets a role (Bass, Inner or Top), keeps its own rhythm, and takes its pitch from the group's shared voicing. The norns shows the Device page of channel 4.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: On channel 1 open Channel tasks > Harmony, go to Groups, create group 1 with the Four-part smooth preset and open Members. The header reads MEMBERS CH01: this is where you choose which channels belong to the group.
steps.title: Create group 1 and open Members

steps.caption: Assign channels 1 to 4 as the members, in order, with E2 and E3, and press K3 to save: the group is complete but still off. Press E1 back to the Harmony list, set Mode to ENSEMBLE with E3, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 1. Then select channel 2 (2,1): its Voice leading page opens.
steps.title: Assign the members, join channel 1

steps.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 2. Then select channel 3 (3,1): its Voice leading page opens.
steps.title: Join channel 2

steps.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 3. Then select channel 4 (4,1): its Voice leading page opens.
steps.title: Join channel 3

steps.caption: Set Mode to ENSEMBLE, choose group 1 and press K3 to join channel 4. Then turn E2 to Ensemble and press K3. The header reads ENSEMBLE CH04.
steps.title: Join channel 4 and open Ensemble

steps.caption: On channel 4's Ensemble page select Group enabled and turn E3 to ON. Until now the group existed but did nothing.
steps.title: Switch the group on

steps.caption: Press K3 to apply, then tap Play. Channels 1 to 4 take the roles Bass, Inner, Inner and Top. Each channel keeps its own rhythm and velocities, but all four take their pitch from one shared chord voicing: listen for a single chord spread across the four channels, MIDI 48, 55, 64 and 67 in the strip below. Tap Play to stop.
steps.title: Four roles, four rhythms, one chord

steps.caption: Tap Scale (4,8) and set scale slot 3 to root E. Return to Channel (3,8), select channel 2, hold step 1 (1,4) and press slot 3 at (3,3) to lock that channel to E major. Tap Play and Stop, then open Harmony > Result for channel 2. The header reads VOICE MOVEMENT CH02.
steps.title: Lock channel 2 to E major

steps.caption: A scale lock on a member conflicts with the shared voicing, so channel 2 steps out of the Ensemble and plays its ordinary pitches: all five of its notes play MIDI 64 instead of 55, and Result reads LOCAL SCALE BYPASS.
steps.title: A scale lock bypasses the group

steps.caption: Select channel 3 (3,1) and press octave +1 at (11,8), then tap Play and Stop. Open Harmony: the Voice leading header for channel 3 reads OCT+1.
steps.title: Give channel 3 its own octave

steps.caption: Select Result in Voice leading and press K3: the Voice movement page for CH03 OCT+1 opens.
steps.title: Open Result for channel 3

steps.caption: A channel octave also leaves the shared voicing, so all six of channel 3's notes play MIDI 72 in the strip. In Result select Step with E2 and turn E3 to step 2. Result reads LOCAL OCTAVE BYPASS.
steps.title: An octave override bypasses too

harmony-ensemble-and-local-bypass.title: Share a voicing while keeping each channel’s rhythm

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on MIDI channel 1: C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 at 90 BPM, rate /1. Harmony is Off with its default registers and Failure fallback SILENCE. Playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page. This scene shows what happens when a register leaves no room for a note, as it can after you shift a voice into an unusual range.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony. Its list holds Mode, Register, Tone Map, Result and the Entry / Failure row used later. Turn E3 to set Mode to PATTERN, select Register with E2 and press K3.
steps.title: Open the Bass register

steps.caption: On the Bass rows turn E2 to Low and E3 to set it to 50. The Low row reads 50.
steps.title: Raise Bass Low to 50

steps.caption: Turn E2 to High and E3 to set it to 50. The High row reads 50, so the register is now the single note 50.
steps.title: Lower Bass High to 50

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Centre and E3 to set it to 50. MIDI 50 is a D, so this register holds no C at all. The Centre row reads 50.
steps.title: Centre the Bass register on 50

steps.caption: Press K3, then E1 back to the Harmony list, select Tone Map with E2 and press K3. Turn E3 so Tone 0, the written C, goes to Bass, and press K3.
steps.title: Send the written C to Bass

steps.caption: Tap Play for two loops, then Stop. Step 1 is silent while D, E and F sound (MIDI 62, 64, 65 in the strip below), because Bass has no C to play.
steps.title: Hear the silent step

steps.caption: Press E1 to go back to the Harmony list, select Result with E2 and press K3.
steps.title: Open Result

steps.caption: Read Result for step 1. Status reads NO VOICING RANGE and CH1 reads NO EVENT, because nothing was sent; a Failure details row appears and K3 opens it.
steps.title: Read the failure

steps.caption: Optional check first: turn E3 to step 5; Status and CH1 read NO EVENT there because the loop has no trig on step 5, which differs from step 1, where an event existed but could not be voiced. Turn Step back to 1, press K2 to return to the list, select Entry and press K3. The Entry / Failure page lists Failure fallback.
steps.title: Find Entry / Failure

steps.caption: Select Failure fallback and turn E3 once right: it reads LEGACY. Press K3 to apply.
steps.title: Choose Legacy

steps.caption: Tap Play for two loops, then Stop. C D E F return (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65): step 1 now plays through its original C instead of falling silent.
steps.title: Hear the fallback

steps.caption: Reopen Result: step 1 now reads Status LEGACY RANGE and CH1 C3 > C3 (planned > sent), the sign that the written pitch was used on purpose.
steps.title: Confirm Legacy in Result

harmony-range-failure-and-fallback.title: See a failed voicing and choose a fallback

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step phrase on steps 1 to 4 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through the test device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (rate /1). Each step is a single voice: no chord notes are set and Harmony is Off. Playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Open Masks for channel 1 and turn E3 one detent on Chd1, the first chord note. Chd1 reads 2nd: each step now sounds a second voice one scale step above its note, so the pairs are C+D, D+E, E+F and F+G (60+62, 62+64, 64+65, 65+67).
steps.title: Add a second voice

steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony; the header reads VOICE LEADING CH01.
steps.title: Open Harmony

steps.caption: Set Mode to REVOICE and press K3 (Preset SMOOTH). Tap Play for two loops. Revoice keeps each pair's two pitch classes but chooses their octaves for the smoothest movement: both notes drop an octave to 48+50, 50+52, 52+53 and 53+55, at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97 in the strip below. Tap Stop.
steps.title: Revoice the pairs

steps.caption: A new empty project that has just started: stopped, Record off, channel 1 selected and no step held. The Channel editor is showing: its header reads NOTE MASKS CH01. The first step visits the page keys before you hold a step.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap each page key in turn and watch the header follow. Scale (4,8) opens the Scale Editor, SCALE SLOT 01. Pattern (5,8) cycles Trig, Note, then Velocity: three taps reach PATTERN VELOCITY PAT01 CH01. Song (6,8) opens SONG PLAYBACK SONG 01. Channel (3,8) brings you back to NOTE MASKS CH01.
steps.title: Visit the page keys

steps.caption: Tap channel 3 at (3,1). The header now reads NOTE MASKS CH03.
steps.title: Select channel 3

steps.caption: Press and hold step 5 at (5,4). The header reads CH03 ST05: ST05 means step 5 of the selected channel. While the step is held, edits on this Masks page apply to step 5 only.
steps.title: Hold a step

steps.caption: With step 5 still held, turn E2 to the Note cell and turn E3 one detent up. The Note cell changes from X to C-2 and the header still reads CH03 ST05, so the edit belongs to step 5 only.
steps.title: Edit while the step is held

steps.caption: Let go of step 5. The header drops back to NOTE MASKS CH03 and edits apply to the whole channel again.
steps.title: Release the step

steps.caption: Look at the Note cell now. It still reads X, the channel's own value, so the C-2 you set lives on step 5 alone.
steps.title: The channel value is unchanged

steps.caption: Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, scroll to Clock and press K3. The Clock page for CH03 is showing.
steps.title: Open the Clock page

steps.caption: Press and hold step 9 at (9,4). While it is held the screen switches to that step's Masks, header NOTE MASKS CH03 ST09, whichever page you were on.
steps.title: Hold a step from the Clock page

steps.caption: Release step 9. The screen returns to the Clock page, the page you were on before you held the step.
steps.title: Return to the parent screen

steps.caption: Two 8-step channels play at 90 BPM through the test device. Channel 1 (MIDI channel 1) has pattern 1 (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) as its Foundation anchor and pattern 2 (steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (MIDI channel 2) has pattern 3, a single trig on step 5, as its Foundation anchor. Channel 1 has no Interlock leader yet. The norns shows channel 1's Rhythm page and the grid lights steps 1 to 5 and 7.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Select Interlock with E2 and press K3 to open the Interlock page for channel 1. This keeps channel 1's additions out of the way of another channel's anchors.
steps.title: Open Interlock

steps.caption: Select Leader and turn E3 once right to CH02. Channel 2 would lead channel 1; nothing changes until you apply.
steps.title: Choose the leader

steps.caption: Press K3. The footer reads APPLIED, Window is 0 and Status reads ON. Step 5 goes dark on the grid because channel 1's addition starts exactly on channel 2's anchor. Steps 1 to 4 and step 7 stay lit.
steps.title: Apply: channel 2 leads

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops sound, then tap Stop. Channel 1 plays steps 1 to 4 and step 7, and channel 2 plays its anchor on step 5 on MIDI channel 2. Nothing from channel 1 sounds on step 5.
steps.title: Only the coincidence is removed

steps.caption: The lesson above is complete; the next four steps are edge cases. Tap Play. While it plays, select Window, turn E3 twice right to 2 and press K3. The footer reads NEXT CYCLE: playback is still running, so Window 2 is queued and starts at the next loop.
steps.title: Edge case: widen the window while playing

steps.caption: Window 2 is still queued. Turn E3 back to 0 as a new draft and press K2: the draft is discarded and Rhythm returns. Press K3 to reopen Interlock: Window still reads 2, the accepted value, not the discarded 0.
steps.title: Edge case: a later draft is discarded

steps.caption: After a few loops press Stop. The strip shows every loop played whole: the first loops with step 7, then without it once Window 2 took effect. The grid now shows steps 1 to 4.
steps.title: Edge case: the window takes over at the loop boundary

steps.caption: Select channel 2 (grid (2,1)). The screen shows channel 2's Merge Shape list, ready to set a leader for it.
steps.title: Select channel 2

steps.caption: Open Rhythm and then Interlock for channel 2: turn E2 to the row and press K3 each time. The header reads INTERLOCK CH02.
steps.title: Open channel 2's Interlock

steps.caption: Select Leader and turn E3 once right to CH01. Channel 2 already leads channel 1, so this would make a chain.
steps.title: Make channel 1 its leader

steps.caption: Press K3 to apply. The footer reads INVALID CHANNEL IS A LEADER: channel 2 already leads channel 1, so it cannot follow channel 1, and nothing changes.
steps.title: Edge case: a leader chain is refused

steps.caption: Press K2 to discard the draft and select channel 1 (grid (1,1)); the screen shows its Merge Shape list. Play two loops: Window 2 still applies, so channel 1 plays steps 1 to 4 and channel 2 plays step 5.
steps.title: The refusal changes nothing

interlock-leader-window.title: Leave room around a leader’s anchors

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and a MIDI keyboard is connected as Mosaic's input. This lesson continues from the degree and rotation lessons. Map scale to white keys is On and the scale is C natural minor, with degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2 set in the Scale Editor. Honour scale degree and Honour scale rotations are On and Honour scale transpose is Off, so the white keys C3 to C4 play 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 58, 60, 74.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Honour scale transpose and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.
steps.title: Turn on Honour scale transpose

steps.caption: Close the menu and play C3 to C4 again. The scale's global transpose of +2 now applies to everything you play, so every key sounds two semitones higher than in the start: 64, 65, 67, 69, 70, 60, 62, 76. The MIDI strip lists the notes Mosaic sent.
steps.title: Apply the scale transpose to live input

keyboard-honour-all.title: Apply the scale transpose to live input

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and a MIDI keyboard is connected as Mosaic's input. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Map scale to white keys and the three Honour switches are Off, and the Scale Editor is on C major.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Play some keys on the keyboard: each sounds the note you pressed, because nothing is mapped yet. Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Map scale to white keys and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.
steps.title: Turn on Map scale to white keys

steps.caption: Close the menu and play the white keys from C3 up to C4 on the keyboard. In C major they sound as written: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71, 72. The MIDI strip lists the notes Mosaic sent.
steps.title: Play the white keys in C major

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 two detents and press K3. The Scale row reads Minor, natural minor.
steps.title: Choose natural minor in the Scale Editor

steps.caption: Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play the white keys again: they now follow C natural minor, 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72 (C D E-flat F G A-flat B-flat C).
steps.title: Play the white keys in natural minor

steps.caption: Open the Scale Editor (4,8) again, turn E2 one click to Degree, turn E3 one detent and press K3. Degree reads ii°. Degree picks which scale note the keyboard's C starts on.
steps.title: Set degree II

steps.caption: Turn E2 to the Rotation row, turn E3 two detents and press K3. Rotation reads r2. Rotation moves the top keys down an octave.
steps.title: Set rotation 2

steps.caption: Tap the global transpose fader on the grid at its lowest value, then tap its increment button fourteen times, and return to the Channel editor (3,8). The Scale overview lists Transpose +2, which shifts everything.
steps.title: Set global transpose +2

steps.caption: The three Honour switches are still Off, so none of this is applied yet: the white keys still play 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72.
steps.title: Nothing applies yet

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Honour scale degree and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.
steps.title: Turn on Honour scale degree

steps.caption: Close the menu and play C3 to C4 again. Key C now plays the scale's second note: 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72, 74 (D E-flat F G A-flat B-flat C D). Rotation and transpose stay unapplied, so you can start a phrase from degree II without changing the scale.
steps.title: Start from the chosen scale degree

keyboard-honour-degree.title: Start from the chosen scale degree

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and a MIDI keyboard is connected as Mosaic's input. Map scale to white keys is On and the scale is C natural minor. The Scale Editor holds degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2, and Honour scale degree is On, so the white keys C3 to C4 play 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72, 74. Honour scale rotations and Honour scale transpose are Off.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Honour scale rotations and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.
steps.title: Turn on Honour scale rotations

steps.caption: Close the menu and play C3 to C4 again. Rotation 2 turns the top of the scale upside down: the last two white keys before the octave, the A and B keys, sound an octave lower, 58 and 60 instead of 70 and 72, giving 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 58, 60, 74. The first five keys do not change. Use it to play a bass note or an inverted voicing of the same scale shape from the keys you already know.
steps.title: Rotate the keyboard voicing

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on the test device: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4. The scale is C major, a MIDI keyboard is connected on port 1 and Map scale to white keys is off, its default. The sequencer is stopped, so the keyboard plays the channel's output directly. The norns shows the Device page.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Play the white keys C, D, E, F, G, A, B, then the black keys between them. With Map scale to white keys off every key sends its own pitch: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71 for the white keys, with 61, 63, 66, 68, 70 for the black keys. The strip below lists the notes in the order you played them.
steps.title: Raw notes by default

steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, go to MOSAIC, open the MIDI controller options and turn Map scale to white keys On. The row now reads On.
steps.title: Turn the mapping on

steps.caption: Leave PARAMS and play the white keys again. They now follow the selected scale with its root on C: in C major C D E F G A B C sound as 60 62 64 65 67 69 71 72, the same pitches as before. What changes is the black keys: each one repeats the white key above it, so C# sounds 62 instead of 61.
steps.title: White keys follow the scale

steps.caption: Tap Scale (4,8), turn E3 two detents to change the scale from Major to natural minor and press K3, then tap Channel (3,8). Play the white keys: C D Eb F G Ab Bb C sound as 60 62 63 65 67 68 70 72. Black keys still repeat the white key above them: C# plays 62 and D# plays 63. Read the strip below for the thirteen keys C to C: 60 62 62 63 63 65 67 67 68 68 70 70 72, the eight white keys being 60 62 63 65 67 68 70 72.
steps.title: Change the scale, change the keys

steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8). Turn E2 once and E3 to set the scale degree to II, press K3, turn E2 three detents and E3 to set rotation 2, press K3, then raise the transposition fader (the minimum at (9,8), then (16,8) fourteen times) to +2. Press Channel (3,8) and play the white keys C to C. All three Honour options are still Off, so the keys follow plain natural minor: look in the strip for 60 62 63 65 67 68 70 72, with each black key repeating the white key above it.
steps.title: Set degree II, rotation 2 and +2

steps.caption: Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC > MIDI controller options and turn Honour scale degree On, leave PARAMS and play the keys again. The seven white keys now start on degree II, so the whole run shifts: read the new notes in the strip below.
steps.title: Honour scale degree

steps.caption: Turn Honour scale rotations On as well and play the keys again. Rotation 2 drops the last two of the seven positions by an octave: compare the strip with the previous step.
steps.title: Add rotation

steps.caption: Turn Honour scale transpose On too and play the keys again. Everything now sounds two semitones higher than in the previous step.
steps.title: Add transposition

steps.caption: Turn Honour scale degree and Honour scale rotations Off and play, then Honour scale transpose Off, and finally turn Map scale to white keys Off in PARAMS > MOSAIC. Press Channel (3,8) and play C to C: every key plays its own pitch once more, 60 to 72, whatever scale is selected.
steps.title: Turn mapping off

keyboard-white-key-options.title: Let a keyboard follow the scale

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Wrap param slides is Off, and nothing is locked yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Trig params and assign the device's CC 1 to a trig slot. The channel default for CC 1 is 63.
steps.title: Assign CC 1 to a trig slot

steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm the CC 1 assignment and K2 to go back. Hold step 1 and turn E3 to 24. Slot 1 shows 24 with an L in its corner while the step is held. Release the step.
steps.title: Lock step 1 to 24

steps.caption: Hold step 3 and turn E3 to 96. Slot 1 shows 96 with the L. Release the step.
steps.title: Lock step 3 to 96

steps.caption: Hold step 4 and turn E3 to 48. Slot 1 shows 48 with the L. Step 2 gets no lock and keeps the channel default, 63.
steps.title: Lock step 4 to 48

steps.caption: Hold step 1 and press K3. Slot 1 shows 24 with an S in its corner, so the lock on step 1 now slides toward the next lock. Release the step.
steps.title: Turn a step slide on

steps.caption: Hold step 1 and press K3 again. The S goes and the L returns, so step 1 jumps again. Release the step.
steps.title: Turn the step slide off again

steps.caption: Play two loops. With no slide, CC 1 does not glide from 24 to 96. Each loop the MIDI strip shows only 24 on step 1, 63 on step 2 (the channel default, because step 2 has no lock), 96 on step 3 and 48 on step 4.
steps.title: Play without a slide

steps.caption: Hold step 4 and press K3 to give the last lock (48) a slide. Slot 1 shows 48 with the S.
steps.title: Slide the last lock

steps.caption: Wrap param slides is still Off, so there is no later lock to slide toward: CC 1 stays at 48 through step 4, and the first lock, 24, is recalled when the loop restarts. Play and listen for the value changing abruptly at the loop point.
steps.title: Give the last lock no destination

steps.caption: Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Wrap param slides and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.
steps.title: Turn Wrap param slides on

steps.caption: Tap K1 to return to Mosaic and play. The step-4 slide now runs from 48 down to 24 across one sixteenth-note step (one sixth of a second): CC 1 passes 40 and 32 and reaches 24 exactly with the first note of the next loop. Look for those CC values in the MIDI strip. Use this for a cyclic sweep, such as a filter that falls back to its start with no jump at the loop point.
steps.title: Slide to the first lock

last-lock-slide-wrap.title: Carry a slide across the loop boundary

steps.caption: Patterns 1 and 2 are both assigned to channel 1, with the same trigs on the same steps: pattern 1's notes are 2 steps long and pattern 2's are 4 steps long. Length merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (16,8). Length merge is set with K1 (shift) held, which turns the velocity merge button (16,8) into the length button.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8). Average is the mean of the two lengths, 2 and 4, so each merged note lasts 3 steps (0.5 s).
steps.title: Average length merging

steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap (16,8) once. The button lights brighter and Length mode on the screen reads UP, which is the manual's Longer: the mean plus the gap between the lengths. Without K1 the same button sets the velocity merge instead.
steps.title: Choose Longer

steps.caption: Tap Play. 3 + 2 = 5 steps (0.83 s), longer than either source: overlapping, legato notes. Use Longer for pads that run into each other.
steps.title: Longer length merging

steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap (16,8) again. The button changes again and Length mode reads DOWN, the manual's Shorter: twice the shortest length minus the mean.
steps.title: Choose Shorter

steps.caption: Tap Play. 2 x 2 - 3 = 1 step (0.17 s): short, staccato notes. Use Shorter for tight plucks.
steps.title: Shorter length merging

steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap (16,8) once more: Length mode reads AVERAGE. The modes cycle Average, Longer, Shorter and back: tap Play and the notes last 3 steps again.
steps.title: Return to Average

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a device with MIDI CCs, at 90 BPM with Rate /1, so one step lasts a sixth of a second. PARAMS is open on the device's CC 1 control at its stored value, 63, set in PARAMS > MOSAIC. CC 1 is not assigned to a Trig params slot yet, and parameter slides are off. The previous scene turned slides on for the whole parameter; this one turns them on for a single step.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K1 to leave PARAMS. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Trig params with E2 and press K3, then press K2 and turn E3 to CC 1 in the parameter list.
steps.title: Find CC 1

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign CC 1 and K2 to return. Slot 1 now reads 63, the stored value, with no marker in its corner, because no step has a lock for it yet.
steps.title: Assign CC 1 to the slot

steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4) and turn E3 to 24. Slot 1 shows 24 with an L in its corner while the step is held. Release the step.
steps.title: Lock step 1 to 24

steps.caption: Hold step 3 at (3,4) and turn E3 to 96. Slot 1 shows 96 with the L. Release the step.
steps.title: Lock step 3 to 96

steps.caption: Hold step 4 at (4,4) and turn E3 to 48. Slot 1 shows 48 with the L. Release the step.
steps.title: Lock step 4 to 48

steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4) and press K3. Slot 1 shows 24 with an S in its corner while step 1 is held, so only the slide that starts at step 1 is on. Release the step.
steps.title: Slide from step 1 only

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), let two loops play, then tap it again to stop. In the MIDI strip, CC 1 glides from 24 to 96 in equal steps of 12 (36, 48, 60, 72, 84) between steps 1 and 3, then jumps straight to 48 at step 4 with no glide.
steps.title: Play and watch the glide stop at step 3

steps.caption: Press K1 to open PARAMS. CC 1 still shows 63, the value you stored: the slide only shapes the messages sent while playing.
steps.title: The device setting does not change

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-note phrase through a MIDI device. The tempo is 130 BPM, the sequencer is stopped, the norns shows channel 1's Device screen and the PARAMS menu is closed. No trig params are assigned yet, so no CC values are sent.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4) and tap step 5 at (5,4) to extend the channel range to steps 1 to 5. Then on Channel tasks > Trig params assign CC 1 to a slot with E3 and K3, so steps can carry CC lock values. The phrase plays from the internal clock at 130 BPM.
steps.title: Assign CC 1 to a Trig params slot

steps.caption: On Trig params, hold each of steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 in turn and turn E3 to give it its own CC 1 lock value. Then tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, choose MOSAIC and select Lock lead time (ms) in the Parameter locks section. Turn E3 to 0. At 0 each lock value is sent at the same moment as its step, together with the note. This is the original timing.
steps.title: Give steps CC values, set lead to 0

steps.caption: Close the menu and press Play (1,8), listen to the phrase and press Play again to stop. In the MIDI strip every CC 1 value sits at the same millisecond as its Note On.
steps.title: Hear it at 0 ms

steps.caption: Tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Lock lead time (ms) and set it to 25, the default. At 130 BPM each lock value will now leave about 29 ms before its step (25 ms rounded up to a whole clock pulse of 4.8 ms). The notes keep their exact times.
steps.title: Set 25 ms lead

steps.caption: Close the menu, press Play (1,8) and Stop. In the MIDI strip each CC 1 value now arrives about 29 ms before its Note On, which still falls at its usual time. A synth that smooths incoming CC changes has already reached the new value when the note starts.
steps.title: Hear it at 25 ms

steps.caption: Tap K1, reopen Lock lead time (ms) and set it to 50. At 130 BPM lock values will leave about 53 ms (11 pulses) ahead of their step, and the notes still sound at their usual times. Use the larger lead for slow filters or effects that need longer to settle.
steps.title: Set 50 ms lead

steps.caption: Close the menu, press Play (1,8) and Stop. In the MIDI strip each CC 1 value arrives about 53 ms before its Note On, so the change lands before the note rather than gliding through it. The notes do not move.
steps.title: Hear it at 50 ms

lock-lead-menu-values.title: Send lock values before their notes

steps.caption: A new project with playback stopped, the default C major scale and Rate /1 (one step is a sixteenth note) on every channel. Channel 1 is set up and its Device page is open: it plays range 1-4, MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, to its own MIDI output. Channel 2 is not set up yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1), turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device and press K3. The header reads CH02: this second channel will play a three-step loop.
steps.title: Select channel 2

steps.caption: Give channel 2 its own MIDI output on the Device page. Give it pattern 1 and the range steps 1-3 (hold step 1 and tap step 3), then open Masks and set its values: Note 79, Vel 40 and Len ½ on every step, with step 2 locked to Note 81, Vel 60 and Len 1¼. Select channel 1 and press Play. Both channels start together on step 1. At step 4 channel 1 plays its fourth note, 65, while channel 2, whose three-step loop has wrapped, plays 79 again: look for 65 beside 79 in the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step".
steps.title: Build channel 2, then play both loops

steps.caption: Keep playing. Channel 1 loops four steps on its own MIDI port and channel 2 loops three on another, so their notes fall out of step and the MIDI strip shows two different phrases running side by side.
steps.title: Both channels keep looping

steps.caption: Keep playing. Hold step 4 and tap step 2 on channel 1: the reversed range (start 4, end 2) is refused and both loops carry on. Twelve steps after the start, the first step count that both 4 and 3 divide into, both phrases begin again from their first notes at the same moment: channel 1 plays 60 as channel 2 plays 79, and the next step plays 62 with 81. Look for that sequence in the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step", two seconds after the loops started.
steps.title: Both loops restart together at step 13

steps.caption: Press Stop. The refused reversed range changed nothing: both phrases keep the same timing, notes, velocities and lengths. Channel 1 still plays 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97 over steps 1 to 4, and channel 2 plays 79, 81, 79 over steps 1 to 3. Playback is stopped and the Masks screen is showing.
steps.title: Both loops stay locked

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device on OUT 1 and channel 2 to a second output, MIDI port 2 on MIDI channel 2. Each channel has its Masks defaults set so that every step sounds: channel 1 plays a low drum note, C1 (MIDI 36), at velocity 100 and channel 2 plays MIDI 72 at velocity 90, both half a step long. Channel 1's Masks screen is open. The Rate is /1 at 90 BPM, so one step lasts a sixth of a second, and playback is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Pattern (5,8) for Pattern Trig and choose pattern 1 at (1,1). Tap steps 2, 3 and 4 off at (2,4), (3,4) and (4,4), then tap steps 5, 9 and 13 on at (5,4), (9,4) and (13,4). Pattern 1 now has trigs on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13: four hits per bar.
steps.title: Enter the drum pattern

steps.caption: Choose pattern 2 at (2,1) and tap steps 1, 3 and 4 at (1,4), (3,4) and (4,4): a figure with trigs on steps 1, 3 and 4.
steps.title: Enter the short figure

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8) and channel 1 at (1,1); pattern 1 is already assigned to it. Hold step 1 at (1,4), tap step 16 at (16,4) and release step 1. The footer reads Channel 1 length changed: channel 1 now loops steps 1 to 16, and its four drum steps stay lit.
steps.title: Give channel 1 sixteen steps

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1) and assign pattern 2 at (2,2). Hold step 1, tap step 5 at (5,4) and release step 1. The footer reads Channel 2 length changed: channel 2 loops steps 1 to 5, and its three figure steps are lit.
steps.title: Give channel 2 five steps

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) and tap Play (1,8). The drum channel repeats every 16 steps and the figure every 5, so the figure's three notes slide across the drum hits. Both channels start together on step 1 and only start together again on step 81, 80 steps or 13 and a third seconds later, because 80 is the first step count that both 16 and 5 divide into. Look at the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step": channel 1 plays MIDI 36 four times in every 16 steps and channel 2 plays MIDI 72 three times in every 5. Tap Play again to stop.
steps.title: Play 80 steps

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97 on steps 1 to 4. Channel 2 does not play yet; in the next step you set it up on MIDI port 2, channel 2 with the same pattern. A saved MIDI map is loaded with two relative controls that both accumulate: CC 20 edits the velocity mask of the selected channel and CC 21 edits the velocity mask of channel 2. Both velocity masks are Off (X) and the norns shows channel 1's Device page.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Set up channel 2: select it (2,1), open its Device page and set its output to port 2, MIDI channel 2 with E2 and E3, press K3, give it pattern 1 with (1,2) and hold step 1 then tap step 4 to loop four steps. Select channel 1 (1,1), tap Play (1,8) and listen, then tap Play to stop. Channel 1 (port 1) and channel 2 (port 2) both play velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97: no control has been moved yet.
steps.title: Hear both channels before any CC

steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Masks for channel 1 and select the Velocity cell, which reads X. Channel 1 is selected. Send CC 20 with value 65 eleven times (the strip shows eleven control changes). For a relative (binary offset) control, 65 means one step up, 63 means one step down and 0 also counts as down. The velocity mask starts at X, so the first step reaches 0 and the eleventh reaches 10: the Velocity cell now reads 10.
steps.title: CC 20 on the selected channel 1

steps.caption: Tap Play. Channel 1 now plays every note at velocity 10. Channel 2 is unchanged.
steps.title: Hear channel 1 at velocity 10

steps.caption: Send CC 20 with value 63 twice and tap Play: channel 1 comes down from 10 to 8 and plays every note at velocity 8. Channel 2 is still unchanged.
steps.title: CC 20 down twice

steps.caption: Tap channel 2 at (2,1). The Masks screen stays open and its Velocity cell reads X for channel 2. Send CC 20 with value 65 three times: the cell reads 2. A selected-channel control follows the channel you select.
steps.title: Select channel 2, CC 20 follows

steps.caption: Tap Play. Channel 2 now plays at velocity 2 and channel 1 stays at 8.
steps.title: Hear channel 2 at velocity 2

steps.caption: Tap channel 1 at (1,1) to select it. Its Velocity cell still reads 8. Send CC 21 with value 65 twice, then tap channel 2 at (2,1) to look: its Velocity cell reads 4, up from 2. CC 21 is mapped to channel 2 itself, so it ignores which channel is selected.
steps.title: CC 21 ignores the selection
