Then turn E3 to 2: each note is its degree, one above or one below. Play and stop (first pass 59, 60, 62, 67). The MIDI strip shows this manual's fixed random run, which repeats exactly; on your norns the notes change on every pass, but always stay within the offsets named here.
steps.title: Turn Random Note up to 1, then 2

steps.caption: Turn E3 to 3: each note may move -1, 0, +1 or +2. Play and stop (first pass 60, 60, 67, 69). Then turn E3 to 4: each note may move -2, -1, 0, +1 or +2 scale degrees. Play and stop (first pass 57, 64, 67, 62).
steps.title: Turn Random Note up to 3, then 4

steps.caption: Turn E2 to the Twos Random Note slot, turn E3 to 4, then turn E2 back and play. The two offsets add, so each note may move anywhere from -6 to +6 scale degrees. First pass: 57, 59, 55, 64.
steps.title: Add Twos Random Note on top

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 (the channel range) with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen and every Mosaic option is at its default. Lock random to pent. and Lock merged to pent. are both On, and no trig params are assigned yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock random to pent. and turn E3 left to Off. The row shows Off. Random note offsets will now land on any degree of the seven-note scale.
steps.title: Turn Lock random to pent. Off

steps.caption: Select Lock merged to pent. and turn E3 left to Off. The row shows Off. That option only affects notes made by merge modes, so it has no effect on this lesson's random notes; the recording turns it Off here and you can leave it On.
steps.title: Turn Lock merged to pent. Off (not needed here)

steps.caption: Close the menu. On Channel tasks > Trig params assign Random Note to the first slot. The slot list shows Random Note; its value is still 0, so the pattern is unchanged.
steps.title: Assign Random Note

steps.caption: Assign Twos Random Note to the second slot in the same way. It stays at 0, so it adds nothing to this lesson; only Random Note is used.
steps.title: Assign Twos Random Note

steps.caption: Press Play (1,8) with Random Note at 0: the pattern repeats C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) with no random offsets. Stop playback.
steps.title: Hear the plain pattern

steps.caption: Raise Random Note to 4 in single steps: turn E3 right once, press Play (1,8) and Stop, and repeat until it reads 4. Random Note 4 offsets each note by -2, -1, 0, +1 or +2 scale degrees chosen at random, and with Lock random to pent. Off the results use all seven degrees of C major. The recorded final run begins 57, 64, 67, 62, 64, 59, 65, 65. F (65) and B (59) are in C major but outside C D E G A, so hearing them shows the lock is off. Random notes change on every run: play several loops and expect F and B to turn up now and then.
steps.title: Hear random notes on all seven degrees

random-pentatonic-off.title: Lock random notes to pentatonic: Off

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 (the channel range) with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen and every Mosaic option is at its default. Lock random to pent. and Lock merged to pent. are both On, and no trig params are assigned yet.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Lock random to pent. and turn E3 right to On (the default). The row shows On. Notes moved by Random Note or Twos Random Note will snap to the five-note selection.
steps.title: Check Lock random to pent.

steps.caption: Select Lock merged to pent. and turn E3 left to Off. The row shows Off. That option only affects notes made by merge modes, so it has no effect on this lesson's random notes; the recording turns it Off here and you can leave it On.
steps.title: Turn Lock merged to pent. Off (not needed here)

steps.caption: Close the menu. On Channel tasks > Trig params assign Random Note to the first slot. The slot list shows Random Note; its value is still 0, so the pattern is unchanged.
steps.title: Assign Random Note

steps.caption: Assign Twos Random Note to the second slot in the same way. It stays at 0, so it adds nothing to this lesson; only Random Note is used.
steps.title: Assign Twos Random Note

steps.caption: Select the Random Note slot, turn E3 right to 4 and press Play (1,8). Random Note 4 offsets each note by -2, -1, 0, +1 or +2 scale degrees chosen at random; with Lock random to pent. On every result snaps to the five-note selection C D E G A. Listen to several loops and press Stop. The recorded run begins 60, 64, 64, 64, 60, 64, 67, 64: step 4, a plain F (65), now sounds as E (64). Random notes change on every run, so your notes will differ. A step whose random offset is 0 keeps its own note, so a plain pattern note outside the selection, such as F, can still sound.
steps.title: Hear random notes locked to pentatonic

random-pentatonic-on.title: Lock random notes to pentatonic: On

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major. In PARAMS > MOSAIC, Lock random to pent. and Lock merged to pent. are Off, so offsets can land on any note of the scale. Random Note is already assigned to the first Trig params slot, and the parameter list is open for the second slot, on Twos Random Note (the manual's Random Twos Note), which is the slot you will turn.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Twos Random Note to the second slot and K2 to return, then press E2 to select the first slot, Random Note. Both slots read 0. Tap Play (1,8), then tap it again to stop: the phrase is unchanged, 60, 62, 64, 65.
steps.title: Offset 0 leaves the phrase alone

steps.caption: Turn E2 to the second slot, Twos Random Note, turn E3 one detent to 1 and turn E2 back: each note is its original degree or two degrees higher. Play and stop (first pass 60, 65, 64, 65). Then repeat to set 2: each note may move -2, 0 or +2 degrees. Play and stop (first pass 57, 59, 60, 69). The MIDI strip shows this manual's fixed random run, which repeats exactly; on your norns the notes change on every pass, but always stay within the offsets named here.
steps.title: Turn Twos Random Note up to 1, then 2

steps.caption: Repeat the E2, E3, E2 turn to set 3: each note may move -2, 0, +2 or +4 degrees. Play and stop (first pass 60, 59, 71, 72). Then set 4: each note may move -4, -2, 0, +2 or +4 degrees, leaps of thirds wider than Random Note's single steps. Play and stop (first pass 53, 65, 71, 59).
steps.title: Turn Twos Random Note up to 3, then 4

steps.caption: With the first slot, Random Note, selected, turn E3 to 4, then play. The two offsets add: each note may move anywhere from -6 to +6 scale degrees. First pass: 57, 59, 55, 64.
steps.title: Add Random Note on top

random-twos-note-seeded-offsets.title: Explore a bounded random contour in thirds

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to the test device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. The channel range is steps 1 to 4, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold step 2 (2,4), tap and release step 4 (4,4), then release step 2. The range is now steps 2 to 4 and those steps brighten. Tap Play (1,8) and listen: the channel loops D, E, F (62, 64, 65). Tap Play again to stop.
steps.title: Set steps 2 to 4

steps.caption: Hold step 4 (4,4), tap step 2 (2,4), then release step 2 and step 4. The end would come before the start, so Mosaic refuses it: the footer reads End must follow start and the grid still shows steps 2 to 4.
steps.title: Refuse an end before the start

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and Stop to check: it still loops D, E, F, because the refused gesture changed nothing. Then press step 2 (2,4), press step 4 (4,4) and release step 2 before step 4. The order of release matters: the footer reads End must follow start again and steps 2 to 4 stay bright. To set a range, release the later step first.
steps.title: Refuse a start released first

steps.caption: Tap Play and listen: D, E, F (62, 64, 65) loop with the same timing, because neither refused gesture altered the range. Tap Play to stop.
steps.title: Still D, E, F

steps.caption: Hold step 3 (3,4), tap and release step 4 (4,4), then release step 3. Steps 3 and 4 are bright and steps 1, 2 and 5 are dark: a correctly ordered gesture is accepted again.
steps.title: Choose a valid range

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen: E and F (64, 65) loop with the same step timing and gate lengths. Tap Play again to stop.
steps.title: Hear the new range

range-reject-and-recover.title: Keep a valid range when a gesture is reversed

steps.caption: Two 8-step channels at 90 BPM. Channel 1 has Pattern 1 (C D E F on steps 1 to 4) as its Foundation anchor and Pattern 2 (trigs on steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (MIDI channel 2) has Pattern 3, one trig on step 5, as its Foundation anchor, and is channel 1's Interlock leader with Window 0. Interlock ON removes a channel 1 addition that lands on the leader's anchor, so channel 1's grid shows steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 lit. Anchor gap is 0: Gap is a safety distance, 0 to 8 steps, kept clear of additions around an anchor, and 0 turns it off. Every step below is on channel 1 under Channel tasks > Merge Shape (E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Merge Shape, K3); Result, Reason and Rhythm are screens of that list.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Open Result and turn E3 to Step 7. Result shows Decision OK: the addition on step 7 is admitted.
steps.title: Open Result for step 7

steps.caption: Select Reason and press K3. Merge Reason lists Step 7, Role ADDITION P2 (an addition taken from Pattern 2), Decision OK, Interlock ON, Velocity 70 and Pitch target LEGACY.
steps.title: Inspect an admitted addition

steps.caption: Return to Result and turn E3 to Step 5. Result shows Decision INTERLOCK CH02: this addition is refused.
steps.title: Open Result for step 5

steps.caption: Open Reason again. Step 5 sits on the leader's anchor, so Role reads EMPTY P2, Decision reads INTERLOCK CH02 and Velocity reads NONE. The addition was refused and sends no note. EMPTY P2 does not mean Pattern 2 lacks a trig on step 5.
steps.title: Inspect an Interlock rejection

steps.caption: Open Rhythm, select Anchor gap, turn E3 once right to 1 and press K3. Anchor gap 1 keeps additions one step clear of an anchor, and step 5 is now next to the anchor on step 4 as well as on the leader's anchor.
steps.title: Set Anchor gap to 1

steps.caption: Open Result and select Step 5. Decision now reads GAP, INTERLOCK: two reasons are listed.
steps.title: Read the two reasons in Result

steps.caption: Open Reason for Step 5: Decision reads GAP, INTERLOCK, with Gap listed first.
steps.title: Inspect two rejection reasons

steps.caption: Press Play (1,8) for two loops, then Stop. Channel 1 plays C D E F on steps 1 to 4 and its addition on step 7. Step 5 stays silent on channel 1 even though Pattern 2 has a trig there.
steps.title: Play the filtered pattern

steps.caption: Channel 1 has pattern 1 assigned over steps 1 to 4, but pattern 1's trigs have been cleared, so no step is lit. A MIDI keyboard is connected on port 1 and Record is off. The norns clock source is internal; an external MIDI clock at 100 BPM is available. Mosaic records each note onto the step that is playing when the note arrives, so recording needs a running clock: this lesson borrows the external one. If you have no external clock, start Mosaic's own clock with Play (1,8) and arm Record the same way.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns PARAMS menu, open the CLOCK group and turn E3 so Source reads midi. Mosaic now follows the external 100 BPM clock.
steps.title: Follow the external clock

steps.caption: Close the menu and tap Record (2,8) to arm recording. While the external clock runs, play MIDI note 72 at velocity 90 and then note 79 at velocity 80 on the keyboard. Each note lands on the step playing when it arrives. Tap Record again to disarm. The grid shows steps 2 and 4 lit, and steps 1 and 3 empty. Which steps light depends on when you press, so your own take may land elsewhere.
steps.title: Record two notes

steps.caption: Tap K1, open the CLOCK group and turn E3 back so Source reads internal. Following the external clock left the tempo at 100 BPM, so turn E2 to the tempo row and turn E3 until it reads 90 BPM; any tempo works, the notes' spacing simply follows it.
steps.title: Back to the internal clock at 90 BPM

steps.caption: Close the menu and tap Play (1,8). The channel plays note 72 at velocity 90, then note 79 at velocity 80, repeating, as the MIDI strip lists. The two notes sit on steps 2 and 4, so they alternate every two steps: at 90 BPM with the default Rate /1 that is one third of a second apart.
steps.title: Replay and hear the rhythm

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped. Song mode is On, and the song has one slot with a 64-step global length. Every other option is at its default: Reset on song seq change is On and Reset on pattern repeat is Off.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold step 1 and tap step 3 to set the range to steps 1-3. On Channel tasks > Clock set Clock Mod to /9. One step now lasts nine sixteenths (1.5 seconds), so the three notes 60, 62, 64 cycle every 4.5 seconds, while the song pattern repeats every 64 steps (10.7 seconds). The two never line up, which is what makes the reset visible.
steps.title: Make a slow channel

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Make sure Song mode is On, then turn Reset on song seq change Off and Reset on pattern repeat Off. Close the menu, press Play and let it run for 24 seconds, then stop. The phrase carries on across each repeat: 60 62 64 60 62 64 60 62, then 64 at 12 seconds. Read the note times in the MIDI strip.
steps.title: Both resets off: the phase carries on

steps.caption: Turn Reset on song seq change On and play 24 seconds. A pattern that is only repeating is not restarted by a song change, so the phrase still carries on, with the same note times as before.
steps.title: Reset on song seq change alone

steps.caption: Turn Reset on song seq change Off and Reset on pattern repeat On, close the menu and play 24 seconds. At each 64-step boundary, 10.7 and 21.3 seconds, the slow channel restarts: note 60 sounds exactly at the boundary instead of waiting for the old cycle. Compare the note times in the MIDI strip with the first run.
steps.title: Reset at each repeat

steps.caption: Turn Reset on song seq change On as well, so both options are On, and play 24 seconds. The channel restarts at each repeat, as in the last step.
steps.title: Turn both reset options on

steps.caption: Select Song mode and turn E3 left to Off; both reset options stay On. Close the menu and play 24 seconds. With Song mode Off the slot is not stepped by the song, so neither reset applies: the phrase runs continuously again, with 64 at 12 seconds.
steps.title: Song mode off: no reset

repeat-reset-policies.title: Decide whether a slow channel restarts

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The Scale editor is open on slot 1, C major, which is the applied scale and is lit brightly on grid row 3. Slots 2 and 3 keep their default settings and are not applied. The sequencer is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap slot 2 at (2,3). The title row names slot 2 and its button lights dimly, while slot 1 stays bright: slot 2 is selected for editing but is not applied.
steps.title: Select slot 2 for editing

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Root, turn E3 two detents up to D and press K3 to save. Slot 2 now holds D major, but it is still not applied.
steps.title: Save D as the root

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), then Stop. The phrase still plays C, D, E, F, because slot 1 is the applied scale and slot 2 is only being edited.
steps.title: Hear that nothing changed

steps.caption: Tap slot 2 at (2,3). Its button lights brightly: it is now the applied scale.
steps.title: Apply slot 2

steps.caption: Tap Play, then Stop. The phrase plays D major: D, E, F#, G (MIDI 62, 64, 66, 67), with the same rhythm and velocities.
steps.title: Hear D major

steps.caption: Press and hold slot 3 at (3,3) for about one second. The editor switches to slot 3, which lights dimly, and slot 2 stays bright.
steps.title: Select slot 3 for editing

steps.caption: Tap Play, then Stop: the phrase keeps playing in D major (62, 64, 66, 67), because selecting a slot for editing never changes what you hear. Now hold K1 and tap slot 2 at (2,3). Slot 2 is both the applied scale and the one being edited.
steps.title: Select the applied scale for editing

steps.caption: Turn E3 two detents up so the root moves from D to E and press K3. Tap Play, then Stop. Saving a scale that playback is using changes it at once: the phrase now plays E major, MIDI 64, 66, 68, 69.
steps.title: Saving an applied scale changes the sound

steps.caption: Press and hold slot 3 at (3,3) for about one second. The editor moves to slot 3 and slot 2 is still the applied scale.
steps.title: Select slot 3 again

steps.caption: Press and hold slot 3 again. A long press on the slot already selected for editing turns the global scale off: no slot button is lit and the editing selection clears. A short press on the applied slot does the same.
steps.title: Turn the global scale off

steps.caption: Tap Play, then Stop. With no scale, pattern notes play as semitone steps from the root: C, C#, D, D# (MIDI 60, 61, 62, 63).
steps.title: Hear chromatic notes

steps.caption: Tap slot 2 at (2,3). The scale returns with the edits you saved. Tap Play, then Stop: E major, MIDI 64, 66, 68, 69. Recap: a tap applies a slot; K1 plus a tap, or a one-second hold, selects a slot for editing without applying it; a second hold on the slot being edited turns the global scale off; saving with K3 changes the sound only if that slot is the applied one.
steps.title: Apply a scale again

scale-edit-versus-apply.title: Prepare a scale before applying it

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays the four-step melody through a MIDI device with the scale locks from the last scenes: slot 3 (E major) locked on channel step 1, slot 4 (G major) locked globally on scale-track step 2, and Scales lock until ptn end Off. Step 2 is a rest, so the strip reads MIDI 64, 71 and 72 with a gap where step 2 was.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Put the trig back on step 2. Hold channel step 3 and press scale slot 2 at (2,3) to lock it to D major, then Play. With the option Off, E major applies at step 1 and ends at step 2, and D major applies at step 3 and ends at step 4. The strip reads MIDI 64, 69, 66 and 72.
steps.title: A new channel lock replaces the old one

steps.caption: Press K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn Scales lock until ptn end On, then return and Play. The E-major lock now lasts until the step 3 lock replaces it, and the D-major lock lasts to the end of the pattern. The strip reads MIDI 64, 66, 66 and 67.
steps.title: Turn the option back on, then play

scale-lock-replacement.title: Replace a scale lock with a later one

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of C major, so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65 in the plain scale. The scale track is four steps long. Scale slot 2 (D major) is applied, slot 3 is E major (root up four semitones) and slot 4 is G major (root up seven). A global scale lock puts slot 4 on scale-track step 2, and a channel lock puts slot 3 on channel step 1. Scales lock until ptn end is On, its default, so the channel lock beats the global lock for the whole pattern. The MIDI strip reads 64, 66, 68, 69: E major.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and turn Scales lock until ptn end Off. Return and Play. The channel lock now ends at the next trig that plays. Step 2 clears it, so steps 2 to 4 follow the global G-major lock: the strip reads MIDI 64, 69, 71 and 72.
steps.title: Turn the lifetime option off, then play

scale-lock-scope-and-lifetime.title: Let a scale lock last for the phrase

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays the same four-step melody (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 in plain C major) through a MIDI device. Slot 3 (E major) is locked on channel step 1, slot 4 (G major) is locked globally on scale-track step 2, and Scales lock until ptn end is Off, so the channel lock ends at the next trig that plays. All four steps play, so the strip reads MIDI 64, 69, 71 and 72: E major on step 1, then G major.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Open Trig params and assign Trig Probability to a slot. Hold step 2 and set its probability to 0, so step 2 is silent, then Play. A trig that does not play does not clear the lock; step 3 is the next trig that plays and clears it. The strip reads MIDI 64, 71 and 72, with a gap where step 2 was.
steps.title: A trig that does not play keeps the lock

steps.caption: Hold step 2 and press K2 on Trig params to remove its probability lock, then Play. Step 2 plays again and clears the channel lock, so the notes return to MIDI 64, 69, 71 and 72.
steps.title: Clear the probability lock

steps.caption: Open the Pattern editor with (5,8), choose pattern 1 at (1,1) and press step 2 to remove its trig, then return to the Channel editor with (3,8) and Play. A rest does not clear the lock either; the next trig that plays does. The strip reads MIDI 64, 71 and 72.
steps.title: A rest also leaves the lock in place

scale-lock-skipped-trig.title: Keep a scale lock through a silent step

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. The Scale editor is open on slot 1, C major, which is the applied scale and is lit brightly on grid row 3. Slots 2 and 3 keep their default settings and are not applied. The sequencer is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold K1 and tap slot 2 at (2,3). The title row names slot 2 and its button lights dimly, while slot 1 stays bright: slot 2 is selected for editing but is not applied.
steps.title: Select slot 2 for editing

steps.caption: Turn E2 to Root, turn E3 two detents up to D and press K3 to save. Slot 2 now holds D major, but it is still not applied.
steps.title: Save D as the root

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), then Stop. The phrase still plays C, D, E, F, because slot 1 is the applied scale and slot 2 is only being edited.
steps.title: Hear that nothing changed

steps.caption: Tap slot 2 at (2,3). Its button lights brightly: it is now the applied scale.
steps.title: Apply slot 2

steps.caption: Tap Play, then Stop. The phrase plays D major: D, E, F#, G (MIDI 62, 64, 66, 67), with the same rhythm and velocities.
steps.title: Hear D major

scale-save-d-and-apply.title: Save D major, then apply it

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern through the test MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 (the channel range) with notes C3, D3, E3 and F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Tempo is the default 90 BPM, Rate is /1 (sixteenth-note steps, one sixth of a second each) and the sequencer is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen and every Mosaic option is at its default. UI motion is at its default On.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC and select UI motion in the Screen section. Turn E3 left to Off. The row shows Off. UI motion only changes decoration; it never changes timing or input.
steps.title: Set UI motion Off

steps.caption: Close the menu. Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Clock and press K3 to open the Clock screen (Rate, Feel source, Swing type). Turn E3 to set Rate to /1.5 and press K3 to apply. Look at the mark in the top-right corner of the screen: it is in its rest pose.
steps.title: Open the Clock screen and set Rate /1.5 (motion Off)

steps.caption: Wait half a second and look at the same corner again. With UI motion Off the mark has not changed, and Rate, Feel source and Swing type are as readable as before.
steps.title: Wait: the mark does not move (motion Off)

steps.caption: Set Rate back to /1 the same way, turning E3 and pressing K3. Every label and value stays fully readable and the header mark stays in its rest pose.
steps.title: Set Rate back to /1

steps.caption: Press Play (1,8), let the four-note pattern play and press Play again to stop. With UI motion Off you hear C3, D3, E3, F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97; keep this as the reference.
steps.title: Play the phrase with motion Off

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select UI motion and turn E3 right to On. The row shows On.
steps.title: Set UI motion On

steps.caption: Close the menu and open the Clock screen again (E1 to Channel tasks, E2 to Clock, K3). Set Rate to /1.5 with E3 and press K3. Watch the mark in the top-right corner: this is the moment it passes through its rest pose, the same picture as with motion Off.
steps.title: Open the Clock screen and set Rate /1.5 (motion On)

steps.caption: Wait a fraction of a second and look at the same corner. The mark has turned to another pose while Rate, Feel source and Swing type still read exactly the same.
steps.title: Wait: the mark has moved (motion On)

steps.caption: Restore Rate to /1 with E3 and K3. Labels and values are still fully readable while the header mark keeps moving.
steps.title: Set Rate back to /1

steps.caption: Press Play (1,8), let the four-note pattern play and press Play again to stop. The notes (60, 62, 64, 65), velocities (127, 117, 107, 97), gates and transport LED are exactly what they were with UI motion Off: it changes only what the screen draws.
steps.title: Play the same phrase with motion On

screen-motion-on-and-off.title: Turn screen motion on or off

steps.caption: Channel 1 has two patterns assigned in an eight-step loop. Pattern 1 plays four notes (C, D, E, F on steps 1 to 4) and is saved as its Anchor; pattern 2 plays MIDI 60 on steps 5 and 7. Merge strategy is Skip, the default. Channel 2 has no anchor. Merge modes is open for channel 1. Terms used below: Strategy is the choice you make with E3 or grid key (14,8); Active is the strategy that is playing now; Pending is a choice waiting for its boundary and Boundary says when it will apply; Request says whether a choice was accepted, for example NEEDS ANCHOR.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 right until it reads FOUNDATION (grid key (14,8) steps through the same choices). Select Active: it reads FOUNDATION. The first pattern stays whole and the second only adds notes.
steps.title: Keep the foundation, add the other pattern

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) for two eight-step loops. The four anchor notes keep their velocities; MIDI 60 is added on steps 5 and 7 at velocity 70.
steps.title: Hear quieter additions

steps.caption: Under Foundation, Note, Velocity and Length modes still edit. Select each on Merge modes and turn E3 right to read UP, then left to read AVERAGE again.
steps.title: Numeric modes still edit

steps.caption: Press (14,8) again: Strategy reads FRAGMENTS.
steps.title: Press the key again

steps.caption: Strategy and Active read FRAGMENTS and (14,8) is at its brightest. The saved Note, Velocity and Length merge settings show AVERAGE SAVED; turning E3 on them changes nothing while Fragments is active.
steps.title: Saved modes are locked

steps.caption: With Size 8 and Seed 0 the loop takes pattern 2 whole: tap Play to hear MIDI 60 on steps 5 and 7 at velocity 100, the source's own velocity.
steps.title: Hear one source fragment

steps.caption: Press (14,8): Strategy wraps from FRAGMENTS round to SKIP and the key dims to its lowest level.
steps.title: Wrap to Skip

steps.caption: Select Note, Velocity and Length mode: the saved settings return as editable AVERAGE. Strategy order: Skip, Only, All, Foundation, Fragments; E3 stops at the ends but the grid key wraps.
steps.title: Return to the retained modes

steps.caption: Press (14,8) to choose ONLY. Only steps used by both patterns sound, and these patterns share none, so the grid shows no sounding trigs and Play gives no notes.
steps.title: Hear only the shared attacks

steps.caption: Press (14,8) once more to choose ALL, then press Play (1,8) for two loops and Play again to stop. With ALL, every attack of both patterns sounds: six in all. The added notes at steps 5 and 7 now use their source velocity, 100, not Foundation's 70.
steps.title: Compare the original additions

steps.caption: Select channel 2 and open Merge Shape > Rhythm. Anchor reads NONE: this channel has no foundation pattern saved.
steps.title: Channel two has no anchor

steps.caption: Assign patterns 1 and 2 to channel 2, open Merge modes, set Strategy to ALL and turn E3 right once to request Foundation. Turn E2 down the list to Request: it reads NEEDS ANCHOR, because channel 2 has no anchor pattern saved. Active stays ALL and Pending stays NONE.
steps.title: Read Request - NEEDS ANCHOR

steps.caption: Turn E2 back up to Strategy. It shows FOUNDATION while the footer reads NEEDS ANCHOR and Active is still ALL, so the refused choice stays visible but nothing changes in what plays.
steps.title: Recognise a missing anchor

steps.caption: Press (14,8) again: Strategy moves on to FRAGMENTS, so a refused request does not trap the key.
steps.title: The key still moves on

steps.caption: Turn E3 left until Strategy reads ALL again on channel 2.
steps.title: Set channel 2 back to ALL

steps.caption: Tap pattern slots 1 and 2 at (1,2) and (2,2) to take both patterns off channel 2, press Channel (3,8) and select channel 1 at (1,1). Open Channel tasks > Merge Shape > Rhythm: Anchor reads 1.
steps.title: Back to channel one

steps.caption: On the Channel editor toggle pattern slot 2 off and on, then remove pattern slot 1, the anchor pattern. Back on Merge modes turn E3 right once and turn E2 down to Request: Foundation is refused in the same way and Request reads NEEDS ANCHOR again. Active stays ALL.
steps.title: Read Request - NEEDS ANCHOR again

steps.caption: Turn E2 back up to Strategy: it shows FOUNDATION and the footer reads NEEDS ANCHOR. Assign the anchor pattern again to recover.
steps.title: Keep the assigned source explicit

steps.caption: Press (14,8): Strategy moves on to FRAGMENTS. Tap pattern slot 1 at (1,2) to assign the anchor pattern again, then select Strategy and turn E3 left to ALL.
steps.title: Return to ALL with the anchor back

steps.caption: Check Strategy still reads ALL, press Play (1,8), then turn E3 right once to request Foundation while ALL is playing. Turn E2 down to Pending: it reads FOUNDATION, the choice waiting for its boundary.
steps.title: Read Pending - FOUNDATION

steps.caption: Turn E2 further down to Boundary, which reads NEXT CYCLE. The current loop keeps playing ALL until it ends.
steps.title: Request a change during playback

steps.caption: Listen across the loop boundary. The first loop still uses the source velocity 100 on the added notes; the next complete loop plays Foundation's velocity 70. Playback never stops for the change.
steps.title: Hear the change at the loop boundary

steps.caption: Open Merge Shape from Channel tasks. It shows the accepted Strategy as a read-only summary; turning E3 there does not choose another strategy. Choose strategies with (14,8) or on Merge modes.
steps.title: Find the single Strategy selector

steps.caption: Press E2 to Rhythm, select Add amount and turn E3 left: it reads an unapplied 99.
steps.title: Edit Add amount without applying

steps.caption: Press K2 to leave without applying, open the Strategy selector and return to Rhythm. The accepted Add amount is still 100: an unapplied draft is discarded.
steps.title: Discard the parameter draft before selecting Strategy

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to a MIDI device and plays pattern 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in the default C major scale, with Rate /1. Its Clock page is set to Shuffle with Feel Smooth, Basis 9 and Amount 1. Timing is counted in pulses: each step is 24 pulses, so at Amount 1 the notes sit almost exactly on the straight grid, at 0, 24, 48 and 72. Feel and Basis stay the same through this lesson; only Amount changes.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Select Amount and turn E3 to 50, then tap Play (1,8). Two of the four notes in each group have moved: the second now lands at 26 pulses instead of 24 and the fourth at 71 instead of 72. Compare the ms offsets in the MIDI strip with the straight grid.
steps.title: Set shuffle amount to 50

steps.caption: Set Amount to 0 and tap Play: shuffle is off and the notes are back on the straight grid at 0, 24, 48, 72 pulses.
steps.title: Set shuffle amount to 0

steps.caption: Set Amount to 100 and tap Play: the fullest shuffle for this feel and basis, with the notes at 0, 26, 48, 69 pulses: the second note is 2 pulses late and the fourth 3 early. The second note was already at 26 at Amount 50 because offsets are whole pulses, so the extra Amount shows in the fourth note (71, then 69). For a stronger groove change Basis; the next steps use Basis 6.
steps.title: Set shuffle amount to 100

steps.caption: Select Basis and turn E3 to 6, then set Amount to 0 and tap Play. Amount 0 is straight timing whatever the basis: the notes sit on the grid at 0, 24, 48 and 72 pulses.
steps.title: Basis 6 at Amount 0

steps.caption: Set Amount to 50 and tap Play. Basis 6 moves the notes further than Basis 9 did: the second note lands at 28 pulses and the fourth at 68, halfway to the full groove.
steps.title: Basis 6 at Amount 50

steps.caption: Set Amount to 100 and tap Play. The second note is now 8 pulses late, at 32, and the fourth 8 early, at 64: two thirds of the way through each pair. Compare the ms offsets in the MIDI strip with the straight grid, where Basis 9 at Amount 100 moved the notes only 2 or 3 pulses.
steps.title: Basis 6 at Amount 100

shuffle-smooth-amount-boundaries.title: Set Smooth shuffle and change its amount

steps.caption: On channel 3's Device page, turn E3 until the Device row reads Doubledecker. The screen asks you to press K3 to confirm, so the selection is still a draft. Press K3 to apply it. The README describes Doubledecker as a two-layer synth; use it for a layered part after applying the selection.
steps.title: Select Doubledecker

steps.caption: On channel 1's Device page, turn E3 until the Device row reads Oilcan 1. The screen asks you to press K3 to confirm, so the selection is still a draft. Press K3 to apply it. The README describes Oilcan as percussion sync; use it for a percussion part after applying the selection.
steps.title: Select Oilcan 1

steps.caption: On channel 2's Device page, turn E3 until the Device row reads Polyperc 1. The screen asks you to press K3 to confirm, so the selection is still a draft. Press K3 to apply it. The README describes Polyperc as poly perc; use it for a percussive part after applying the selection.
steps.title: Select Polyperc 1

steps.caption: A fresh session with Song mode On, its default. Channel 1 plays its default phrase through the test device and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1; nothing is playing. You will build a two-note motif (MIDI 60, 62) copied into slots 1, 2, 4 and 5, with slots 3 and 6 left empty.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once. The Playback screen reads Global length 2, so every slot plays a two-note motif, 60 and 62.
steps.title: Set the global length to 2

steps.caption: Hold slot 1 at (1,1) and tap slot 2 at (2,1) to copy it, then tap slot 2. The Slot setup screen names Song 02 and the footer reads Song sequence 2 selected.
steps.title: Copy slot 1 into slot 2

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). The footer reads Ch. 1 octave: 1 and slot 2 will sound 72 and 74.
steps.title: Raise slot 2 an octave

steps.caption: Repeat for slot 4, leaving slot 3 empty: copy slot 1 into slot 4 and give it octave +2 at (12,8). Then copy slot 1 into slot 5 and give it octave -1 at (9,8). Slots 3 and 6 stay empty, so there are two groups: slots 1 and 2, and slots 4 and 5.
steps.title: Add slots 4 and 5

steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Slot 1 sounds 60, 62, then slot 2 sounds 72, 74. Slot 3 is empty, so the group ends and playback returns to slot 1: look at the MIDI strip for 60, 62, 72, 74, 60, 62, 72, 74. Press Stop.
steps.title: Hear the first group loop

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped. Channel 1 has been made slow: its range is steps 1-3 and Clock Mod is /9, so one step lasts 1.5 seconds and the phrase 60, 62, 64 cycles every 4.5 seconds. Song mode is On and the song has two 64-step slots, 10.7 seconds each. Slot 2 is a copy of slot 1 with the channel octave raised by one, so it sounds an octave higher: C4 D4 E4 are 72, 74, 76. Slot 1 is selected, so on the Song editor (grid (6,8)) its LED (1,1) is bright and (2,1) dim. Both reset options are Off.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Play. After 10.7 seconds, at the 64-step slot change, the slot LEDs swap brightness: (2,1) is now the bright one.
steps.title: Watch the slot change

steps.caption: Let it play to 23 seconds, then stop. The phrase keeps its place across the slot change: slot 2 starts on E4 (76) at 12 seconds, not C4. Read the note times in the MIDI strip.
steps.title: Both resets off: the phase carries across two slots

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Reset on song seq change and turn E3 right to On; Reset on pattern repeat stays Off. Close the menu and play 23 seconds. At each slot change, 10.7 and 21.3 seconds, the channel restarts on its first step: C4 (72) sounds exactly at the change, an octave above slot 1's C3, and the slot LEDs swap as before.
steps.title: Restart at a changed song slot

steps.caption: A fresh session with Song mode On, its default. Channel 1 plays its default phrase through the test device and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1; nothing is playing. The song has one slot, Song 01.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Open the Song editor with Song (6,8) and set a global length of 2 steps: tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once. Hold slot 1 at (1,1) and tap slot 2 at (2,1) to copy it, then tap slot 2. The Slot setup screen names Song 02 and the footer reads Song sequence 2 selected: slot 2 is selected and holds the same two-note motif as slot 1.
steps.title: Copy slot 1 into slot 2

steps.caption: Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). The octave button lights and the footer reads Ch. 1 octave: 1. Slot 2 now plays the motif an octave higher than slot 1, and slot 1 is unchanged: each song slot keeps its own octave.
steps.title: Raise the copy an octave

song-copy-and-compare.title: Copy a slot, then change the copy

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-note pattern. The song has one slot, Song 01, at the full global length of 64 steps, with Song mode AUTO, and the sequencer is stopped. The norns is showing the Pattern editor, left over from setup; it is not part of this lesson.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8). The Playback screen lists Playing SONG 01, Next SONG 01, Pass 1/1, Global length 64 and Song mode AUTO. The global length fader is on grid row 7: (1,7) subtracts one step, (8,7) adds one, and the buttons between jump to 1, 13, 32, 38, 51 and 64.
steps.title: Open the Song editor

steps.caption: Tap the fader's left end (1,7). It takes one step off the length and the Playback screen shows Global length 63. To loop a short fragment instead, jump with (2,7) to 1 step and add steps with (8,7); see the recipe on this page.
steps.title: Shorten by one step

steps.caption: Tap the fader's right end (8,7), which adds one step. Global length reads 64 again, so the whole phrase plays.
steps.title: Return to 64 steps

steps.caption: Tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once to add one. Global length reads 2. Press Play (1,8): the song plays only its first two steps and starts again, so the MIDI sent in this step is C and D (60, 62) over and over, never E or F. Press Play again to stop.
steps.title: Set the length to 2 steps and play

steps.caption: Tap (8,7) twice. Global length reads 4. Press Play: the whole four-note phrase now plays before the song starts again, so the MIDI sent in this step is 60, 62, 64, 65. Press Play again to stop.
steps.title: Set the length to 4 steps and play

steps.caption: Tap (7,7), the button that jumps to 64. Global length reads 64 again and the whole phrase is available to the song.
steps.title: Return to 64

steps.caption: A fresh session with Song mode On, its default. Channel 1 plays its default phrase through the test device and the norns shows the Device page; nothing is playing. You build the song in the next step: a two-note motif (MIDI 60, 62) copied into slots 1, 2, 4 and 5, with slots 3 and 6 left empty.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8), tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once. The Playback screen reads Global length 2, so every slot plays a two-note motif, 60 and 62.
steps.title: Set the global length to 2

steps.caption: Hold slot 1 at (1,1) and tap slot 2 at (2,1) to copy it, then tap slot 2. Tap Channel (3,8), select channel 1 at (1,1) and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Slot 2 will sound 72 and 74.
steps.title: Copy slot 1 into slot 2 and raise it an octave

steps.caption: Repeat for slot 4, leaving slot 3 empty: copy slot 1 into slot 4 and give it octave +2 at (12,8). Then copy slot 1 into slot 5 and give it octave -1 at (9,8). Slots 3 and 6 stay empty, so there are two groups: slots 1 and 2, and slots 4 and 5.
steps.title: Add slots 4 and 5

steps.caption: Tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Slot 1 sounds 60, 62, then slot 2 sounds 72, 74. Slot 3 is empty, so the group ends and playback returns to slot 1: 60, 62, 72, 74, 60, 62, 72, 74. Press Stop.
steps.title: Loop the first group

steps.caption: Tap slot 4 at (4,1) and press Play. Slot 4 sounds 84, 86 and slot 5 sounds 48, 50. Slot 6 is empty, so this second group repeats on its own: 84, 86, 48, 50, 84, 86, 48, 50. Press Stop.
steps.title: A second group

steps.caption: Tap slot 4 at (4,1) and press Play: slot 4 sounds 84, 86. While it plays, press slot 2 at (2,1). The press is queued, not instant. Slot 4 finishes, then slot 2 plays (72, 74) and its group carries on with slot 1 (60, 62) and slot 2 (72, 74). Press Stop; the screen shows where playback ended.
steps.title: Select the next slot while playing

steps.caption: Tap slot 1 and press Play. After the first note, press slot 4 and then slot 5 before slot 1 ends. Slot 1 finishes (60, 62), then the later press wins: slot 5 plays (48, 50), and its group continues with slot 4 (84, 86) and slot 5 again. Press Stop.
steps.title: Two presses before the boundary

steps.caption: Tap K1 to open the norns menu, choose PARAMS > MOSAIC, find Song mode and turn E3 to Off. The row reads Off.
steps.title: Turn Song mode off

steps.caption: Press K2 to leave the menu, select slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play. Slot 1 repeats, 60, 62, 60, 62, and does not advance to slot 2. Slot setup shows Song mode Off. Press Stop.
steps.title: Song mode off holds the slot

steps.caption: With Song mode Off, press Play on slot 1, then tap slot 2 at (2,1) while it plays. The press is still queued: slot 1 finishes (60, 62), then slot 2 repeats (72, 74, 72, 74) and keeps repeating. Song Playback reads Song mode MANUAL and Next HOLD.
steps.title: Manual selection still works

steps.caption: Turn Song mode On again the same way (PARAMS > MOSAIC), select slot 2 and press Play. Progression resumes inside the group: slot 2 (72, 74), slot 1 (60, 62), slot 2, slot 1.
steps.title: Song mode back on

song-mode-groups-and-selection.title: Loop a song group or hold one slot

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device at 90 BPM, Rate /1. Only Song slot 1 is filled, Song mode is at its default On and playback is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Song (6,8) and tap fader cell (2,7) on the Song page, then tap (8,7) seven times: Song Playback reads Global length 8, so one pass of a slot lasts 8 steps (about 1.3 seconds).
steps.title: Shorten the song to 8 steps

steps.caption: Hold slot 1 at (1,1), press slot 2 at (2,1) and release; tap (2,1) to select slot 2. Press Channel (3,8) and tap octave +1 at (11,8), then press Song (6,8). Turn E1 to Song tasks, E2 to Slot setup and press K3, turn E3 up one detent and press K3: Repeats reads 2 for slot 2.
steps.title: Copy slot 1 to slot 2 an octave higher with Repeats 2

steps.caption: Press Song (6,8), tap slot 1 at (1,1) and press Play (1,8). Slot 1 is bright and plays C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65); Song Playback reads Pass 1 / 1. Watch the MIDI strip "MIDI sent in this step": each note is one sixth of a second after the last.
steps.title: Play slot 1 once

steps.caption: After eight steps the song moves on by itself. Slot 2 is bright and slot 1 mid-bright; the phrase sounds an octave higher (MIDI 72, 74, 76, 77) and Song Playback reads Pass 1 / 2.
steps.title: Slot 2, first of two passes

steps.caption: Slot 2 stays bright and plays the same octave-higher phrase again; Song Playback reads Pass 2 / 2. Repeats held the slot for exactly two passes.
steps.title: Slot 2, second pass

steps.caption: Slot 3 is empty, so after slot 2 the song returns to slot 1: it is bright again, the notes drop back to C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and Song Playback reads Pass 1 / 1. Press Stop at (1,8).
steps.title: The song loops back to slot 1

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65 at velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) through a MIDI device on OUT 1, in C major at 90 BPM with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). Only Song slot 1 is filled. Song mode is Off, the global length is 32 steps (fader cell (4,7) on the Song page; Song Playback reads Global length 32) and playback is stopped. The norns shows channel 1's Device screen.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Close the menu and press Song at grid (6,8). Hold slot 1 at (1,1), press slot 2 at (2,1), then release both: slot 1 is copied to slot 2. Tap (2,1) to select slot 2. The top row now reads slot 1 mid-bright (filled), slot 2 bright (selected) and slot 3 dim (empty). The norns shows Slot setup for SONG 02 with the message Song sequence 2 selected.
steps.title: Copy a populated slot

steps.caption: Turn E1 to Song tasks, turn E2 to Slot setup and press K3. Turn E3 up to Repeats 2 and press K3 to apply. Song mode is Off, so Repeats does not hold the slot for extra passes here; it only shows as the pass count on Song Playback.
steps.title: Give slot 2 Repeats 2

steps.caption: Press Song (6,8) and then Play at (1,8). Slot 2 plays the phrase C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and stays bright; slot 1 stays mid-bright and empty slot 3 stays dim. Song Playback reads Playing SONG 02, Pass 1 / 2, Song mode MANUAL.
steps.title: Play the selected slot

steps.caption: Do these in order. 1: press Stop (1,8). 2: press Song (6,8) and select slot 1 at (1,1). 3: press Channel (3,8) and tap octave +1 at (11,8), so slot 1 sounds an octave higher. 4: press Song (6,8) again, select slot 2 at (2,1) and press Play (1,8). 5: while slot 2 sounds, press slot 1 at (1,1) to queue it. Slot 1 now blinks between dim and mid-bright (a still shows one moment of the blink) while slot 2 stays bright. Song mode is Off, so playback continues on slot 2 until one pass of its sequence ends.
steps.title: Queue slot 1 while slot 2 plays

steps.caption: Do nothing for about five seconds: slot 2 plays its full 32 steps (32 steps at one sixth of a second each). Slot 1 then becomes bright and plays its phrase an octave higher (MIDI 72, 74, 76, 77); slot 2 returns to mid-bright. Press Stop at (1,8). Song Playback reads Playing SONG 01.
steps.title: Hear the queued slot take over

steps.caption: With playback stopped, hold empty slot 3 at (3,1), press slot 2 at (2,1) and release: the empty slot is copied over slot 2 and erases it. Tap slot 1 at (1,1). Slot 1 is bright; slots 2 and 3 are both dim. There is no undo.
steps.title: Erase by copying an empty slot

steps.caption: Song slot 1 holds the four-step phrase (channel 1: MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and has just been copied to slot 2, which is selected. The top row of the Song page reads slot 1 mid-bright, slot 2 bright and slot 3 dim. Song mode is Off and playback is stopped. Repeats is the number of passes a slot plays before Song mode advances to the next slot; it ranges from 1 to 16.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: With slot 2 selected, turn E1 to Song tasks, turn E2 to Slot setup and press K3. Slot setup lists Repeats and Song mode. Repeats reads 1 for this freshly copied slot.
steps.title: Open Slot setup: Repeats 1

steps.caption: Repeats is already selected. Turn E3 up 15 detents to 16 and press K3 to apply. The screen shows OK and Repeats reads 16, the highest value.
steps.title: Set Repeats 16

steps.caption: Turn E3 down 14 detents to 2 and press K3 to apply. Repeats reads 2. With Song mode on, slot 2 would play two passes before the next slot. Song mode is Off in this example, so the value does not hold the slot here; it shows as Pass 1 / 2 on Song Playback.
steps.title: Set Repeats 2

steps.caption: Song slot 1 holds the four-step phrase on channel 1 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) and slot 2 is a copy with channel 1 raised one octave. Song mode is Off, the tempo is 90 BPM, slot 1 is selected and playback is stopped. Song tasks > Tempo / feel is the screen that holds the song's one tempo, next to its swing and shuffle feel.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Close the menu. With slot 1 selected at (1,1), turn E1 to Song tasks, turn E2 to Tempo / feel and press K3. Turn E3 all the way down: Tempo reads 30, the lowest value.
steps.title: Turn Tempo down to 30

steps.caption: Press K3 to apply, then press Play (1,8) to hear the phrase at 30 BPM and press Play again to stop. Swing type stays Swing and Swing 0.
steps.title: Hear slot 1 at 30 BPM

steps.caption: Select slot 2 at (2,1), the copy that plays an octave higher, then turn E1 to Song tasks, E2 to Tempo / feel and press K3. It already reads 30: tempo belongs to the whole song, not to one slot.
steps.title: Slot 2 reads the same tempo

steps.caption: Press Play (1,8) and Stop to hear slot 2 at 30 BPM. With slot 2 selected, open Tempo / feel again, turn E3 all the way up: Tempo reads 300, the highest value. Press K3 to apply.
steps.title: Turn Tempo up to 300

steps.caption: Press Play (1,8) to hear slot 2 at 300 BPM, ten times as fast as before, then press Play again to stop.
steps.title: Hear slot 2 at 300 BPM

steps.caption: Select slot 1 at (1,1) and open Tempo / feel again. It reads 300, the value you set while slot 2 was selected.
steps.title: Slot 1 reads 300

steps.caption: Press Play (1,8) to hear slot 1 at 300 BPM and Stop. Open Tempo / feel on slot 1, turn E3 down to 30, then up 60 detents to 90, and press K3 to apply.
steps.title: Set Tempo back to 90

steps.caption: Press Play (1,8) to hear slot 1 at 90 BPM, the starting tempo, then press Play again to stop.
steps.title: Hear slot 1 at 90 BPM

steps.caption: Select slot 2 at (2,1) and open Tempo / feel. It reads 90 too: the tempo you set on any slot applies to every slot.
steps.title: Slot 2 follows to 90

song-tempo-across-slots.title: Set Tempo and feel across Song slots

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 on the test device, the four-note melody C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) on steps 1 to 4. The additions of the Foundation phrase on steps 5 and 7 do not exist yet; you add them in the next step. No Harmony Ensemble group exists and Structure markers are off, so every note plays as written. The norns shows the Device page and the grid lights steps 1 to 4.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold step 1 (1,4) and tap step 8 (8,4) to loop eight steps. Open the pattern page (5,8), choose pattern 2 (2,1), tap trigs on steps 5 and 7, return to Channel (3,8) and assign pattern 2 (2,2). Then open Channel tasks > Harmony and choose Ensemble. The header reads ENSEMBLE CH01.
steps.title: Add the additions, open Ensemble

steps.caption: On the Ensemble list choose Create group and press K3 to make group 1. Select Template count with E2 and turn E3 to 3: the group's chord has three tones.
steps.title: Make the chord three notes

steps.caption: Select Tone 2 with E2 and turn E3 to 2, two scale degrees above the root, which is E in C major.
steps.title: Set Tone 2

steps.caption: Select Tone 3 with E2 and turn E3 to 4, four scale degrees above the root, which is G. The chord is now C, E and G.
steps.title: Set Tone 3

steps.caption: Press K3 to apply: the footer reads APPLIED.
steps.title: Apply the chord

steps.caption: Press K2 to return to the Ensemble list, select Members and press K3. The header reads MEMBERS CH01: the list of channels that follow the group's chord.
steps.title: Open Members

steps.caption: Set Group enabled to On with E3 and press K3. Voice count reads 1: channel 1, the only member, carries the chord on its own. The footer reads APPLIED.
steps.title: Switch the group on

steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Merge Shape, set Mode to Foundation and press K3 to apply. Open Merge modes: Strategy and Active read FOUNDATION, so the four anchors on steps 1 to 4 plus the additions on steps 5 and 7 now play.
steps.title: Turn Foundation on

steps.caption: Open Merge Shape > Pitch, then choose Structure. Structure snaps chosen moments of the Foundation line to a chord while the notes in between keep their own pitch.
steps.title: Open Structure

steps.caption: Turn E3 once to set Markers to ANCHORS: every anchor onset now counts as a marker.
steps.title: Markers on anchors

steps.caption: A Chord group row appears showing 1, the Ensemble group you made. Structure needs an enabled group before Apply will accept the markers.
steps.title: Chord group one appears

steps.caption: Press K3 to apply, then tap Play. Each anchor note snaps to the nearest chord tone, and a note exactly between two chord tones snaps to the lower one. Step 1 stays at 60, step 2 moves from 62 to 60, step 3 stays at 64 and step 4 moves from 65 to 64: the loop plays MIDI 60, 60, 64, 64 in the strip below. The added notes on steps 5 and 7 keep their own pitch and accent. Tap Play to stop.
steps.title: Anchors snap to the chord

steps.caption: Open Channel tasks > Harmony > Ensemble and choose Delete group for group 1. A confirmation opens before anything is deleted; its Affected row reads 1, naming channel 1 as the channel that uses the group.
steps.title: Check who deletion affects

steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm. Deleting the group also sets Markers to OFF in the same change. Tap Play: the anchors return to their written pitches, MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65, and the added notes on steps 5 and 7 are unchanged. Tap Play to stop.
steps.title: Deletion restores authored pitches

structure-anchor-chord-and-delete.title: Snap Foundation anchors to a chord

steps.caption: Channel 1 loops eight steps: pattern 1 plays C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) on steps 1 to 4, and pattern 2 adds trigs on steps 5 and 7. Merge Shape has Foundation on with pattern 1 as the anchor, and Harmony Ensemble has an enabled group holding C, E and G. The Structure screen is open with Markers on Anchors, so each anchor note is a marker. Playback is stopped.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent to the right of Anchors and press K3. Markers reads EVERY 4 and the footer says APPLIED: steps 1, 5, 9 and so on are the markers, whatever plays there.
steps.title: Set Markers to Every 4

steps.caption: Press Play, then Stop. Only the marker steps snap to the group, so look at the MIDI strip: step 1 plays 60 and step 5 plays 60 too, because its D snaps to C, while steps 2, 3 and 4 are no longer markers and keep their own notes 62, 64 and 65. Step 7 adds another 60. Each loop sounds 60, 62, 64, 65, 60, 60.
steps.title: Markers 1 and 5 snap to the chord

steps.caption: Channel 1 sends to the test device and plays pattern 1: four notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) on steps 1 to 4 in C major. Nothing is assigned to Trig params yet, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page for channel 1.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Open Trig params (E1 to the channel's Trig params page), press K2 to enter the slot list, turn E3 until the parameter reads Chord Note Strum, press K3 to assign it to the first slot, then press K2 to leave the list. The slot shows as Strm on the screen: it is the strum slot.
steps.title: Give Chord Note Strum a slot

steps.caption: Press K3 to select the Strm slot. It reads X, which means no strum: the notes of a chord sound together. Every strum division is chosen with E3 from here.
steps.title: A new slot starts at X

steps.caption: Turn E3 left a few detents: nothing happens, because X is the lowest value. Then turn E3 one detent right. The slot reads 1/24, one twenty-fourth of a channel step between chord notes, the smallest strum division.
steps.title: First supported division

steps.caption: Keep turning E3 right, about ninety detents, through the supported divisions until the slot reads 128 channel steps, then turn a few detents further: it stays at 128 and extra turns do not go higher.
steps.title: Climb to the upper bound

steps.caption: Turn E3 one detent left. The slot reads 120, the next supported division below 128; turning back left continues down towards 1/24 and X.
steps.title: One step back down

steps.caption: Two 8-step channels at 90 BPM. Channel 1 has Pattern 1 (C D E F on steps 1 to 4) as its Foundation anchor and Pattern 2 (trigs on steps 5 and 7) as additions. Channel 2 (MIDI channel 2) has one anchor trig on step 5 and is channel 1's Interlock leader. Interlock removes channel 1's addition on step 5, so channel 1's grid shows steps 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 lit. Clock Rate is /1 and Swing is not set (X).
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Clock and press K3. Set Feel source to CHANNEL (E3, then K3) so this channel uses its own feel instead of the Song page's. Then select Swing and turn E3 up to 25. Swing runs from -50 to 50 and at 25 every second step is played a quarter of a step late.
steps.title: Set Swing to 25

steps.caption: Open Merge Shape > Interlock: Status is still ON and step 5 is still removed (step 7 is lit). Swing did not change the merge.
steps.title: Interlock is still on

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8), listen to a loop or two and tap Play again to stop. Step 5 is still silent. Steps 2 and 4 sound a quarter of a step (about 42 ms) late: in the MIDI strip they sit near 208 ms and 542 ms instead of 167 ms and 500 ms, while steps 1 and 3 stay put (0 and 333 ms) and the added step 7 plays quietly (velocity 70) at 1000 ms. Swing moves the notes but the merge result stays the same.
steps.title: Hear the swung notes

swing-interlock-pulse-times.title: Swing a merged part: Interlock still removes step 5

steps.caption: The norns matrix and toolkit mods are installed and enabled, and the norns tempo is 90 BPM. Channel 1 plays the four-step phrase (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) through a CC device with Rate /1, the sequencer is stopped, and the Matrix has no routes yet. The Device page for CH01 is showing.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open MODS > MATRIX. Choose MOSAIC CH 1: CC DEVICE and select Fixed Note, the parameter the LFO will drive. Press K3 to open Fixed Note's sources and turn E2 to lfo 1; its row shows dashes, no depth yet. Hold E3 turning right until lfo 1's depth reads 1.00, so the LFO controls Fixed Note at full strength.
steps.title: Route lfo 1 to Fixed Note at full depth

steps.caption: Open the parameters list, choose toolkit lfo 1 (PARAMETERS / lfo 1) and select clocked, which makes the LFO follow the tempo instead of running in seconds. Press K3 to switch it on: clocked shows a filled marker.
steps.title: Clock the LFO to the tempo

steps.caption: Turn E2 down one row to Beats, the LFO period in beats. It reads 1/4. Turn E3 right until Beats reads 4, a period of four beats. Turn E2 down two rows to Shape, which still reads sine.
steps.title: Set the period and the shape

steps.caption: Turn E3 two detents to choose Pulse. Shape now reads pulse.
steps.title: Choose Pulse

steps.caption: Tap K1 and press Play. The LFO now alternates every two beats, half of its four-beat period: eight steps at MIDI 127, the Fixed Note pitch, then eight steps of the authored phrase, 60, 62, 64, 65, repeating. The MIDI strip lists the notes in that order.
steps.title: Play the phrase

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. The Scale page is open on the transposition fader along the bottom row. Global transposition is +4 (set at (13,8)). Scale-track step 2 has a transposition lock of 0, the fader's centre at (12,8), and step 1 has a lock of -12, the lowest value at (9,8). The MIDI strip reads 48, 62, 64, 65: step 1 sounds an octave below its written note, while steps 2 to 4 ignore the global +4 because the zero lock on step 2 holds for the rest of the loop. This is how you keep one part of a song at its written pitch while the rest is transposed.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and press the right end of the fader, (16,8), twelve times, playing as you go if you like. Each press adds one semitone, from -12 up to 0. A lock of 0 is an explicit lock: it overrides the global +4, so step 1 plays MIDI 60 and not 64.
steps.title: Walk step 1 up to an explicit zero

steps.caption: Keep holding step 1 and press (16,8) twelve more times. Each press adds one semitone, up to +12. The first note jumps an octave to MIDI 72. Steps 2 to 4 still follow the zero lock on step 2 and stay at MIDI 62, 64 and 65.
steps.title: Walk on up to +12

steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and press K2 to remove its lock. Step 1 now follows the global +4 and plays MIDI 64. The zero lock on step 2 is still active for steps 2 to 4, so the loop plays MIDI 64, 62, 64 and 65.
steps.title: Clear the lock on step 1

transpose-explicit-zero-and-clear.title: Lock transposition without losing the global setting

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. The Scale page is open on the transposition fader along the bottom row. Global transposition is +4. Scale-track step 2 has a transposition lock of 0, the fader's centre at (12,8), and step 1 has just been locked to -12 with one tap on the lowest value, (9,8), while it was held. The MIDI strip reads 48, 62, 64, 65.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and tap the centre of the fader, (12,8), once. The lock moves from -12 straight to 0 with no walking. A lock of 0 overrides the global +4, so step 1 plays MIDI 60 and not 64.
steps.title: Jump to an explicit zero

steps.caption: Hold step 1 and tap (15,8) once. The lock jumps to +12, and the first note sounds an octave up at MIDI 72. Steps 2 to 4 still follow the zero lock on step 2, MIDI 62, 64 and 65.
steps.title: Jump up an octave

steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and press K2 to remove its lock. Step 1 follows the global +4 again and plays MIDI 64, so the loop plays 64, 62, 64 and 65.
steps.title: Clear the lock on step 1

transpose-lock-direct-taps.title: Jump a transposition lock straight to a value

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the test device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Global transposition is 0, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8) to open the Scale Editor, then tap Play (1,8). One step lasts about a sixth of a second at 90 BPM, so the four-note phrase repeats about every two thirds of a second; exact timing does not matter. While it loops, press (16,8) on the transposition fader once. The screen shows Scale overview with Transpose +1: the note sounding at that moment keeps its pitch and length, and the next notes play a semitone higher, MIDI 61, 63, 65 and 66, as the MIDI strip lists.
steps.title: Press +1 while it plays

steps.caption: After a few more notes press (9,8) to set -12. Transpose reads -12: again the sounding note is untouched and the next notes drop an octave below the written pitches, 48, 50, 52 and 53.
steps.title: Press -12 a few notes later

steps.caption: Tap Play to stop. Transpose still reads -12, and in the strip every note-on has its own matching note-off.
steps.title: Stop

steps.caption: Both edits changed only the next onset: the notes before the first edit are 60, 62, 64, 65, then 61, 63, 65, 66, then 48, 50, 52, 53, and each held note finished at its own pitch and length.
steps.title: The whole run

transpose-next-onset.title: Transpose the next note without cutting the current one

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody on the test device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Global transposition is 0, the Song editor holds only slot 1, playback is stopped and the norns shows the Device page.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press Song (6,8) to open the Song editor. Hold slot 1 at (1,1) and press slot 2 at (2,1), then release both, and tap slot 2. Slot 2 is selected and bright, slot 1 is lit: slot 2 holds a copy of the melody.
steps.title: Copy slot 1 to slot 2

steps.caption: Press Scale (4,8). Press the left end of the transposition fader at (9,8) to set -12, then press (16,8) fourteen times to reach +2. The Scale overview shows Transpose +2 for this slot.
steps.title: Raise the copy by two semitones

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8) and listen, then tap Play to stop. The copy loops D, E, F sharp, G: MIDI 62, 64, 66 and 67 in the strip below.
steps.title: Hear the copy

steps.caption: Press Song (6,8), tap slot 1 at (1,1) and tap Play (1,8). Slot 1 still loops C, D, E, F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65): the transposition belongs to the copy only. Tap Play to stop.
steps.title: Slot 1 keeps its pitches

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device on OUT 1: four trigs on steps 1-4 (C, D, E, F = MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65; velocities 127, 117, 107, 97) in C major at 90 BPM, with sixteenth-note steps (Rate /1). The Trig params screen is open on its parameter list, showing Fixed Note; every slot is empty (None).
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Press K3 to assign Fixed Note to the first slot and K2 to return. With no step held, turn E3 to 60 (C3). Play, then stop: the MIDI strip lists C3 (60) on all four steps.
steps.title: Set the channel default

steps.caption: Hold step 2 at (2,4), turn E3 to 63 (D#3) and release. A value set on a held step is a lock. Play, then stop: step 2 plays 63 and the other steps keep the default, 60, 63, 60, 60.
steps.title: Lock one step

steps.caption: Hold step 1 at (1,4), turn E3 down to 0 and release. Play, then stop: 0, 63, 60, 60. Zero is a real note, not Off.
steps.title: Lock a second step

steps.caption: Hold step 4, turn E3 down to X (Off) and release: a step at X has no lock, so it follows the default. Then, with no step held, turn E3 up five detents to 65. Play, then stop: 0, 63, 65, 65. Steps 1 and 2 keep their locks.
steps.title: Raise the default beneath the locks

steps.caption: Hold step 2 at (2,4), press K2 and release: its lock is cleared and step 2 returns to the default. Play, then stop: 0, 65, 65, 65. Step 1 keeps its MIDI 0 lock; steps 2 to 4 follow the default. To lock a CC value the same way, see Brighten the last note with a cutoff lock.
steps.title: Let the default apply again

trig-parameter-locks.title: Lock a value, then clear just that step

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and the Device page for CH01 is showing. Channel 2 is not set up yet: you will make it a steady timing reference. Trigless locks is at its default On.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC, select Trigless locks and turn E3 left to Off. The row reads Off.
steps.title: Turn Trigless locks off

steps.caption: Press K2, then K1 to leave the menu. Set up channel 2 as the timing reference: tap (2,1), open Channel tasks > Device, point it at the second MIDI port, give it pattern 1 at (1,2) and range steps 1-4 (hold (1,4), tap (4,4)). It will play C D E F on MIDI channel 2 on every loop whatever you do to channel 1. Then tap channel 1 (1,1), open Channel tasks > Trig params and assign CC 1 to the first slot.
steps.title: Assign CC 1

steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm CC 1 and K2 to go back. Hold step 1 and turn E3 to 24. Slot 1 shows 24 with an L in its corner while the step is held. Release the step.
steps.title: Lock step 1 to 24

steps.caption: Do the same on the other steps. Hold step 2 and turn E3 to 48, hold step 3 for 72 and hold step 4 for 96. Slot 1 reads 96 with the L while step 4 is held, so every step now carries its own CC 1 value.
steps.title: Lock steps 2 to 4 to 48, 72 and 96

steps.caption: Assign Trig probability to the second slot, so you can silence channel 1's notes and see only its CC 1 stream beside channel 2's steady notes.
steps.title: Add Trig probability

steps.caption: Set Trig probability to 0 so channel 1's notes never sound, and play two loops. All four steps still have trigs, so CC 1 still goes out at every step (24, 48, 72, 96) even with Trigless locks Off: look for those four CC values each loop in the MIDI strip, beside channel 2's steady notes. A probability of 0 is not a rest: only a removed trig is.
steps.title: Probability 0 silences the notes, not the locks

steps.caption: Open the Pattern editor (5,8), tap step 3 to remove its trig, and return to the Channel editor (3,8). Play. With Trigless locks Off, a lock on a step with no trig is skipped: the MIDI strip shows CC 1 sending 24, 48 and 96 but not 72, the value on step 3.
steps.title: Remove the third trig

steps.caption: Hold step 4 and turn E3 to set its Trig probability lock to 100, then play. Step 4's note (F3, 65) now sounds, with its CC 1 lock (96) sent just before it. Steps 1 and 2 stay silent, and step 3 still sends no value. The scene Keep automation on rests plays the same steps with Trigless locks On, for comparison.
steps.title: Keep a lock ahead of its accepted note

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and the Device page for CH01 is showing. Channel 2 is not set up yet: you will make it a steady timing reference. Trigless locks is at its default On.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC. Trigless locks reads On, its default, so locks on steps without a trig will still be sent. Press K2, then K1 to leave the menu. Set up channel 2 as the timing reference: tap (2,1), open Channel tasks > Device, point it at the second MIDI port, give it pattern 1 at (1,2) and range steps 1-4 (hold (1,4), tap (4,4)). It will play C D E F on MIDI channel 2 on every loop whatever you do to channel 1. Then tap channel 1 (1,1), open Channel tasks > Trig params and assign CC 1 to the first slot.
steps.title: Check Trigless locks, then set up the channels

steps.caption: Press K3 to confirm CC 1 and K2 to go back. Hold step 1 and turn E3 to 24. Slot 1 shows 24 with an L in its corner while the step is held. Release the step.
steps.title: Lock step 1 to 24

steps.caption: Do the same on the other steps. Hold step 2 and turn E3 to 48, hold step 3 for 72 and hold step 4 for 96. Slot 1 reads 96 with the L while step 4 is held, so every step now carries its own CC 1 value.
steps.title: Lock steps 2 to 4 to 48, 72 and 96

steps.caption: Assign Trig probability to the second slot, so you can silence channel 1's notes and see only its CC 1 stream beside channel 2's steady notes.
steps.title: Add Trig probability

steps.caption: Set Trig probability to 0 so channel 1's notes never sound, and play two loops. All four steps have trigs, so CC 1 goes out at every step (24, 48, 72, 96) even though no note plays: look for those four CC values each loop in the MIDI strip, beside channel 2's steady notes.
steps.title: Probability 0 silences the notes, not the locks

steps.caption: Open the Pattern editor (5,8), tap step 3 to remove its trig, and return to the Channel editor (3,8). Play. With Trigless locks On, a lock on a step with no trig is still sent: the MIDI strip shows CC 1 still sending 72 at step 3, so automation keeps moving through rests, for example a filter sweep under a sparse rhythm.
steps.title: Remove the third trig

steps.caption: Hold step 4 and turn E3 to set its Trig probability lock to 100, then play. Step 4's note (F3, 65) now sounds, with its CC 1 lock (96) sent just before it. Steps 1 and 2 stay silent, and step 3 still sends its 72. The scene Skip automation on rests plays the same steps with Trigless locks Off, for comparison.
steps.title: Keep a lock ahead of its accepted note

steps.caption: Channel 1 has two patterns assigned with different velocities for four notes: 127, 117, 107, 97 and 100, 100, 100, 100. Its notes come from a third pattern, shown on the screen as Note mode PAT 4 (pattern 4 is not assigned to the channel; all its notes are MIDI 67), so only velocity changes. Velocity merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (16,8).
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8). Each velocity is the mean of the two sources, for example (127 + 100) / 2 = 114, so the four notes sound at 114, 109, 104 and 99. Read the velocities in the MIDI strip, "MIDI sent in this step": every note is MIDI 67 and only the velocity changes.
steps.title: Average velocity merging

steps.caption: Tap (16,8) once, without K1 (with K1 held the same button sets length merge instead). The button lights brighter and Velocity mode on the screen reads UP, which is the manual's Higher: the mean plus the gap between the sources.
steps.title: Choose Higher

steps.caption: Tap Play. The four velocities in the MIDI strip are 127, 126, 111 and 102. The first is 114 + 27 = 141, limited to 127. Use Higher to accent a step.
steps.title: Higher velocity merging

steps.caption: Tap (16,8) again. The button changes again and Velocity mode reads DOWN, the manual's Lower: twice the lowest source minus the mean.
steps.title: Choose Lower

steps.caption: Tap Play. The four velocities in the MIDI strip are 86, 91, 96 and 95. The first is 2 x 100 - 114 = 86. Use Lower for ghost notes.
steps.title: Lower velocity merging

steps.caption: Tap (16,8) once more. The modes cycle Average, Higher, Lower and back: tap Play and the MIDI strip shows the velocities 114, 109, 104 and 99 again.
steps.title: Return to Average

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through the test MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, in C major, stopped. Clock Rate is /1 and no Swing or Shuffle is set. Channel 1 is selected and its Clock page is open. Your goal is to give channel 1 its own shuffle feel. Rate is the first row of a vertical list.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E2 left until Rate is selected, the first row (it reads /1, the default). The list shows Rate, Feel source and Swing type together, so you can read the channel's clock and feel settings at a glance.
steps.title: Read the Clock settings together

steps.caption: Tap K1 twice: the first tap opens the norns menu and the second closes it, and the page keeps your place. Turn E2 to Swing type. It reads X: this channel has no feel of its own yet.
steps.title: Select Swing type

steps.caption: Turn E3 left as far as it goes and press K3. It stays at X. X means this channel follows the global feel set in Song > Tempo and feel.
steps.title: Follow the global feel

steps.caption: Turn E3 right to Shuffle and press K3. Shuffle adds its own rows below Swing type for setting this channel's feel.
steps.title: Choose Shuffle

steps.caption: Keep turning E2 right. The list stops on its last row, Shuffle amount (0), and does not wrap round however far you turn.
steps.title: Reach the end of the list

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays pattern 1 through a MIDI device: four trigs on steps 1 to 4 with the notes C, D, E and F (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97. Nothing else exists yet: no second pattern, no scale change, no second channel and one song slot. Trig merge modes decide what happens when two patterns on one channel both have a trig on a step: Skip (the default) drops those steps, Only keeps only those steps, and All keeps every step.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Do these in order. 1) Tap Pattern (5,8), choose pattern 2 at (2,1) and tap steps 1 and 3 on Pattern Trig. 2) Tap Pattern (5,8) again for Pattern Note and raise step 1 to (1,3) and step 3 to (3,1): degrees 4 and 6. 3) Tap Scale (4,8), tap slot 2 at (2,3), turn E2 to Root and E3 two detents up to D, then press K3: D major is applied. 4) Tap Channel (3,8) and tap pattern slot (2,2) to assign pattern 2 to channel 1 beside pattern 1. 5) Press Play, then Stop. Skip drops steps 1 and 3, where both patterns have a trig, so only steps 2 and 4 play: E and G of D major (MIDI 64 and 67) at velocities 117 and 97.
steps.title: Build pattern 2 and hear Skip

steps.caption: Tap the trig merge button (14,8) twice to move from Skip through Only to All. The button lights at medium brightness.
steps.title: Move the trig merge to All

steps.caption: Hold the velocity merge button (16,8) and tap pattern 1 at (1,2) to take velocities from pattern 1, then press Play and Stop. All four steps play.
